stem: A large company is migrating ils entire IT portfolio to AWS. Each business unit in the company has a standalone AWS account that supports both development and test environments. New accounts to support production workloads will be needed soon. The finance department requires a centralized method for payment but must maintain visibility into each group's spending to allocate costs. The security team requires a centralized mechanism to control 1AM usage in all the company's accounts. What combination of the following options meet the company's needs with the LEAST effort? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Use a collection of parameterized AWS CloudFormation templates defining common 1AM permissions that are launched into each account. Require all new and existing accounts to launch the appropriate stacks to enforce the least privilege model.

Use AWS Organizations to create a new organization from a chosen payer account and define an organizational unit hierarchy. Invite the existing accounts to join the organization and create new accounts using Organizations.
Require each business unit to use its own AWS accounts. Tag each AWS account appropriately and enable Cost Explorer to administer chargebacks.
Enable all features of AWS Organizations and establish appropriate service control policies that filter 1AM permissions for sub-accounts.
Consolidate all of the company's AWS accounts into a single AWS account. Use tags for billing purposes and the lAM's Access Advisor feature to enforce the least privilege model.

explanation:
Create an organization (consolidated billing, OUs, invite existing accounts, create new ones) and enable all features so you can use
service control policies to restrict IAM permissions across accounts. Finance still sees spend per account.
wrongOptionsExplanation:
A. Launching IAM CloudFormation templates into every account relies on teams to comply and does not centrally enforce anything. C.
Tags and Cost Explorer give visibility but no central payment or permission control. E. Merging into one account removes isolation
and makes cost allocation and security harder.
plainWords:
Many business units have separate accounts. Finance wants central payment with cost visibility, and security wants central IAM
control, using the least effort.
keyPoints:
• Central bill + central guardrails = Organizations (all features) + SCPs. • Existing accounts can be invited to join.
Reference: AWS documentation — https://docs.aws.amazon.com/

stem: A company is developing a new service that will be accessed using TCP on a static port A solutions architect must ensure that the service is highly available, has redundancy across Availability Zones, and is accessible using the DNS name myservice.com, which is publicly accessible The service must use fixed address assignments so other companies can add the addresses to their allow lists. Assuming that resources are deployed in multiple Availability Zones in a single Region, which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Create Amazon EC2 instances with an Elastic IP address for each instance Create a Network Load Balancer (NLB) and expose the static TCP port Register EC2instances with the NLB Create a new name server record set named my service com, and assign the Elastic IP addresses of the EC2 instances to the record set Provide the Elastic IP addresses of the EC2 instances to the other companies to add to their allow lists

Create an Amazon ECS cluster and a service definition for the application Create and assign public IP addresses for the ECS cluster Create a Network Load Balancer (NLB) and expose the TCP port Create a target group and assign the ECS cluster name to the NLB Create a new A record set named my service com and assign the public IP addresses of the ECS cluster to the record set Provide the public IP addresses of the ECS cluster to the other companies to add to their allow lists

Create Amazon EC2 instances for the service Create one Elastic IP address for each Availability Zone Create a Network Load Balancer (NLB) and expose the assigned TCP port Assign the Elastic IP addresses to the NLB for each Availability Zone Create a target group and register the EC2 instances with the NLB Create a new A (alias) record set named my service com, and assign the NLB DNS name to the record set.

Create an Amazon ECS cluster and a service definition for the application Create and assign public IP address for each host in the cluster Create an Application Load Balancer (ALB) and expose the static TCP port Create a target group and assign the ECS service definition name to the ALB Create a new CNAME record set and associate the public IP addresses to the record set Provide the Elastic IP addresses of the Amazon EC2 instances to the other companies to add to their allow lists

explanation:
A Network Load Balancer supports TCP on any port and can use one Elastic IP per AZ, giving fixed addresses. Register the EC2
targets, then create a Route 53 alias A record for myservice.com pointing to the NLB.
wrongOptionsExplanation:
A. Putting Elastic IPs directly on instances and listing them in DNS does not provide load balancing and breaks when instances are
replaced. B. ECS public IPs change, so they cannot be allow-listed. D. An ALB handles HTTP/HTTPS, not arbitrary TCP, and cannot use
static Elastic IPs.
plainWords: A TCP service must be highly available across AZs, reachable by a DNS name, and use fixed IPs that partners can allow-list.
keyPoints:
• Static IP + TCP/UDP + multi-AZ = NLB with Elastic IPs. • ALB has no static IP.
Reference: AWS documentation — https://docs.aws.amazon.com/

stem: A company’s web application uses an Amazon API Gateway API, AWS Lambda functions, and Amazon DynamoDB global tables to handle backend requests. The web application is deployed in two AWS Regions in an active-passive model. The company uses Amazon Route 53 for DNS. The web application requires a manual DNS update to fail over to the secondary Region. An analytics Lambda function runs in the same AWS account. The function has caused Lambda concurrency to reach 90% of the current quota on an average day. A recent surge in traffic for the analytics workload resulted in throttled Lambda requests and a poor user experience for the web application users. A solutions architect must increase the reliability of the web application. The solution must use an Amazon CloudWatch alarm to send an Amazon SNS notification when the Lambda concurrency reaches a specific utilization threshold. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Set reserved concurrency on the web application Lambda functions. Implement Route 53 health checks and failover records to route traffic to the secondary Region. Configure the CloudWatch alarm to use the AWS Trusted Advisor ServiceLimitUsage metric and to send the SNS notification.

Set reserved concurrency on the web application Lambda functions. Implement Route 53 health checks and latency records to route traffic to the secondary Region. Configure the CloudWatch alarm to use the AWS Trusted Advisor ServiceLimitUsage metric and to send an SNS notification.

Set provisioned concurrency on the web application Lambda functions. Implement Route 53 health checks and failover records to route traffic to the secondary Region. Configure the CloudWatch alarm to use the Lambda ConcurrentExecutions metric and to send an SNS notification.

Set provisioned concurrency on the web application Lambda functions. Implement Route 53 health checks and geolocation records to route traffic to the secondary Region. Configure the CloudWatch alarm to use the Lambda ProvisionedConcurrencyInvocations metric and to send an SNS notification.

explanation:
Give the web application functions provisioned concurrency so they have ready capacity, use Route 53 health checks with failover
records to automate Regional failover, and alarm on the Lambda ConcurrentExecutions metric to notify through SNS when utilization
approaches the limit.
wrongOptionsExplanation:
A. The Trusted Advisor metric is a more roundabout way to alarm on a limit than the Lambda metric itself. B. Latency records are for
performance routing, not active-passive failover. D. Geolocation routing is not failover, and ProvisionedConcurrencyInvocations does
not measure account concurrency usage.
plainWords:
An analytics Lambda uses about 90 percent of the account concurrency quota. A traffic surge throttles the web app functions.
Failover to the second Region is manual. You want an alarm and better reliability with little overhead.
keyPoints:
• Lambda account concurrency alarm = ConcurrentExecutions metric. • Active-passive DNS failover = Route 53 failover routing with
health checks.
HEADS-UP ON THIS QUESTION
• Reserved concurrency for the web functions would also protect them from the analytics function. The key chooses provisioned
concurrency; the main reasoning (failover record plus the ConcurrentExecutions alarm) is what separates C from the others.
Reference: AWS documentation — https://docs.aws.amazon.com/

stem: A company has multiple business units that each have separate accounts on AWS. Each business unit manages its own network with several VPCs that have CIDR ranges that overlap. The company’s marketing team has created a new internal application and wants to make the application accessible to all the other business units. The solution must use private IP addresses only. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Instruct each business unit to add a unique secondary CIDR range to the business unit's VPC. Peer the VPCs and use a private NAT gateway in the secondary range to route traffic to the marketing team.

Create an Amazon EC2 instance to serve as a virtual appliance in the marketing account's VPC. Create an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection between the marketing team and each business unit's VPC. Perform NAT where necessary.

Create an AWS PrivateLink endpoint service to share the marketing application. Grant permission to specific AWS accounts to connect to the service. Create interface VPC endpoints in other accounts to access the application by using private IP addresses.

Create a Network Load Balancer (NLB) in front of the marketing application in a private subnet. Create an API Gateway API. Use the Amazon API Gateway private integration to connect the API to the NLB. Activate IAM authorization for the API. Grant access to the accounts of the other business units.

explanation:
PrivateLink does not care about overlapping CIDRs. Publish the app as an endpoint service behind an NLB, grant specific accounts
permission, and each business unit creates an interface endpoint that gives a private IP in its own VPC. It is one-way and easy to
manage.
wrongOptionsExplanation:
A. Adding secondary CIDRs, peering and private NAT in every VPC is a lot of work to coordinate and maintain. B. EC2 appliances and
many VPNs with NAT create heavy operational burden. D. API Gateway with private integration can work, but it adds an API layer,
authorization design and extra cost without being simpler than PrivateLink.
plainWords: Business units have VPCs with overlapping IP ranges. An internal app must be reachable privately from all of them.
keyPoints:
• Overlapping CIDRs + private service sharing = PrivateLink. • Peering and Transit Gateway do not work with overlapping CIDRs.
Reference: AWS documentation — https://docs.aws.amazon.com/

stem: A solutions architect must provide a secure way for a team of cloud engineers to use the AWS CLI to upload objects into an Amazon S3 bucket Each cloud engineer has an IAM user. IAM access keys and a virtual multi-factor authentication (MFA) device The IAM users for the cloud engineers are in a group that is named S3-access The cloud engineers must use MFA to perform any actions in Amazon S3 Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Attach a policy to the S3 bucket to prompt the 1AM user for an MFA code when the 1AM user performs actions on the S3 bucket Use 1AM access keys with the AWS CLI tocall Amazon S3
Update the trust policy for the S3-access group to require principals to use MFA when principals assume the group Use 1AM access keys with the AWS CLI to call Amazon S3
Attach a policy to the S3-access group to deny all S3 actions unless MFA is present Use 1AM access keys with the AWS CLI to call Amazon S3

Attach a policy to the S3-access group to deny all S3 actions unless MFA is present Request temporary credentials from AWS Security Token Service (AWS STS) Attach the temporary credentials in a profile that Amazon S3 will reference when the user performs actions in Amazon S3

explanation:
A group policy denies S3 actions unless aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent is true. Long-term access keys never carry MFA context, so
engineers must call STS (get-session-token with their MFA code) and use the returned temporary credentials in a CLI profile. Those
credentials include the MFA flag, so the policy allows them.
wrongOptionsExplanation:
A. Bucket policies do not "prompt" for MFA, they only allow or deny based on request conditions. B. You cannot assume a group, and
a trust policy on a group is not a thing. C. With only long-term keys, the MFA condition is never true, so every request is denied.
plainWords: Engineers use IAM users with access keys and a virtual MFA device. They must use MFA for all S3 actions from the CLI.
keyPoints:
• MFA for CLI/API = deny unless aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent + get temporary credentials from STS using the MFA code. • Access keys
alone cannot prove MFA.
Reference: AWS documentation — https://docs.aws.amazon.com/

stem: An environmental company is deploying sensors in major cities throughout a country to measure air quality The sensors connect to AWS loT Core to ingest timesheets data readings. The company stores the data in Amazon DynamoDB For business continuity the company must have the ability to ingest and store data in two AWS Regions Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Create an Amazon Route 53 alias failover routing policy with values for AWS loT Core data endpoints in both Regions Migrate data to Amazon Aurora global tables

Create a domain configuration for AWS loT Core in each Region Create an Amazon Route 53 latency-based routing policy Use AWS loT Core data endpoints in both Regions as values Migrate the data to Amazon MemoryDB for Radis and configure Cross-Region replication

Create a domain configuration for AWS loT Core in each. Region Create an AmazonRoute 53 health check that evaluates domain configuration health Create a failover routing policy with values for the domain name from the AWS loT Core domain configurations Update the DynamoDB table to a global table
Create an Amazon Route 53 latency-based routing policy. Use AWS loT Core data endpoints in both Regions as values. Configure DynamoDB streams and Cross-Region data replication

explanation:
Create IoT Core custom domain configurations in each Region, use a Route 53 health check on the domain configuration health with
failover routing, and convert the DynamoDB table into a global table so data is stored in both Regions.
wrongOptionsExplanation:
A. Aurora global tables do not exist (Aurora has Global Database) and the app would need to be redesigned. B. MemoryDB is an
in-memory database, not the right store for sensor time series, and latency routing is not health-based failover. D. Latency routing is
not failover, and DynamoDB Streams with manual cross-Region replication is DIY compared with global tables.
plainWords:
Sensors send readings to AWS IoT Core and DynamoDB. The company needs the ability to ingest and store data in two Regions for
business continuity.
keyPoints:
• Multi-Region IoT ingestion = IoT domain configurations + Route 53 health check failover. • Multi-Region DynamoDB = global tables.
Reference: AWS documentation — https://docs.aws.amazon.com/

stem: A solutions architect must analyze a company's Amazon EC2 Instances and Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes to determine whether the company is using resources efficiently The company is running several large, high-memory EC2 instances lo host database dusters that are deployed in active/passive configurations The utilization of these EC2 instances varies by the applications that use the databases, and the company has not identified a pattern The solutions architect must analyze the environment and take action based on the findings. Which solution meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

options.text: Create a dashboard by using AWS Systems Manager OpsConter Configure visualizations tor Amazon CloudWatch metrics that are associated with the EC2 instances and their EBS volumes Review the dashboard periodically and identify usage patterns Right size the EC2 instances based on the peaks in the metrics

Turn on Amazon CloudWatch detailed monitoring for the EC2 instances and their EBS volumes Create and review a dashboard that is based on the metrics Identify usage patterns Right size the FC? instances based on the peaks In the metrics

Install the Amazon CloudWatch agent on each of the EC2 Instances Turn on AWS Compute Optimizer, and let it run for at least 12 hours Review the recommendations from Compute Optimizer, and right size the EC2 instances as directed
Sign up for the AWS Enterprise Support plan Turn on AWS Trusted Advisor Wait 12 hours Review the recommendations from Trusted Advisor, and rightsize the EC2 instances as directed

explanation:
AWS Compute Optimizer analyzes utilization history with machine learning and recommends better instance types and EBS volume
settings. Memory is not a default EC2 metric, so you install the CloudWatch agent to send memory data. Compute Optimizer is free
for its basic recommendations, so this is the cheapest and least manual approach.
wrongOptionsExplanation:
A. Building and reviewing a dashboard by hand and sizing "to the peaks" is manual, subjective and misses memory metrics. B.
Detailed monitoring costs money and still gives only raw metrics with no recommendations and no memory data. D. Enterprise
Support is very expensive just to get checks, and Trusted Advisor does not look at memory.
plainWords:
Large high-memory EC2 database hosts have unpredictable utilization. You must find out whether they are over-sized and act, in the
most cost-effective way.
keyPoints:
• Rightsizing recommendations = Compute Optimizer (+ CloudWatch agent for memory). • Default EC2 metrics exclude memory and
disk usage.
HEADS-UP ON THIS QUESTION
• The option says to wait 12 hours. In practice Compute Optimizer needs about 30 hours of metric history before it gives
recommendations. The reasoning and the answer are unaffected.
Reference: AWS documentation — https://docs.aws.amazon.com/

stem: A company has an application that stores user-uploaded videos in an Amazon S3 bucket that uses S3 Standard storage. Users access the videos frequently in the first 180 days after the videos are uploaded. Access after 180 days is rare. Named users and anonymous users access the videos. Most of the videos are more than 100 MB in size. Users often have poor internet connectivity when they upload videos, resulting in failed uploads. The company uses multipart uploads for the videos. A solutions architect needs to optimize the S3 costs of the application. Which combination of actions will meet these requirements? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Configure the S3 bucket to be a Requester Pays bucket.
Use S3 Transfer Acceleration to upload the videos to the S3 bucket.
Create an S3 Lifecycle configuration to expire incomplete multipart uploads 7 days after initiation.
Create an S3 Lifecycle configuration to transition objects to S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval after 1 day.
Create an S3 Lifecycle configuration to transition objects to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) after 180 days.

explanation:
Incomplete multipart uploads keep their uploaded parts in S3 and you pay for them, so a lifecycle rule that aborts incomplete
multipart uploads after 7 days removes that waste. After 180 days the videos are rarely accessed, so moving them to S3 Standard-IA
lowers storage cost and still gives instant access.
wrongOptionsExplanation:
A. Requester Pays only works for authenticated requesters. Anonymous users cannot use it. B. Transfer Acceleration improves upload
speed but adds charges, so it does not optimize cost. D. Moving to Glacier Instant Retrieval after 1 day is wrong. Videos are accessed
often in the first 180 days, so you would pay retrieval fees and a 90-day minimum.
plainWords:
Videos are hot for 180 days then rarely read. Users upload large files on poor connections, leaving failed multipart uploads behind.
Cut S3 cost.
keyPoints:
• Abort incomplete multipart uploads lifecycle rule = easy S3 savings. • Match the storage class to when access actually drops.
Reference: AWS documentation — https://docs.aws.amazon.com/

stem: A company is migrating its development and production workloads to a new organization in AWS Organizations. The company has created a separate member account for development and a separate member account for production. Consolidated billing is linked to the management account. In the management account, a solutions architect needs to create an 1AM user that can stop or terminate resources in both member accounts. Which solution will meet this requirement?

options.text: Create an IAM user and a cross-account role in the management account. Configure the cross-account role with least privilege access to the member accounts.

Create an IAM user in each member account. In the management account, create a cross-account role that has least privilege access. Grant the IAM users access to the cross-account role by using a trust policy.

Create an IAM user in the management account. In the member accounts, create an IAM group that has least privilege access. Add the IAM user from the management account to each IAM group in the member accounts.
Create an IAM user in the management account. In the member accounts, create cross- account roles that have least privilege access. Grant the IAM user access to the roles by using a trust policy.

explanation:
Create the IAM user in the management account. In each member account create an IAM role with least-privilege permissions (stop
and terminate only) whose trust policy trusts that user (or the management account). The user switches into the role in whichever
account it needs. This is the standard cross-account pattern with no duplicate users.
wrongOptionsExplanation:
A. The role must be in the account that owns the resources (the member accounts), not in the management account. B. Creating an
IAM user in every member account defeats the single-identity goal, and the role is placed in the wrong account. C. IAM groups cannot
contain users from another account.
plainWords:
You need one IAM user in the management account who can stop or terminate resources in the development and production member
accounts.
keyPoints:
• Access to another account = role in the target account that trusts the caller. • IAM groups never span accounts.
Reference: AWS documentation — https://docs.aws.amazon.com/

stem: A company has a website that runs on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The instances are in an Auto Scaling group. The ALB is associated with an AWS WAF web ACL. The website often encounters attacks in the application layer. The attacks produce sudden and significant increases in traffic on the application server. The access logs show that each attack originates from different IP addresses. A solutions architect needs to implement a solution to mitigate these attacks. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm that monitors server access. Set a threshold based on access by IP address. Configure an alarm action that adds the IP address to the web ACL’s deny list.
Deploy AWS Shield Advanced in addition to AWS WAF. Add the ALB as a protected resource.

Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm that monitors user IP addresses. Set a threshold based on access by IP address. Configure the alarm to invoke an AWS Lambda function to add a deny rule in the application server’s subnet route table for any IP addresses that activate the alarm.
Inspect access logs to find a pattern of IP addresses that launched the attacks. Use an Amazon Route 53 geolocation routing policy to deny traffic from the countries that host those IP addresses.

wrongOptionsExplanation:
A. A CloudWatch alarm cannot directly add an IP to a web ACL, and constantly changing IPs make manual lists useless. C. Route
tables do not support deny rules. Only network ACLs and security groups filter traffic, so this design is not possible as written. D.
Blocking whole countries by guessing is crude and Route 53 geolocation routing does not block traffic.
plainWords:
Application-layer attacks come from many different IP addresses and cause traffic spikes. A WAF web ACL already protects the ALB.
You want the least operational work. Why my answer (B) works AWS Shield Advanced adds automatic application-layer DDoS
detection and mitigation on top of AWS WAF. It can create and apply WAF rules automatically in response to an attack, so you do not
chase IP addresses by hand. You enable it and add the ALB as a protected resource.
keyPoints:
• Layer 7 DDoS with minimal effort = Shield Advanced + WAF (automatic mitigation). • A WAF rate-based rule is the other common
tool for request floods.
HEADS-UP ON THIS QUESTION
• The bank key says C, but a route table cannot hold a deny rule, so that option cannot work as written. B is the answer widely
accepted for this scenario. If you see this on the real exam, look for Shield Advanced or a WAF rate-based rule.
Reference: AWS documentation — https://docs.aws.amazon.com/
sourceWarning: Source key C invalid: VPC subnet route tables cannot deny traffic by source IP. B is feasible; WAF rate-based rules would be preferable but are not offered.

review.auditNote: C invalid: subnet route tables do not implement source-IP deny rules. B is the only feasible supplied managed mitigation, although WAF rate-based rules are a better low-overhead recommendation not offered.

stem: A company migrated its antivirus solution for 10,000 Amazon EC2 instances to a new software as a service SaaS solution. Fewer than 5% of instances reported in the new SaaS agent. The company suspects that either the new agent failed to load or the new agent’s configuration was altered. The company needs to implement a solution to ensure that all instances consistently run the most recent agent version with a predefined configuration. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST administrative overhead?

options.text: Create an AWS Lambda function that is invoked on a schedule. Store a machine list in Amazon S3. Configure the Lambda function to log in to every machine, download and install the most recent version of the agent, and configure the agent.

Implement an AWS Config rule with auto remediation that uses AWS Lambda for noncompliant events. Develop a Lambda function to access machines and download and install the most recent agent version. Schedule the Lambda function to invoke daily.

Create an AWS Systems Manager document that defines the agent installation and configuration process. Configure AWS Systems Manager State Manager to associate the document with EC2 instances. Apply the desired state on a daily schedule.

Log in to EC2 instances by using AWS Systems Manager Session Manager. Update the EC2 user data script to download and install the most recent agent and configure the agent. Reboot all EC2 instances to ensure that the script applies successfully.

explanation:
Write a Systems Manager Command document that installs and configures the agent, then create a State Manager association that
applies it to the instances on a schedule. State Manager enforces the desired state continuously and re-applies the configuration if it
drifts.
wrongOptionsExplanation:
A. A Lambda that logs in to thousands of machines needs credentials, networking and custom code. B. A Config rule with a custom
Lambda remediation still means writing and running your own installer code. D. Editing user data and rebooting 10,000 instances is
disruptive and does not keep the configuration enforced.
plainWords:
Only a small share of 10,000 EC2 instances report to a new antivirus SaaS. You must ensure every instance runs the latest agent with
the right configuration, with minimal admin work.
keyPoints:
• Keep software/config in a desired state on many instances = Systems Manager State Manager. • Run ad hoc commands = Run
Command. Patch = Patch Manager.
Reference: AWS documentation — https://docs.aws.amazon.com/

stem: A healthcare company is building a user support chat-based assistant on Amazon Bedrock. Users will ask health questions that might include personal details in the prompts. A solutions architect must configure a solution that can do the following: • Prevent the assistant from providing medical diagnosis advice. • Redact personally identifiable information (PII) from both user inputs and model responses. • Enforce the same controls even if the company changes foundation models (FMs) later. • Evaluate risky user prompts before sending the prompts to a model to avoid unnecessary inference costs. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Store approved health support guidelines in an Amazon Bedrock knowledge base. Configure system prompts that instruct the model not to provide diagnosis advice. Use an AWS Lambda function after inference to remove PII from the model response before the response is returned to users.

Fine-tune an FM on approved support conversations. Add prompt templates that prohibit diagnosis advice. Run a separate review process that scans transcripts for prohibited topics and sensitive information after the conversations end.

Build a custom moderation layer in the application to inspect prompts for prohibited topics and to redact sensitive information from user inputs. Invoke the model through the Converse API. Use separate post-processing logic to redact sensitive information from responses before displaying responses to users.

Create an Amazon Bedrock guardrail. Configure denied topics for medical diagnosis advice. Configure sensitive information filters to mask PII. Configure content filters. Call the ApplyGuardrail API on user prompts before inference. Include the same guardrail in the Converse API to evaluate model responses.

explanation:
Amazon Bedrock Guardrails are model-independent. You define denied topics (diagnosis advice), sensitive information filters that
mask PII, and content filters. The ApplyGuardrail API checks the user prompt before invoking the model (saving inference cost on bad
prompts), and the same guardrail attached to the Converse API checks the model response.
wrongOptionsExplanation:
A. System prompts are not a reliable control, and a Lambda that only cleans the response does not check inputs. B. Fine-tuning and
after-the-fact reviews do not enforce controls in real time. C. A custom moderation layer is heavy to build and maintain and is not
centrally managed.
plainWords:
A healthcare chat assistant on Amazon Bedrock must block medical diagnosis advice, redact PII in prompts and answers, keep
working if the model is swapped, and screen risky prompts before paying for inference.
keyPoints:
• Safety and privacy controls for generative AI = Bedrock Guardrails. • ApplyGuardrail checks text without calling a model, so it is
independent of model choice and cheap.
Reference: AWS documentation — https://docs.aws.amazon.com/

stem: A company is creating a REST API to share information with six of its partners based in the United States. The company has created an Amazon API Gateway Regional endpoint. Each of the six partners will access the API once per day to post daily sales figures. After initial deployment, the company observes 1.000 requests per second originating from 500 different IP addresses around the world. The company believes this traffic is originating from a botnet and wants to secure its API while minimizing cost. Which approach should the company take to secure its API?

options.text: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution with the API as the origin. Create an AWS WAF web ACL with a rule lo block clients thai submit more than fiverequests per day. Associate the web ACL with the CloudFront distnbution. Configure CloudFront with an origin access identity (OAI) and associate it with the distribution. Configure API Gateway to ensure only the OAI can run the POST method.

Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution with the API as the origin. Create an AWS WAF web ACL with a rule to block clients that submit more than five requests per day. Associate the web ACL with the CloudFront distnbution. Add a custom header to the CloudFront distribution populated with an API key. Configure the API to require an API key on the POST method.

Create an AWS WAF web ACL with a rule to allow access to the IP addresses used by the six partners. Associate the web ACL with the API. Create a resource policy with a request limit and associate it with the API. Configure the API to require an API key on the POST method.

Create an AWS WAF web ACL with a rule to allow access to the IP addresses used by the six partners. Associate the web ACL with the API. Create a usage plan with a request limit and associate it with the API. Create an API key and add it to the usage plan.

explanation:
A WAF allow rule for only the six partners' IP addresses blocks the botnet at the edge of API Gateway. A usage plan with an API key
adds a per-key request limit and quota (throttling), so even allowed callers cannot flood the API. All of it is attached directly to the API.
wrongOptionsExplanation:
A. Origin Access Identity is for S3, not for API Gateway, and a WAF rule cannot count "five requests per day" (rate-based rules use
short windows). B. Adds CloudFront cost and an unworkable per-day WAF rule. C. A resource policy controls who can call (IP, VPC,
account) but has no request limit. Usage plans provide limits.
plainWords:
Six US partners call an API once a day. A botnet from 500 global IPs sends 1,000 requests per second. Secure the API and keep cost
low.
keyPoints:
• Throttle callers = usage plan + API key. Block unknown IPs = WAF or resource policy. • Known, small set of partners = IP allow list.
Reference: AWS documentation — https://docs.aws.amazon.com/

stem: A company deploys its applications on Amazon EC2 instances in a VPC in the us-east-1 Region. The company recently acquired another company that has a data center in the ap- east-1 Region. A private application in us-east-1 needs to access the data that is stored in the data center in ap-east-1. The company needs a solution that supports IPv6. The solution also must encrypt the data in transit. The company has already created an AWS customer gateway that represents the customer gateway device in the data center in ap-east-1. The company will configure the route tables and modify the existing security groups to allow appropriate traffic after the network components are created. Which solution will meet the requirements for connectivity?

options.text: Create a transit gateway. Attach the transit gateway to the VPC in us-east-1. Create an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection. Specify the transit gateway as the target gateway. Download the configuration file and set up the customer gateway device.

Create a virtual private gateway. Attach the virtual private gateway to the VPC in us- east-1. Create an AWS Client VPN endpoint. Configure the customer gateway device to connect to the Client VPN endpoint.

Create a virtual private gateway. Attach the virtual private gateway to the VPC in us- east-1. Create an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection. Specify the virtual private gateway as the target gateway. Download the configuration file and set up the customer gateway device.
Create a transit gateway. Attach the transit gateway to the VPC in us-east-1. Create an AWS Client VPN endpoint. Configure the customer gateway device to connect to the Client VPN endpoint.

explanation:
Site-to-Site VPN uses IPsec, which gives encryption in transit. IPv6 traffic over a Site-to-Site VPN is supported only when the VPN
terminates on a Transit Gateway (or Cloud WAN), not on a virtual private gateway. So attach a transit gateway to the VPC and create
the VPN with the transit gateway as the target.
wrongOptionsExplanation:
B. Client VPN is for individual remote users and cannot terminate a customer gateway device. C. A virtual private gateway VPN does
not carry IPv6 traffic. D. Client VPN again is the wrong service for a data center connection.
plainWords:
A private app in us-east-1 must reach a data center in ap-east-1 with IPv6 support and encryption in transit. A customer gateway
already exists.
keyPoints:
• IPv6 over Site-to-Site VPN = Transit Gateway as the VPN target. • Client VPN = people. Site-to-Site VPN = networks.
Reference: AWS documentation — https://docs.aws.amazon.com/

stem: A company is developing a web application that runs on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind a public-facing Application Load Balancer (ALB). Only users from a specific country are allowed to access the application. The company needs the ability to log the access requests that have been blocked. The solution should require the least possible maintenance. Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create an IPSet containing a list of IP ranges that belong to the specified country. Create an AWS WAF web ACL. Configure a rule to block any requests that do not originate from an IP range in theIPSet. Associate the rule with the web ACL. Associate the web ACL with the ALB.
Create an AWS WAF web ACL. Configure a rule to block any requests that do not originate from the specified country. Associate the rule with the web ACL. Associate the web ACL with the ALB.
Configure AWS Shield to block any requests that do not originate from the specified country. Associate AWS Shield with the ALB.
Create a security group rule that allows ports 80 and 443 from IP ranges that belong to the specified country. Associate the security group with the ALB.

explanation:
AWS WAF has a geographic match rule. Create a web ACL that blocks requests not from the allowed country and associate it with the
ALB. AWS maintains the country mapping for you, and WAF logging records blocked requests.
wrongOptionsExplanation:
A. Maintaining IP ranges per country by hand is constant work and error prone. C. Shield protects against DDoS and does not filter by
country. D. A security group cannot filter by country, would need many rules, and cannot log blocked requests.
plainWords: Only users from one country may use the ALB-fronted app, you must log blocked requests, and maintenance must be minimal.
keyPoints:
• Country-based filtering on ALB/CloudFront/API Gateway = WAF geo match rule. • Need logs of blocked requests = enable WAF
logging.
Reference: AWS documentation — https://docs.aws.amazon.com/

stem: A company is running a compute workload by using Amazon EC2 Spot Instances that are in an Auto Scaling group. The launch template uses two placement groups and a single instance type. Recently, a monitoring system reported Auto Scaling instance launch failures that correlated with longer wait times for system users. The company needs to improve the overall reliability of the workload. Which solution will meet this requirement?

options.text: Replace the launch template with a launch configuration to use an Auto Scaling group thatuses attribute-based instance type selection.
Create a new launch template version that uses attribute-based instance type selection. Configure the Auto Scaling group to use the new launch template version.
Update the launch template Auto Scaling group to increase the number of placement groups.
Update the launch template to use a larger instance type.

explanation:
Spot capacity is limited per instance type. Attribute-based instance type selection lets you describe what you need (vCPU, memory)
and the Auto Scaling group can launch any matching type, which greatly improves the chance of finding capacity. You use it with a
launch template version, not a launch configuration.
wrongOptionsExplanation:
A. Launch configurations are legacy and do not support attribute-based selection. C. More placement groups do not add capacity
pools. They can even make launches harder. D. A larger single type is still one capacity pool, so the same shortage can occur.
plainWords: A Spot Auto Scaling group with one instance type and two placement groups has launch failures. Make it more reliable.
keyPoints:
• Spot reliability = diversify instance types (attribute-based selection or mixed instances). • Use launch templates, not launch
configurations.
Reference: AWS documentation — https://docs.aws.amazon.com/

stem: A company runs a serverless ecommerce application on AWS. The application uses API Gateway to invoke Java Lambda functions that connect to an Amazon RDS for MySQL database. During a sale event, traffic spikes caused slow performance and DB connection failures. Which solution will improve performance with the LEAST application change?

options.text: Move DB connection outside Lambda handler and increase provisioned concurrency.
Use RDS Proxy. Store DB credentials in Secrets Manager. Update Lambda to use RDS Proxy. Increase provisioned concurrency.
Increase max_connections parameter in a custom DB parameter group and reboot. Increase reserved concurrency.
Use RDS Proxy and Secrets Manager. Increase reserved concurrency.

explanation:
RDS Proxy pools database connections so Lambda scale-out does not overwhelm MySQL, and Secrets Manager holds the credentials
the proxy uses. Java Lambda functions also have slow cold starts, so provisioned concurrency keeps warm execution environments
ready. Together they address both symptoms.
wrongOptionsExplanation:
A. Opening the connection outside the handler helps per environment but cannot control total connections, and it skips RDS Proxy. C.
Raising max_connections needs a reboot and just lets the database fall over later. Reserved concurrency does not reduce cold starts.
D. RDS Proxy is right, but reserved concurrency only caps or guarantees concurrency, it does not pre-warm Java environments.
plainWords:
During a sale, a Java Lambda function behind API Gateway is slow and the MySQL database refuses connections. Fix it with the least
application change.
keyPoints:
• Connection failures from Lambda = RDS Proxy. Slow Java cold starts = provisioned concurrency (or SnapStart). • Reserved
concurrency limits and guarantees; provisioned concurrency pre-warms.
Reference: AWS documentation — https://docs.aws.amazon.com/

stem: A company is developing a gene reporting device that will collect genomic information to assist researchers with collecting large samples of data from a diverse population. The device will push 8 KB of genomic data every second to a data platform that will need to process and analyze the data and provide information back to researchers. The data platform must meet the following requirements: •Provide near-real-time analytics of the inbound genomic data •Ensure the data is flexible, parallel, and durable •Deliver results of processing to a data warehouse Which strategy should a solutions architect use to meet these requirements?

options.text: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to collect the inbound sensor data, analyze the data with Kinesis clients, and save the results to an Amazon RDS instance.
Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to collect the inbound sensor data, analyze the data with Kinesis clients, and save the results to an Amazon Redshift cluster using Amazon EMR.
Use Amazon S3 to collect the inbound device data, analyze the data from Amazon SOS with Kinesis, and save the results to an Amazon Redshift cluster.
Use an Amazon API Gateway to put requests into an Amazon SQS queue, analyze the data with an AWS Lambda function, and save the results to an Amazon Redshift cluster using Amazon EMR.

explanation:
Kinesis Data Streams ingests the data durably, splits it across shards for parallel processing, and keeps records for replay. Kinesis
consumers (KCL applications) analyze the stream in near real time and the results are loaded into Amazon Redshift, the data
warehouse, using EMR.
wrongOptionsExplanation:
A. Firehose is a delivery service with limited custom consumers, and RDS is not a data warehouse. C. S3 is storage, not a real-time
stream, and the described SQS-to-Kinesis flow makes little sense. D. API Gateway to SQS adds cost and SQS is not designed for
parallel stream analytics or replay.
plainWords:
A device sends 8 KB every second. You need near-real-time analytics that are parallel and durable, with results going to a data
warehouse.
keyPoints:
• Real-time, ordered, replayable, parallel = Kinesis Data Streams. • Data warehouse = Redshift.
HEADS-UP ON THIS QUESTION
• Today the same idea is often built with Kinesis Data Streams, Managed Service for Apache Flink and Firehose to Redshift, with less
to manage than EMR. The core answer stays Kinesis Data Streams.
Reference: AWS documentation — https://docs.aws.amazon.com/

stem: A company recently wanted a web application from an on-premises data center to the AWS Cloud. The web application infrastructure consists of an Amazon CloudFront distribution that routes to an Application Load Balancer (ALB), with Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) to process requests. A recent security audit revealed that the web application is accessible by using both CloudFront and ALB endpoints. However. the company requires that the web application must be accessible only by using the CloudFront endpoint. Which solution will meet this requirement with the LEAST amount of effort?

options.text: Create a new security group and attach it to the CloudFront distribution. Update the ALB security group ingress to allow access only from the CloudFront security group.
Update ALB security group ingress to allow access only from the CloudFront managed prefix list.
Create a VPC interface endpoint for Elastic Load Balancing. Update the ALB scheme from internet-facing to internal_
Extract CloudFront IPS from the AWS provided ip-ranges.json document. Update ALB security group ingress to allow access only from CloudFront IPs.

explanation:
AWS publishes a managed prefix list of CloudFront origin-facing IP ranges. Reference it in the ALB security group inbound rule and
AWS keeps the list up to date automatically, so you do no manual IP maintenance.
wrongOptionsExplanation:
A. CloudFront is not attached to security groups, so there is no CloudFront security group. C. Making the ALB internal would cut off
CloudFront, which needs a reachable origin (unless you use CloudFront VPC origins). D. Parsing ip-ranges.json by hand means
constant updates.
plainWords: Users can reach the app through both CloudFront and the ALB endpoint. Only CloudFront must be allowed, with the least effort.
keyPoints:
• Lock an ALB to CloudFront = CloudFront managed prefix list in the ALB security group. • For stronger protection add a secret
custom header check, because the prefix list admits any CloudFront distribution.
Reference: AWS documentation — https://docs.aws.amazon.com/

stem: A company wants to migrate an application to Amazon EC2 from VMware Infrastructure that runs in an on-premises data center. A solutions architect must preserve the software and configuration settings during the migration. What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

options.text: Configure the AWS DataSync agent to start replicating the data store to Amazon FSx for Windows File Server Use the SMB share to host the VMware data store. Use VM Import/Export to move the VMs to Amazon EC2.

Use the VMware vSphere client to export the application as an image in Open Virealization Format (OVF) format Create an Amazon S3 bucket to store the image in the destination AWS Region. Create and apply an IAM role for VM Import Use the AWS CLI to run the EC2 import command.

. Configure AWS Storage Gateway for files service to export a Common Internet File System(CIFSJ share. Create a backup copy to the shared folder. Sign in to the AWS Management Console and create an AMI from the backup copy Launch an EC2 instance that is based on the AMI.

Create a managed-instance activation for a hybrid environment in AWS Systems Manager. Download and install Systems Manager Agent on the on-premises VM Register the VM with Systems Manager to be a managed instance Use AWS Backup to create a snapshot of the VM and create an AMI. Launch an EC2 instance that is based on the AMI

explanation: SOURCE KEY D IS TECHNICALLY INVALID AS WRITTEN. Registering an on-premises VM as a Systems Manager managed instance does not make AWS Backup create a VMware VM snapshot or AMI from that managed-instance registration. AWS Backup's VMware integration requires AWS Backup gateway and a registered VMware hypervisor; AWS Backup can then restore supported VM recovery points to EC2. B is the closest feasible listed option: export a VMware VM to a supported import image, upload it to S3, configure the VM Import service role, and use VM Import/Export to import it to EC2, subject to supported formats and OS restrictions. B's wording should specify supported export format and import-image steps. A/C do not describe a workable VM migration workflow. Keep original D in snapshot; the key is corrected to B as the best offered option, but exact source-site verification is pending.
wrongOptionsExplanation:
A. DataSync and FSx for Windows are for file data, not a method to move whole VMs, so this combination does not make sense. C.
Storage Gateway file shares do not capture a bootable VM image. D. Systems Manager hybrid activation manages servers but does
not snapshot an on-prem VM into an AMI, and AWS Backup does not back up arbitrary on-prem VMs this way.
plainWords:
Migrate an application from on-prem VMware to EC2 while preserving the software and configuration settings. Why my answer (B)
works Export the VM from vSphere as an OVF/OVA image, upload it to S3, create the IAM role VM Import requires, and run the EC2
import command (VM Import/Export). The result is an AMI that contains the same operating system, software and settings as the
original VM.
keyPoints:
• Whole VM to an AMI = VM Import/Export (OVA/OVF to S3, then import). • For continuous replication and cutover, the managed
service is Application Migration Service (MGN).
HEADS-UP ON THIS QUESTION
• The bank key says D, but Systems Manager plus AWS Backup cannot turn an on-prem VM into an AMI. B is the answer commonly
accepted for this question. In a new design you would usually pick AWS Application Migration Service.
Reference: AWS documentation — https://docs.aws.amazon.com/

review.auditNote: Source D does not describe AWS Backup VMware gateway mechanism. B is feasible using VM Import/Export; AWS MGN or AWS Backup gateway restore are modern alternatives not listed.

stem: A company runs a Linux app on Amazon EKS usingM6iEC2 instances under a Savings Plan that is about to expire. They want toreduce costsafter expiration.

options.text: Rebuild containers forARM64architecture.
Rebuild containers for container compatibility (invalid/unclear).
Migrate EKS nodes toGraviton(e.g., C7g, M7g).
Replace nodes with latestx86_64instances.
Purchase new Savings Plan for Graviton instance family.
Purchase new Savings Plan for x86_64 instances.

explanation:
Graviton (ARM64) instances give better price performance. You need to rebuild the container images for ARM64 (A), move the EKS
node group to Graviton instance types such as M7g or C7g (C), and then buy a new Savings Plan that covers the Graviton usage (E).
wrongOptionsExplanation:
B. This option is unclear in the source and describes nothing useful. D. Newer x86 instances help a little but do not deliver the
Graviton savings. F. Buying a plan for x86 would lock you into the more expensive family.
plainWords: A Linux app on EKS runs on M6i (x86) nodes under a Savings Plan that is about to expire. Reduce cost afterward.
keyPoints:
• Linux + containers + cost = consider Graviton: rebuild for arm64, move nodes, buy a matching plan. • A Compute Savings Plan
follows you across instance families, including Graviton.
HEADS-UP ON THIS QUESTION
• The wording of the options in your PDF is garbled in places. The key A, C, E follows the standard Graviton migration steps.
Reference: AWS documentation — https://docs.aws.amazon.com/

stem: A data analytics company has an Amazon Redshift cluster that consists of several reserved nodes. The cluster is experiencing unexpected bursts of usage because a team of employees is compiling a deep audit analysis report. The queries to generate the report are complex read queries and are CPU intensive. Business requirements dictate that the cluster must be able to service read and write queries at all times. A solutions architect must devise a solution that accommodates the bursts of usage. Which solution meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

options.text: Provision an Amazon EMR cluster. Offload the complex data processing tasks.
Deploy an AWS Lambda function to add capacity to the Amazon Redshift cluster by using a classic resize operation when the cluster's CPU metrics in Amazon CloudWatch reach 80%.
Deploy an AWS Lambda function to add capacity to the Amazon Redshift cluster by using an elastic resize operation when the cluster's CPU metrics in Amazon CloudWatch reach 80%.
Turn on the Concurrency Scaling feature for the Amazon Redshift cluster.

wrongOptionsExplanation:
A. Standing up an EMR cluster and moving the processing there is a redesign, not a fix for bursts. B. A classic resize is slow and puts
the cluster in read-only mode, breaking the write requirement. C. An elastic resize still briefly interrupts the cluster and needs custom
Lambda code. It also does not scale back down by itself.
plainWords:
A Redshift cluster has short bursts of heavy read queries from an audit report. The cluster must stay available for reads and writes at
all times, at the lowest cost. Why my answer (D) works Concurrency Scaling automatically adds extra transient cluster capacity when
many queries queue, then removes it. The main cluster stays online for reads and writes, there is no custom code to run, and AWS
gives free usage credits that often cover the burst.
keyPoints:
• Bursty concurrent queries on Redshift = Concurrency Scaling. • Resizing means downtime or complexity. Concurrency Scaling does
not.
HEADS-UP ON THIS QUESTION
• The bank key says C (elastic resize). That conflicts with "must serve reads and writes at all times". Concurrency Scaling (D) is the
textbook answer for bursty read demand.
Reference: AWS documentation — https://docs.aws.amazon.com/

stem: A company needs to improve the security of its web application on AWS. The application runs on a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances behind a public Application Load Balancer (ALB). The instances are in an Auto Scaling group. The ALB is registered as a custom origin in an Amazon CloudFront distribution. The company wants customers to access the website by using a fully qualified domain name (FQDN) that is associated with the CloudFront distribution. A security audit shows that the ALB can be accessed directly and that some requests bypass the CloudFront distribution. The company needs a solution that will prevent direct access to the ALB. The solution also must ensure that all requests pass through the CloudFront distribution. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Modify the security group that is attached to the ALB to allow incoming traffic from only the CloudFront distribution’s origin.
Configure the CloudFront distribution to use an AWS WAF web ACL to block requests that bypass the CloudFront distribution.
Add a security header to the CloudFront distribution. Implement header validation and enforcement at the ALB.
Configure an origin access control (OAC) for the CloudFront distribution. Update the ALB to allow only requests that come from the OAC.

explanation:
Have CloudFront add a secret custom header (a random value) on every origin request, and configure the ALB listener rule (or WAF)
to forward only requests that carry that header. Direct requests do not have the secret, so they are rejected.
wrongOptionsExplanation:
A. There is no single "CloudFront distribution origin" you can name in a security group, only shared CloudFront address ranges. B. A
WAF on CloudFront only sees requests that already came through CloudFront, so it cannot stop requests that bypass it. D. Origin
Access Control works for S3 and similar origins, not for an ALB.
plainWords: The ALB is a public custom origin for CloudFront, but people can hit the ALB directly. All traffic must come through CloudFront.
keyPoints:
• Make CloudFront the only way in to an ALB = secret custom header validated at the ALB (plus the prefix list). • OAC/OAI are for S3
origins.
Reference: AWS documentation — https://docs.aws.amazon.com/

stem: A company hosts a payment processing platform across multiple AWS Regions. The processing platform exposes payment processing API endpoints. The company uses Amazon Route 53 to route traffic to an Application Load Balancer (ALB) in each Region to distribute requests to backend payment gateways. The company has implemented Auto Scaling for the payment gateways. The company needs to improve reliability and availability by handling application failures quickly. Which solution will meet this requirement with the LEAST response time for global users?

options.text: Configure Route 53 to use a geolocation routing policy to resolve DNS to an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Configure the distribution with an origin group that includes the ALBs from each Region as origins.
Create an accelerator in AWS Global Accelerator. Create an endpoint group and add each ALB as an endpoint in the group. Update the Route 53 alias records to point to the accelerator.
Configure Route 53 to use a latency-based routing policy and health checks for each Regional endpoint.
Set up cross-Region connectivity by using AWS Cloud WAN to connect VPCs across Regions. Use network policies to route traffic from each Region to the Region that is closest to the origin Region.

explanation:
AWS Global Accelerator gives two static anycast IPs, brings users onto the AWS network at the nearest edge, and continually
health-checks the ALB endpoints. When an endpoint fails it shifts traffic within seconds, without waiting for DNS caches to expire.
wrongOptionsExplanation:
A. CloudFront origin groups with geolocation routing fit web content caching, not a dynamic payment API, and geolocation is not a
health-based failover method. C. DNS-based failover depends on TTLs and resolver caches, so it is slower. D. Cloud WAN builds
private networks between your own VPCs. It does not route global internet users to the closest healthy Region.
plainWords: A multi-Region payment API behind Regional ALBs needs the quickest response to application failures for users worldwide.
keyPoints:
• Fastest regional failover for TCP/HTTP apps = Global Accelerator (no DNS caching). • Route 53 failover is good but bounded by DNS
TTL.
Reference: AWS documentation — https://docs.aws.amazon.com/

stem: How can applications in multiple AWS accounts privately access aPostgreSQL RDS instancein a separate AWS account, while managing the number of connections?

options.text: Transit Gateway + NAT Gateway
RDS Proxy + PrivateLink via NLB
VPC Peering + Application Load Balancer
VPC Peering + NAT Gateway

explanation:
RDS Proxy pools and limits connections. Put a Network Load Balancer in front of the proxy endpoint and publish it as a PrivateLink
endpoint service. Each consumer account creates an interface endpoint to it, so access is private, one-way and works even with
overlapping CIDRs.
wrongOptionsExplanation:
A. Transit Gateway with NAT does not limit connections and NAT is for outbound internet access. C. Peering plus an ALB does not
make sense here since the ALB speaks HTTP and not PostgreSQL, and peering does not control connections. D. Peering plus NAT
gateway does not provide private service exposure or connection pooling.
plainWords:
Applications in several AWS accounts must reach a PostgreSQL RDS instance in another account privately, and the number of
database connections must be controlled.
keyPoints:
• Private, one-way, multi-account service access = PrivateLink. • Too many DB connections = RDS Proxy.
Reference: AWS documentation — https://docs.aws.amazon.com/

stem: A company is subject to regulatory audits of its financial information. External auditors who use a single AWS account need access to the company's AWS account. A solutions architect must provide the auditors with secure, read-only access to the company's AWS account. The solution must comply with AWS security best practices. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: In the company's AWS account, create resource policies for all resources in the account to grant access to the auditors' AWS account. Assign a unique external ID to the resource policy.

In the company's AWS account create an IAM role that trusts the auditors' AWS account Create an IAM policy that has the required permissions. Attach the policy to the role. Assign a unique external ID to the role's trust policy.
In the company's AWS account, create an IAM user. Attach the required IAM policies to the IAM user. Create API access keys for the IAM user. Share the access keys with the auditors.
In the company's AWS account, create an IAM group that has the required permissions Create an IAM user in the company s account for each auditor. Add the IAM users to the IAM group.

explanation:
Create an IAM role in your account that trusts the auditors' AWS account, attach a read-only (for example SecurityAudit or
ViewOnlyAccess) policy, and add an external ID to the trust policy. The auditors assume the role and get temporary credentials, with
no long-lived secrets to share.
wrongOptionsExplanation:
A. Resource policies for every resource would be endless to build and not all resources support them. C. Sharing IAM user access keys
breaks best practices (long-lived, shareable credentials). D. Creating individual IAM users in your account adds user lifecycle work and
long-term credentials.
plainWords: External auditors, who have their own AWS account, need secure read-only access to your account following best practices.
keyPoints:
• Third-party or external access = cross-account role + external ID. • Never share access keys.
Reference: AWS documentation — https://docs.aws.amazon.com/

stem: A company's factory and automaton applications are running in a single VPC More than 23 applications run on a combination of Amazon EC2, Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS), are Amazon RDS. The company has software engineers spread across three teams. One of the three teams owns each application, and each team is responsible for the cost and performance of all of its applications.Team resources have tags that represent their application and team. The learns use IAH access for daily activities. The company needs to determine which costs on the monthly AWS bill are attributable to each application or team. The company also must be able to create reports to compare costs item the last 12 months and to help forecast costs tor the next 12 months. A solution architect must recommend an AWS Billing and Cost Management solution that provides these cost reports. Which combination of actions will meet these requirement? Select THREE.)

options.text: Activate the user-defined cost allocation tags that represent the application and the team.
Activate the AWS generated cost allocation tags that represent the application and the team.
Create a cost category for each application in Billing and Cost Management
Activate IAM access to Billing and Cost Management.
Create a cost budget
Enable Cost Explorer.

explanation:
Tags only appear in billing after you activate them as user-defined cost allocation tags (A). Cost Explorer provides cost history,
comparisons and forecasting (F). Cost categories (C) let you group costs by application or team using rules and tags so the reports
map cleanly to business groups.
wrongOptionsExplanation:
B. AWS-generated tags are things like createdBy. They do not represent your own application and team tags. D. IAM access to Billing
is useful if non-root IAM users must see the data (the teams do use IAM), so this is a close call. E. A budget alerts on spend but is not
the reporting and forecasting tool the question asks for.
plainWords:
Teams tag resources by application and team. Finance wants cost per team or application, 12-month comparisons and a 12-month
forecast.
keyPoints:
• Tags are invisible in billing until activated as cost allocation tags. • Cost Explorer = history and forecast. Cost categories = business
groupings.
HEADS-UP ON THIS QUESTION
• This is a close call. A and F are clearly needed. For the third, the key picks cost categories (C), but because the teams work as IAM
users, enabling IAM access to Billing (D) is also needed in real life. Follow the key (A, C, F) unless the exam wording emphasizes IAM
users seeing billing.
Reference: AWS documentation — https://docs.aws.amazon.com/

stem: A company is running a large containerized workload in the AWS Cloud using Amazon ECS. The development team recently started usingAWS Fargateinstead of EC2 in the ECS cluster. The company is worried about reaching themaximum number of ECS tasksallowed in the account. A solutions architect must implement a solution that notifies the development team when Fargate usage reaches80% of the quota. What should the architect do?

options.text: Use CloudWatch to monitor the Sample Count for each service. Alert when usage exceeds 80%.
Use CloudWatch to monitor ECS service quotas under the AWS/Usage namespace. Create an alarm when utilization exceeds 80%. Notify via SNS.
Use a Lambda function to poll Fargate metrics. Notify via SES when usage exceeds 80%.
Use AWS Config to monitor Fargate quotas. Notify via SES if non-compliant.

explanation:
Service Quotas publishes usage metrics to the CloudWatch AWS/Usage namespace for many services. Create a CloudWatch alarm
that triggers at 80 percent of the quota and send it to an SNS topic. It is native, serverless and needs no custom code.
wrongOptionsExplanation:
A. Sample Count is a statistic of a metric, not a quota usage measure. C. A Lambda that polls and sends email through SES is custom
code to build and maintain. D. AWS Config tracks resource configuration compliance, not service quota utilization.
plainWords: Notify the team when ECS Fargate usage reaches 80 percent of the account quota.
keyPoints:
• Quota usage alarm = Service Quotas + CloudWatch AWS/Usage metric + SNS.
Reference: AWS documentation — https://docs.aws.amazon.com/

stem: A solutions architect has created a single VPC on AWS. The VPC has one internet gateway and one NAT gateway. The VPC extends across three Availability Zones. Each Availability Zone includes one public subnet and one private subnet. The three private subnets contain Amazon EC2 instances that must be able to connect to the internet. Which solution will increase the network resiliency of this architecture?

options.text: Add two NAT gateways so that each Availability Zone has a NAT gateway. Configure a route table for each private subnet to send traffic to the NAT gateway in the subnet's Availability Zone.
Add two NAT gateways so that each Availability Zone has a NAT gateway. Configure a route table for each public subnet to send traffic to the NAT gateway in the subnet's Availability Zone.

Add two internet gateways so that each Availability Zone has an internet gateway. Configure a route table for each private subnet to send traffic to the internet gateway in the subnet's Availability Zone.

Add two internet gateways so that each Availability Zone has an internet gateway. Configure a route table for each public subnet to send traffic to the internet gateway in the subnet's Availability Zone.

explanation:
NAT gateways are tied to one AZ. Create one in each AZ and route each private subnet to the NAT gateway in its own AZ. An AZ
outage then only affects that AZ.
wrongOptionsExplanation:
B. Public subnets route to the internet gateway, not through NAT, so changing their routes does not help. C. A VPC has just one
internet gateway and private subnets cannot use it directly. D. Same problem: you cannot add multiple internet gateways.
plainWords: Same scenario as Question 5: one NAT gateway serves private subnets in three AZs.
keyPoints:
• One NAT gateway per AZ and route each private subnet to its local one.
Reference: AWS documentation — https://docs.aws.amazon.com/

stem: A company has deployed its database on an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance in the us-east-1 Region. The company needs to make its data available to customers in Europe. The customers in Europe must have access to the same data as customers in the United States (US) and will not tolerate high application latency or stale data. The customers in Europe and the customers in the USneed to write to the database. Both groups of customers need to see updates from the other group in real time. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Create an Amazon Aurora MySQL replica of the RDS for MySQL DB instance. Pause application writes to the RDS DB instance. Promote the Aurora Replica to a standalone DB cluster. Reconfigure the application to use the Aurora database and resume writes. Add eu-west-1 as a secondary Region to the 06 cluster. Enable write forwarding on the DB cluster. Deploy the application in eu-west-1. Configure the application to use the Aurora MySQL endpoint in eu- west-1.

Add a cross-Region replica in eu-west-1 for the RDS for MySQL DB instance. Configure the replica to replicate write queries back to the primary DB instance. Deploy the application in eu-west-1. Configure the application to use the RDS for MySQL endpoint in eu-west-1.

Copy the most recent snapshot from the RDS for MySQL DB instance to eu-west-1. Create a new RDS for MySQL DB instance in eu-west-1 from the snapshot. Configure MySQL logical replication from us-east-1 to eu-west-1. Enable write forwarding on the DB cluster. Deploy the application in eu-west-1. Configure the application to use the RDS for MySQL endpoint in eu-west-1.

Convert the RDS for MySQL DB instance to an Amazon Aurora MySQL DB cluster. Add eu-west-1 as a secondary Region to the DB cluster. Enable write forwarding on the DB cluster. Deploy the application in eu-west-1. Configure the application to use the Aurora MySQL endpoint in eu-west-1.

explanation:
Move to Aurora MySQL by creating an Aurora read replica of the RDS MySQL instance and promoting it. Then add eu-west-1 as a
secondary Region of an Aurora Global Database and enable write forwarding. EU applications read locally with sub-second replication
lag, and their writes are forwarded to the primary Region.
wrongOptionsExplanation:
B. RDS cross-Region read replicas are read-only and have no feature to replicate writes back. C. Logical replication is one-way, and
write forwarding is an Aurora Global Database feature, not an RDS MySQL one. D. You cannot simply convert an RDS MySQL instance
to an Aurora cluster in place. The supported path is an Aurora read replica (or snapshot restore).
plainWords:
US and EU customers both write to a MySQL database, need the same data in near real time, and cannot tolerate high latency or stale
data.
keyPoints:
• Global reads with write forwarding = Aurora Global Database. • Path from RDS MySQL to Aurora = Aurora read replica, then
promote.
Reference: AWS documentation — https://docs.aws.amazon.com/

stem: A company developed a pilot application by using AWS Elastic Beanstalk and Java. To save costs during development, the company's development team deployed the application into a single-instance environment. Recent tests indicate that the application consumes more CPU than expected. CPU utilization is regularly greater than 85%, which causes some performance bottlenecks. A solutions architect must mitigate the performance issues before the company launches the application to production. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Create a new Elastic Beanstalk application. Select a load-balanced environment type. Select all Availability Zones. Add a scale-out rule that will run if the maximum CPU utilization is over 85% for 5 minutes.

Create a second Elastic Beanstalk environment. Apply the traffic-splitting deployment policy. Specify a percentage of incoming traffic to direct to the new environment in the average CPU utilization is over 85% for 5 minutes.

Modify the existing environment's capacity configuration to use a load-balanced environment type. Select all Availability Zones. Add a scale-out rule that will run if the average CPU utilization is over 85% for 5 minutes.
Select the Rebuild environment action with the load balancing option Select an Availability Zones Add a scale-out rule that will run if the sum CPU utilization is over 85% for 5 minutes.

explanation:
Change the existing environment's capacity settings to a load-balanced, auto scaling environment across multiple AZs and add a
scale-out trigger on average CPU utilization. Beanstalk handles the load balancer and scaling for you, and you keep the same
application.
wrongOptionsExplanation:
A. Creating a brand-new application is unnecessary extra work. B. Traffic splitting is a deployment policy for releases, not a way to
scale for CPU. D. Rebuilding the environment is more disruptive, and "sum" CPU is the wrong statistic. Average is correct for scaling.
plainWords:
A Java app in a single-instance Elastic Beanstalk environment runs at over 85 percent CPU. Fix it before production with the least
work.
keyPoints:
• Single-instance Beanstalk to scalable = change environment type to load-balanced and set Auto Scaling triggers.
Reference: AWS documentation — https://docs.aws.amazon.com/

stem: A company is planning to migrate to the AWS Cloud. The company hosts many applications on Windows servers and Linux servers. Some of the servers are physical, and some of the servers are virtual. The company uses several types of databases in its on- premises environment. The company does not have an accurate inventory of its on- premises servers and applications. The company wants to rightsize its resources during migration. A solutions architect needs to obtain information about the network connections and the application relationships. The solutions architect must assess the company's current environment and develop a migration plan. Which solution will provide the solutions architect with the required information to develop the migration plan?

options.text: Use Migration Evaluator to request an evaluation of the environment from AWS. Use the AWS Application Discovery Service Agentless Collector to import the details into a Migration Evaluator Quick Insights report.

Use AWS Migration Hub and install the AWS Application Discovery Agent on the servers. Deploy the Migration Hub Strategy Recommendations application data collector. Generate a report by using Migration Hub Strategy Recommendations.

Use AWS Migration Hub and run the AWS Application Discovery Service Agentless Collector on the servers. Group the servers and databases by using AWS Application Migration Service. Generate a report by using Migration Hub Strategy Recommendations.
Use the AWS Migration Hub import tool to load the details of the company's on- premises environment. Generate a report by using Migration Hub Strategy Recommendations.

explanation: B is the intended answer. The Application Discovery Agent gathers server configuration, performance, running processes, and network connections from supported physical and virtual servers; Strategy Recommendations adds application analysis for migration planning. A focuses on cost assessment and does not fully capture the application relationship workflow. C incorrectly says to run the agentless collector 'on the servers' and to group servers using Application Migration Service. D assumes an existing inventory despite the stem stating it is incomplete. Verify current availability of legacy Migration Hub Strategy Recommendations before implementing this as a new architecture.
wrongOptionsExplanation:
A. Migration Evaluator is a business case and TCO tool and the agentless collector does not collect network dependencies. C. The
agentless collector supports VMware VMs only and does not capture network connections. It does not work for physical servers. D.
Importing details requires you to already have the data.
plainWords:
The company has physical and virtual Windows and Linux servers, no reliable inventory, and needs network connections and
application relationships to rightsize and plan.
keyPoints:
• Dependency mapping for physical and virtual servers = Application Discovery Agent. • Agentless collector = VMware only, no
network connections.
Reference: AWS documentation — https://docs.aws.amazon.com/
