stem: A global ecommerce company has many data centers worldwide. The company needs scalable cloud storage for legacy file applications. Requirements: Must support iSCSI access from on-premises servers. Must support point-in-time snapshots via AWS Backup. Must retain low-latency access to frequently accessed data.Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Provision an AWS Storage Gateway tape gateway with S3 and AWS Backup.
Use Amazon FSx File Gateway and S3 File Gateway. Use AWS Backup.
Provision an AWS Storage Gateway volume gateway in cache mode. Back up the volumes using AWS Backup.
Provision an AWS Storage Gateway file gateway in cache mode. Use AWS Backup.

explanation: Verified answer C using AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway and AWS Backup documentation plus exact-question SAP-C02 external copies (ExamTopics Q494, ExamCollection, Pass4Future). Cached Volume Gateway exposes iSCSI block volumes to on-premises servers, stores primary data in Amazon S3 and caches frequently accessed blocks locally for low-latency access. AWS Backup supports point-in-time backups of cached and stored gateway volumes, represented as EBS snapshots, and restore to Storage Gateway volumes or EBS. The local cache is not a complete offline copy; uncached reads require cloud connectivity. The application accesses a filesystem placed on the iSCSI volume; it does not use File Gateway SMB/NFS access.
wrongOptionsExplanation: A: Tape Gateway exposes virtual tape library/tape drives for backup software (including iSCSI tape targets), not normal writable iSCSI disk volumes for application data. B: FSx File Gateway and S3 File Gateway offer file protocols such as SMB/NFS, not required iSCSI block volumes. C: Correct, cached Volume Gateway provides iSCSI, local hot-data cache, S3-backed capacity, and AWS Backup point-in-time volume protection. D: S3 File Gateway caches file shares but does not provide iSCSI disk volumes.
plainWords: Provide scalable cloud-backed storage to legacy on-premises applications using iSCSI, keep frequently used data fast in a local cache, and back up volumes using AWS Backup.
keyPoints: Domain 4 single-answer position 17/138 (Q143 of 674 total bank). C. Volume Gateway cached mode = iSCSI block device + local hot-data cache + S3 primary storage. AWS Backup snapshots stored as EBS snapshots. Stored Volume Gateway keeps all primary data locally, unlike cached mode. AWS: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/storagegateway/latest/vgw/StorageGatewayConcepts.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/storagegateway/latest/vgw/backing-up-volumes.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/storagegateway/latest/vgw/WhatIsStorageGateway.html . External exact question: https://www.examtopics.com/discussions/amazon/view/142930-exam-aws-certified-solutions-architect-professional-sap-c02/ ; https://www.examcollection.us/exam/SAP-C02-question-answer-2.html ; https://www.pass4future.com/questions/amazon/sap-c02
sourceWarning: Original question and options preserved; source has missing space in 'data.Which' and uses 'file applications' while explicitly requiring iSCSI block storage. Tape Gateway may expose iSCSI virtual tape devices but not ordinary iSCSI block disks; distinguish tape from Volume Gateway. Cached mode depends on AWS for cache misses and does not guarantee all data locally. No answer-changing defect identified.

stem: A company migrated to AWS and uses AWS Business Support. The company wants to monitor thecost-effectiveness of Amazon EC2 instances. The EC2 instances have tags for department, business unit, and environment. Development EC2 instances have high cost but low utilization. The company needs to detect and stop any underutilized development EC2 instances. Instances are underutilized if they had 10% or less average CPU utilization and 5 MB or less network I/O for at least 4 of the past 14 days. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Configure Amazon CloudWatch dashboards to monitor EC2 instance utilization based on tags for department, business unit, and environment. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that invokes an AWS Lambda function to stop underutilized development EC2 instances.

Configure AWS Systems Manager to track EC2 instance utilization and report underutilized instances to Amazon CloudWatch. Filter the CloudWatch data by tags for department, business unit, and environment. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that invokes an AWS Lambda function to stop underutilized EC2 instances.

Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to detect low utilization of EC2 instances reported by AWS Trusted Advisor. Configure the rule to invoke a Lambda function that filters the data by tags for department, business unit, and environment and stops underutilized development EC2 instances.

Create an AWS Lambda function to run daily to retrieve utilization data for all EC2 instances. Save the data to an Amazon DynamoDB table. Create a QuickSight dashboard that uses the DynamoDB table as a data source to identify and stop underutilized development EC2 instances.

explanation: CORRECTED B -> C based on AWS Trusted Advisor official documentation, AWS-published Trusted-Advisor-Tools automation example, and external exact-question SAP-C02 copy selecting C. The specific threshold (<=10% daily average CPU and <=5 MB network I/O on at least 4 of previous 14 days) exactly matches the legacy Trusted Advisor Low utilization Amazon EC2 instances check (Qch7DwouX1). Trusted Advisor identifies underutilized EC2 resources without custom historical metric processing; EventBridge check notifications can trigger Lambda, which validates department/business-unit/environment tags, checks current state, and stops eligible development EC2 instances. Trusted Advisor EventBridge events are best effort and emitted in us-east-1; production implementations should use periodic reconciliation and avoid stopping critical or ASG-managed instances without safeguards. The legacy check is now superseded by newer Cost Optimization Hub-backed EC2 cost optimization recommendations.
wrongOptionsExplanation: A: CloudWatch dashboards visualize utilization but do not by themselves implement the 4-of-14-days CPU+network check or detect instances for EventBridge; custom evaluation is required. B: Original incorrect key; Systems Manager does not provide this exact Trusted Advisor low-utilization check and the option never defines the required 14-day rule; extra configuration. C: Correct intended choice; Trusted Advisor native low-utilization finding -> EventBridge -> Lambda checks tags and stops development instances. D: Daily Lambda + DynamoDB history + QuickSight dashboard is custom, high-overhead and QuickSight does not itself stop instances.
plainWords: Automatically stop only development EC2 instances meeting AWS's specific low-utilization rule while minimizing the need to build custom monitoring.
keyPoints: Q144 answer CORRECTED B -> C. Trusted Advisor legacy check Qch7DwouX1 uses <=10% CPU, <=5 MB network I/O for >=4 of previous 14 days. EventBridge receives Trusted Advisor events in us-east-1 on best-effort basis; Lambda filters environment/dept/business-unit tags and safely calls EC2 StopInstances. Sources: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awssupport/latest/user/cost-optimization-checks.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awssupport/latest/user/cloudwatch-events-ta.html ; https://github.com/aws/Trusted-Advisor-Tools/blob/master/LowUtilizationEC2Instances/README.md ; https://www.examtopics.cn/exam-aws-certified-solutions-architect-professional-1
sourceWarning: SOURCE ANSWER ERROR: Original JSON keyed B, but exact AWS Trusted Advisor threshold and external exact question verify C. Legacy/outdated wording: AWS Business Support plan name differs from current AWS Business Support+ documentation, and Trusted Advisor Low utilization Amazon EC2 instances check Qch7DwouX1 is explicitly marked legacy in current docs, superseded by EC2 cost optimization recommendations backed by Cost Optimization Hub. Trusted Advisor EventBridge notifications are best effort, emitted in us-east-1, and should not be the only production detection mechanism; implement periodic reconciliation, tag safeguards and exclusions. Original stem and options preserved, including typo 'thecost-effectiveness'.

review.sourceAnswerCorrection: B → C (already present in source before this review)
review.notes: Legacy check matches <=10% daily CPU and <=5 MB network I/O on 4 of 14 days. Trusted Advisor -> EventBridge (best effort, us-east-1) -> tag-aware Lambda is intended low-overhead answer. Periodic reconciliation and stop safeguards recommended. Original wording retained; check is legacy and current support plan terminology is Business Support+.

stem: A company runs its sales reporting application in an AWS Region in the United States. The application uses an Amazon API Gateway Regional API and AWS Lambda functions to generate on-demand reports from data in an Amazon RDS for MySQL database. The frontend of the application is hosted on Amazon S3 and is accessed by users through an Amazon CloudFront distribution. The company is using Amazon Route 53 as the DNS service for the domain. Route 53 is configured with a simple routing policy to route traffic to the API Gateway API. In the next 6 months, the company plans to expand operations to Europe. More than 90% of the database traffic is read-only traffic. The company has already deployed an API Gateway API and Lambda functions in the new Region. A solutions architect must design a solution that minimizes latency for users who download reports. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Use an AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) task with full load to replicate the primary database in the original Region to the database in the new Region. Change the Route 53 record to latency-based routing to connect to the API Gateway API.

Use an AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) task with full load plus change data capture (CDC) to replicate the primary database in the original Region to the database in the new Region. Change the Route 53 record to geolocation routing to connect to the API Gateway API.
Configure a cross-Region read replica for the RDS database in the new Region. Change the Route 53 record to latency-based routing to connect to the API Gateway API.
Configure a cross-Region read replica for the RDS database in the new Region. Change the Route 53 record to geolocation routing to connect to the API

explanation: VERIFIED C against AWS documentation and exact matching CertEnsure SAP-C02 Question 150. RDS for MySQL supports asynchronous cross-Region read replicas to serve >90% read-only report queries from a nearby European database. Route 53 latency-based routing chooses the deployed API Gateway Region with the lowest measured user-to-Region latency. Ensure European Lambda uses the European replica endpoint and all writes still go to the US primary; replication lag means read-after-write consistency is not guaranteed. AWS official: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_ReadRepl.XRgn.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/routing-policy-latency.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_ReadRepl.html . wrongOptionsExplanation: A: DMS full load migrates existing data only; it does not continuously replicate subsequent updates, making regional reports stale even though latency routing is appropriate. B: DMS full load + CDC does support ongoing replication but adds migration/replication management; geolocation chooses by user geography rather than measured latency. C: Native RDS cross-Region read replica is managed and suits read-heavy reporting; Route 53 latency routing optimizes API Region selection. D: Native replica is appropriate, but geolocation is not latency-optimized; original D text is truncated after 'connect to the API'.
plainWords: Keep the writable MySQL database in the US, place a continuously updated read replica near European users, and send each user's API requests to the lowest-latency AWS Region.
keyPoints: RDS MySQL cross-Region read replica (asynchronous, read-only, potential replication lag); Route 53 latency-based routing vs geolocation; DMS full load vs full load+CDC; Lambda must use regional replica for reads and primary for writes. Official: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_ReadRepl.XRgn.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/routing-policy-latency.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/userguide/CHAP_Task.CDC.html . stem: A company is planning to migrate an application to AWS. The application runs as a Docker container and uses an NFS version 4 file share. Use Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) for shared storage. Mount the EFS file system on the ECS container instances. Add the EFS authorization IAM role to the EC2 instance profile.

Deploy the application containers by using Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with the Amazon EC2 launch type and auto scaling turned on. Use Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes with Multi-Attach enabled for shared storage. Attach the EBS volumes to ECS container instances. explanation: Verified answer A from AWS documentation and exact external SAP-C02 matches (ExamTopics topic 1 Q191 and PUPUWEB). ECS Fargate runs Docker containers without provisioning/managing EC2 hosts; EFS supports NFSv4 shared elastic file storage and ECS Fargate EFS volume definitions. Define EFS fileSystemId, mountPoints and IAM authorization (authorizationConfig.iam ENABLED using ECS task role), enable transitEncryption, and apply EFS access point and security-group controls. Official: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/specify-efs-config.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/efs-best-practices.html .
wrongOptionsExplanation: A: CORRECT. Fargate is serverless container compute and EFS is managed NFS shared storage; ECS task definition configures the EFS mount and IAM task role authorization. B: WRONG. FSx for Lustre uses Lustre rather than NFSv4; AWS explicitly states FSx for Lustre mounting is unsupported on Fargate. C: WRONG. EFS works with ECS EC2, but EC2 host provisioning, OS patching, node capacity and mounts remain managed by customer, violating no infrastructure management. D: WRONG. ECS EC2 needs host management, and EBS Multi-Attach is block storage rather than an NFSv4 shared file service; concurrent writes require suitable coordination/cluster-aware file systems.
plainWords: Run Docker containers without managing servers, while preserving the existing shared NFS file storage: use ECS Fargate plus EFS.
keyPoints: Fargate=no EC2 host management; EFS=managed shared NFSv4 file system; ECS EFS volume configuration uses fileSystemId, mountPoints, authorizationConfig.iam ENABLED with taskRoleArn, transitEncryption ENABLED. FSx for Lustre unsupported on Fargate. EC2 launch type requires managing hosts. EBS Multi-Attach is block storage, not NFS. stem: A company has a payment gateway that processes millions of daily transactions on AWS. explanation: AWS-DOC-VERIFIED intended answer C: move ECS service from a single unmanaged EC2 host to ECS on Fargate with multiple tasks across at least two AZs; add an Aurora PostgreSQL reader in another AZ as an automatic failover target. Fargate eliminates host management and ECS balances tasks across AZs. Aurora reader promotion addresses writer-instance failure. Configure multi-AZ load balancer, task desiredCount>=2, health checks, scaling and idempotent payment retries. stem: A company is migrating to AWS and needs to inventory physical and virtual servers, apps, and database relationships to properly rightsize and plan migration.

Use Migration Hub import tool.

explanation: Historically B is best of four options. AWS Application Discovery Agent runs on physical and virtual Linux/Windows hosts and collects system utilization, running processes and TCP network connections, enabling dependency mapping and sizing. Migration Hub Strategy Recommendations assesses migration/modernization options. IMPORTANT 2026 UPDATE: AWS Migration Hub stopped accepting new customers on 2025-11-07; AWS recommends AWS Transform for new projects. Existing Migration Hub customers can continue using the service. No exact external exam-site question match established. wrongOptionsExplanation: A: Migration Evaluator and Agentless Collector help assess infrastructure and cost but are less comprehensive for physical/virtual server running-process and application dependency discovery. B: Intended historical correct answer: Discovery Agent inventories physical and virtual servers with processes, performance and TCP dependencies; Strategy Recommendations supports migration planning. C: Agentless Collector covers VMware VMs and database metadata but differs from per-server agent for physical host/process detail; 'Migration Service' is ambiguous and does not provide complete planning strategy. D: Migration Hub import uses preexisting inventory data and cannot independently detect processes or live network connections.

keyPoints: Discovery Agent: physical+VM Windows/Linux, CPU/RAM, processes, TCP dependencies. Agentless Collector: VMware and DB inventory/metrics, different coverage. CSV import does not discover runtime dependencies. Migration Hub Strategy Recommendations historically supports migration planning; AWS Migration Hub stopped onboarding new customers Nov 7 2025 and AWS Transform is recommended. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/application-discovery/latest/userguide/discovery-agent.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/application-discovery/latest/userguide/what-is-appdiscovery.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/migrationhub-strategy/latest/userguide/migrationhub-availability-change.html . Use Multi-AZ EKS worker nodes and Multi-AZ FSx for availability. Enhanced scanning targets images in ECR, not live running pods; configure image scanning and remediation workflows. Deploy an AWS DataSync agent on a new general purpose Amazon EC2 instance Configure the DataSync agent to copy the batch of files from the NFS on-premises server to Amazon S3 Standard After the successful copy deletes the data from the on-premises storage Create an S3 Lifecycle rule to transition objects from S3 Standard to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 1 day

Deploy an AWS Storage Gateway Tape Gateway on premises in the Hyper-V environment Connect the Tape Gateway to AWS Use automatic tape creation Specify an Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive pool Eject the tape after the batch of images is copied

explanation: VERIFIED B using AWS DataSync FAQ and user guide plus exact SAP-C02 Question 457 external match. Deploy the DataSync agent as an on-premises Hyper-V VM to reuse existing compute; transfer NFS-stored ZIP archives directly to S3 Glacier Deep Archive, with DataSync task scheduling for non-business hours and built-in bandwidth throttling. Deep Archive retrieval (hours to days) meets within-one-week requirement at lower long-term storage cost than Instant Retrieval or S3 Standard. Verify successful transfers and integrity before removing local source files. AWS: https://aws.amazon.com/datasync/faqs/ ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/datasync/latest/userguide/create-s3-location.html . Exact external: https://www.examtopics.com/discussions/amazon/view/136604-exam-aws-certified-solutions-architect-professional-sap-c02-topic-1-question-457-discussion/ .
wrongOptionsExplanation: A: GPU EC2 instance is unnecessary and adds cost; S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval has higher long-term storage cost than Deep Archive and immediate access is not needed. B: CORRECT; DataSync agent on existing Hyper-V compute reads NFS, directly stores in Deep Archive, supports schedule and bandwidth limits. C: New EC2 agent and initial S3 Standard staging/lifecycle transition add compute, temporary storage and management costs; direct transfer to Deep Archive is supported. D: Tape Gateway is designed for virtual tape backup applications, not a direct NFS ZIP archive transfer, and requires a new tape-oriented workflow.
plainWords: Use the spare Hyper-V capacity to run a DataSync agent, copy compressed archive files from NFS directly to low-cost S3 Glacier Deep Archive at night, and throttle bandwidth.
keyPoints: DataSync supports on-premises Hyper-V agent, NFS source, direct S3 Glacier Deep Archive destination, off-hours task scheduling and bandwidth throttling. S3 Glacier Deep Archive restoration takes hours to days, meeting one-week SLA; verify successful copy before source deletion. Deep Archive verification use Verify only data transferred, not Verify all destination. Exact ExamTopics SAP-C02 Q457 confirms B. https://aws.amazon.com/datasync/faqs/ ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/datasync/latest/userguide/create-s3-location.html ; https://www.examtopics.com/discussions/amazon/view/136604-exam-aws-certified-solutions-architect-professional-sap-c02-topic-1-question-457-discussion/ .

stem: A company has many AWS accounts in an organization in AWS Organizations. The accounts contain many Amazon EC2 instances that run different types of workloads. The workloads have different usage patterns. The company needs recommendations for how to rightsize the EC2 instances based on CPU and memory usage during the last 90 days. options.text: Opt in to AWS Compute Optimizer and enable trusted access for Compute Optimizer for the organization.
Configure a delegated administrator account for AWS Systems Manager for the organization.
Use an AWS CloudFormation stack set to enable detailed monitoring for all the EC2 instances.
Install and configure the Amazon CloudWatch agent on all the EC2 instances to send memory utilization metrics to CloudWatch.
Activate enhanced metrics in AWS Compute Optimizer.
Configure AWS Systems Manager to pass metrics to AWS Trusted Advisor.

stem: A company uses AWS Organizations to manage a multi-account structure. The company has hundreds of AWS accounts and expects the number of accounts to increase. The company is building a new application that uses Docker images. The company will push the Docker images to Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR). Only accounts that are within the company's organization should have access to the images. The company has a CI/CD process that runs frequently. The company wants to retain all the tagged images. However, the company wants to retain only the five most recent untagged images. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Create a private repository in Amazon ECR. Create a permissions policy for the repository that allows only required ECR operations. Include a condition to allow the ECR operations if the value of the aws:PrincipalOrglD condition key is equal to the ID of the company's organization. Add a lifecycle rule to the ECR repository that deletes all untagged images over the count of five.

Create a public repository in Amazon ECR. Create an IAM role in the ECR account. Set permissions so that any account can assume the role if the value of the aws:PrincipalOrglD condition key is equal to the ID of the company's organization. Add a lifecycle rule to the ECR repository that deletes all untagged images over the count of five.

Create a private repository in Amazon ECR. Create a permissions policy for the repository that includes only required ECR operations. Include a condition to allow the ECR operations for all account IDs in the organization. Schedule a daily Amazon EventBridge rule to invoke an AWS Lambda function that deletes all untagged images over the count of five.

Create a public repository in Amazon ECR. Configure Amazon ECR to use an interface VPC endpoint with an endpoint policy that includes the required permissions for images that the company needs to pull. Include a condition to allow the ECR operations for all account IDs in the company's organization. Schedule a daily Amazon EventBridge rule to invoke an AWS Lambda function that deletes all untagged images over the count of five.

stem: A company uses IAM Identity Center for data scientist access. Each user should be able to accessonly their own datain an S3 bucket. The company also needs to generatemonthly access reportsper user. Options:

options.text: Use IAM Identity Center permission sets to allow S3 access scoped to userName tag.
Use a shared IAM Identity Center role for all users and bucket policy.
Use AWS CloudTrail to log S3 data events, query via Athena.

stem: A company is running a serverless application that consists of several AWS Lambda functions and Amazon DynamoDB tables. The company has created new functionality that requires the Lambda functions to access an Amazon Neptune DB cluster. The Neptune DB cluster is located in three subnets in a VPC. Which of the possible solutions will allow the Lambda functions to access the Neptune DB cluster and DynamoDB tables? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Create three public subnets in the Neptune VPC, and route traffic through an internet gateway. Host the Lambda functions in the three new public subnets.
Create three private subnets in the Neptune VPC, and route internet traffic through a NAT gateway. Host the Lambda functions in the three new private subnets.
Host the Lambda functions outside the VPC. Update the Neptune security group to allow access from the IP ranges of the Lambda functions.
Host the Lambda functions outside the VPC. Create a VPC endpoint for the Neptune database, and have the Lambda functions access Neptune over the VPC endpoint.
Create three private subnets in the Neptune VPC. Host the Lambda functions in the three new isolated subnets. Create a VPC endpoint for DynamoDB, and route DynamoDB traffic to the VPC endpoint.

stem: A company plans to migrate a legacy on-premises application to AWS. The application is a Java web application that runs on Apache Tomcat with a PostgreSQL database. The company does not have access to the source code but can deploy the application Java Archive (JAR) files. The application has increased traffic at the end of each month. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Launch Amazon EC2 instances in multiple Availability Zones. Deploy Tomcat and PostgreSQL to all the instances by using Amazon EFS mount points. Use AWS Step Functions to deploy additional EC2 instances to scale for increased traffic.
Provision Amazon EKS in an Auto Scaling group across multiple AWS Regions. Deploy Tomcat and PostgreSQL in the container images. Use a Network Load Balancer to scale for increased traffic.

Refactor the Java application into Python-based containers. Use AWS Lambda functions for the application logic. Store application data in Amazon DynamoDB global tables. Use AWS Storage Gateway and Lambda concurrency to scale for increased traffic.

Use AWS Elastic Beanstalk to deploy the Tomcat servers with auto scaling in multiple Availability Zones. Store application data in an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL database. Deploy Amazon CloudFront and an Application Load Balancer to scale for increased traffic.

explanation: D is the intended best answer, corroborated by exact external SAP-C02 copies (ExamTopics Q504; CertsTopics Q48 answer D) and current AWS Elastic Beanstalk/RDS documentation. Elastic Beanstalk Tomcat load-balanced environment provisions and Auto Scales Java/Tomcat servers across AZs; RDS PostgreSQL manages DB infrastructure; ALB distributes requests and CloudFront caches suitable content. IMPORTANT defect: source says deployable JARs only, whereas Elastic Beanstalk Tomcat requires a deployable WAR. Elastic Beanstalk Java SE can run executable JARs but is not identical to Tomcat platform; if only library JARs are available, more packaging detail is needed. Official: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticbeanstalk/latest/dg/create_deploy_Java.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticbeanstalk/latest/dg/java-tomcat-platform.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticbeanstalk/latest/dg/java-se-platform.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticbeanstalk/latest/dg/java-rds.html .
wrongOptionsExplanation: A: EC2 Tomcat and PostgreSQL self-management plus Step Functions custom scaling is operationally expensive; EFS shared mounts do not provide appropriate relational DB architecture. B: EKS containerization and Kubernetes across Regions add complexity; PostgreSQL in app containers adds stateful DB burden; NLB distributes traffic but does not itself scale EKS workloads. C: Source code unavailable, so Java-to-Python refactor is infeasible; DynamoDB requires data-model/application rewrite; Storage Gateway is irrelevant. D: Best available: Elastic Beanstalk Tomcat managed environment with multi-AZ Auto Scaling, RDS PostgreSQL, ALB and optionally CloudFront. Caveat: Tomcat platform expects WAR, not arbitrary JAR; Java SE platform can run executable JARs.
plainWords: For an existing Tomcat and PostgreSQL application with monthly traffic spikes, choose managed Elastic Beanstalk scaling and RDS rather than rebuilding the application or managing servers. Confirm the available Java package is deployable.
keyPoints: Elastic Beanstalk Tomcat supports Java servlet WAR apps, load-balanced multi-AZ Auto Scaling; Java SE supports executable JAR apps. RDS PostgreSQL handles managed DB. ALB balances traffic; CloudFront improves cacheable/static responses but is not the core Auto Scaling mechanism. Exact external Q504 and Q48 answer D. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticbeanstalk/latest/dg/java-tomcat-platform.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticbeanstalk/latest/dg/java-se-platform.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticbeanstalk/latest/dg/java-rds.html .
sourceWarning: TECHNICAL PACKAGING DEFECT: Question says company can deploy Java Archive (JAR) files, but choice D uses Elastic Beanstalk Tomcat platform, which expects a web application archive (WAR). A runnable fat/executable JAR may work with Elastic Beanstalk Java SE, not automatically on Tomcat. If JARs are only dependencies and no deployable WAR exists, none of the options fully describes a working deployment. D is best intended architecture, not an unqualified deployable configuration. CloudFront optional for cacheable content; ALB does not itself increase EC2 capacity—Auto Scaling does. Exact external matches preserve same defect.

defects: JAR-only source conflicts with Tomcat WAR deployment requirement
ALB balances traffic; Auto Scaling adjusts capacity; CloudFront is optional
review.notes: Retain D as exam-intended best choice; warn WAR/JAR packaging gap. AWS documentation and two exact exam sites checked.

stem: A company runs a web-crawling process on a list of target URLs to obtain training documents for machine learning (ML) training algorithms. A fleet of Amazon EC2 t2.micro instances pulls the target URLs from an Amazon SQS queue. The instances write the result of the crawling algorithm as a CSV file to an Amazon EFS volume. The EFS volume is mounted on all instances in the fleet. A second system occasionally adds the URLs to the SQS queue. The EC2 instances crawl each new URL in 10 seconds or less. Metrics indicate that some instances are idle when no URLs are in the SQS queue. A solutions architect needs to redesign the architecture to optimize costs. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Use m5.8xlarge instances instead of t2.micro instances for the web-crawling process. Reduce the number of instances in the fleet by 50%.
Use an AWS Lambda function to run the web-crawling process. Configure the Lambda function to pull URLs from the SQS queue.
Modify the web-crawling process to store results in Amazon Neptune.
Modify the web-crawling process to store results in an Amazon Aurora Serverless MySQL instance.
Modify the web-crawling process to store results in Amazon S3.

stem: A startup company recently migrated a large ecommerce website to AWS The website has experienced a 70% increase in sates Software engineers are using a private GitHub repository to manage code The DevOps team is using Jenkins for builds and unit testing The engineers need to receive notifications for bad builds and zero downtime during deployments The engineers also need to ensure any changes to production are seamless for users and can be rolled back in the event of a major issue The software engineers have decided to use AWS CodePipeline to manage their build and deployment process Which solution will meet these requirements'?

options.text: Use GitHub websockets to trigger the CodePipeline pipeline Use the Jenkins plugin for AWS CodeBuild to conduct unit testing Send alerts to an Amazon SNS topic for any bad builds Deploy inan in-place all-at-once deployment configuration using AWS CodeDeploy

Use GitHub webhooks to trigger the CodePipelme pipeline Use the Jenkins plugin for AWS CodeBuild to conduct unit testing Send alerts to an Amazon SNS topic for any bad builds Deploy in a blue'green deployment using AWS CodeDeploy

Use GitHub websockets to trigger the CodePipelme pipeline. Use AWS X-Ray for unit testing and static code analysis Send alerts to an Amazon SNS topic for any bad builds Deploy in a blue/green deployment using AWS CodeDeploy.

Use GitHub webhooks to trigger the CodePipeline pipeline Use AWS X-Ray for unit testing and static code analysis Send alerts to an Amazon SNS topic for any bad builds Deploy in an m-place. all-at-once deployment configuration using AWS CodeDeploy

explanation: Intended answer B: GitHub change notifications trigger CodePipeline, Jenkins performs existing build/unit tests (integration via Jenkins action or CodeBuild Jenkins plugin must be clarified), Amazon SNS sends failed-build alerts, and AWS CodeDeploy blue/green traffic shifting enables lower-downtime deployments and rollback. AWS current recommendation for new GitHub source actions is AWS CodeConnections GitHub App, rather than legacy OAuth source action with separate webhook. Exact external exam copy lists same correct technical combination as option C because choices are reordered; user's JSON correct choice is B. AWS: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/update-github-action-connections.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/connections-github.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codedeploy/latest/userguide/deployments.html . External: https://myportal.utt.edu.tt/ICS/icsfs/e500bdfa-17d4-440e-8e02-1a46ed59d675.pdf?target=95f8256a-0bbf-48f2-b967-cb2097efacb3 .
wrongOptionsExplanation: A: 'GitHub websockets' is not the appropriate push-change trigger, and in-place all-at-once CodeDeploy risks downtime and poor rollback. B: Correct historical option; GitHub webhooks, Jenkins testing, SNS alerts, and CodeDeploy blue/green deployment. Current best practice is GitHub App CodeConnections; 'Jenkins plugin for AWS CodeBuild' is imprecise about how Jenkins is integrated. C: Websockets are wrong and AWS X-Ray traces distributed requests; it is not a unit-testing or static analysis replacement, although blue/green is good. D: GitHub webhook and SNS are fine but X-Ray is not a test/analysis tool, and all-at-once in-place deploy risks interruption.
plainWords: For safer CI/CD, trigger builds from GitHub changes, keep Jenkins tests, alert on failures, and deploy blue/green so you can switch back if a release breaks. Today prefer a GitHub App connection.
keyPoints: GitHub event triggers: webhooks/CodeConnections, not websockets. AWS X-Ray: distributed tracing, not unit testing. SNS: notifications on failed pipeline/build via EventBridge/notifications. CodeDeploy blue/green: shift traffic to new version, support rollback. In-place all-at-once: downtime risk. CodeConnections GitHub App preferred to legacy GitHub OAuth/webhook source. External exact copy reorders correct choice as C; JSON correct B. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/update-github-action-connections.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/connections-github.html .
sourceWarning: SOURCE OCR: 'sates' means sales; 'CodePipelme', 'inan', 'blue\'green', 'm-place' and missing punctuation. TECHNICAL AMBIGUITY: 'Jenkins plugin for AWS CodeBuild' conflates Jenkins-as-CodePipeline action with invoking CodeBuild via Jenkins plugin; specify actual integration in production. OUTDATED: legacy GitHub OAuth action + separate webhook is no longer AWS-recommended; use GitHub App via CodeConnections for new pipelines. EXACT EXTERNAL MATCH: external source labels correct technical combination C due to reordered options, while JSON answer B is the same solution; never copy external option letter without matching text. Blue/green can reduce downtime but zero downtime depends on health checks, target readiness, and traffic-shift configuration.

Legacy OAuth webhook source is not recommended for new CodePipeline integrations
Jenkins CodeBuild plugin wording conflates integration modes
Zero downtime needs appropriate health checks and traffic-shifting

stem: A company is using Amazon API Gateway to deploy a private REST API that will provide access to sensitive data. The API must be accessible only from an application that is deployed in a VPC. The company deploys the API successfully. However, the API is not accessible from an Amazon EC2 instance that is deployed in the VPC. Which solution will provide connectivity between the EC2 instance and the API?

options.text: Create an interface VPC endpoint for API Gateway. Attach an endpoint policy that allows apigateway:* actions. Disable private DNS naming for the VPC endpoint. Configure an API resource policy that allows access from the VPC. Use the VPC endpoint's DNS name to access the API.

Create an interface VPC endpoint for API Gateway. Attach an endpoint policy that allows the execute-api:lnvoke action. Enable private DNS naming for the VPC endpoint. Configure an API resource policy that allows access from the VPC endpoint. Use the API endpoint's DNS names to access the API. Most Voted

stem: A company is deploying an AI agent on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime. The agent automates business processes by accessing AWS resources and external services. The agent performs actions that do not require user interaction. The company needs the agent to authenticate as its own identity when accessing downstream services. The agent must maintain an audit trail that logs the agent identity for every action the agent performs. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Register the agent as a workload identity in an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity agent identity directory. Configure resource credential providers by using the OAuth 2.0 client credentials grant flow for each downstream service. Use the workload identity to give downstream services and audit systems the ability to identify which agent performed each action.
Create an IAM user for the agent. Store long-lived access keys in AWS Secrets Manager. Configure the agent to retrieve the keys at runtime and use the keys to authenticate to each downstream service.

Register the agent as a workload identity in an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity agent identity directory. Configure resource credential providers by using the OAuth 2.0 authorization code grant flow for each downstream service to obtain access tokens delegated on behalf of each user.
Create an IAM role for the agent. Configure each downstream service to accept IAM Signature Version 4 (SigV4) signed requests. Use AWS CloudTrail to log the IAM role ARN for auditing purposes.

stem: A retail business runs an orders and payments solution that uses more than 100 AWS Lambda functions that are written in Python. As the company's product catalog grows, the company observes that many of the functions time out. The company reconfigures the functions to have the maximum available timeout values, and the company increases memory for the functions. However, the functions continue to time out. The company investigates the timeout issue and finds that most failures occur when several functions have been chained together, which results in the initial function timing out while it waits for responses. A solutions architect must resolve these timeout issues while maintaining the cost and operational benefits of using Lambda functions. Which solution will meet these requirements with the MINIMUM amount of application changes?

options.text: Convert the solution to run in containers. Deploy an Amazon EKS cluster and enable auto scaling for the containers.
Rewrite the Lambda functions in Java. Implement Amazon SQS queues between functions.
Convert the solution to use an AWS Step Functions workflow to invoke the Lambda functions. Remove the direct function-to-function invocations.
Combine groups of linked functions together in a single container image. Deploy the container by using Amazon ECS on Amazon EC2 Spot Instances.

stem: A company is using a single AWS Region for its ecommerce website. The website includes a web application that runs on several Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The website also includes an Amazon DynamoDB table. A custom domain name in Amazon Route 53 is linked to the ALB. The company created an SSL/TLS certificate in AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) and attached the certificate to the ALB. The company is not using a content delivery network as part of its design. The company wants to replicate its entire application stack in a second Region to provide disaster recovery, plan for future growth, and provide improved access time to users. A solutions architect needs to implement a solution that achieves these goals and minimizes administrative overhead. Which combination of steps should the solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Select THREE.)

options.text: Create an AWS CloudFormation template for the current infrastructure design. Use parameters for important system values, including Region. Use the CloudFormation template to create the new infrastructure in the second Region.
Use the AWS Management Console to document the existing infrastructure design in the first Region and to create the new infrastructure in the second Region.
Update the Route 53 hosted zone record for the application to use weighted routing. Send 50% of the traffic to the ALB in each Region.
Update the Route 53 hosted zone record for the application to use latency-based routing. Send traffic to the ALB in each Region.
Update the configuration of the existing DynamoDB table by enabling DynamoDB Streams. Add the second Region to create a global table.

Create a new DynamoDB table. Enable DynamoDB Streams for the new table. Add the second Region to create a global table. Copy the data from the existing DynamoDB table to the new table as a one-time operation.

stem: A company runs a test application on an Amazon EC2 instance. Testing clients across the United States send data to the application by using a REST API. As traffic increases, application response times increase. The company wants to migrate to a serverless architecture and stream data to clients through WebSockets. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Create a new Amazon API Gateway REST API. Implement the business logic in AWS Lambda functions. Set the Lambda functions as integrations to the new REST API. Create a new AWS Step Functions state machine and set the clients as targets. Use the state machine to send data back to the clients.

Create a new Amazon API Gateway HTTP API and an Amazon SQS queue. Configure the HTTP API to integrate with the SQS queue. Implement the business logic in an AWS Lambda function. Use the SQS queue to invoke the Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to write data to an AWS AppSync Events channel. Ensure that the clients subscribe to the AWS AppSync Events channel.

Create a new AWS AppSync API and a new Amazon SQS queue. Integrate the SQS queue with the AWS AppSync API. Update the current business logic to consume from the SQS queue. Create a new Amazon EventBridge event bus and an EventBridge rule. Set the clients as targets for the rule. Use the EventBridge event bus to send data back to the clients.

Create a new Amazon CloudFront distribution. Implement the business logic in a CloudFront function. Set the CloudFront function as an origin of the CloudFront distribution. Enable AWS IoT Core. Configure the CloudFront function to write data to an MQTT topic. Ensure that the clients subscribe to the IoT Core MQTT topic through WebSockets.

explanation: VERIFIED B: API Gateway HTTP API supports first-class SQS-SendMessage integration; SQS buffers request bursts; Lambda SQS event source mapping polls queue and invokes business logic; Lambda publishes results to AWS AppSync Events HTTP endpoint; subscribed clients receive real-time WebSocket messages. AppSync Events launched March 2025 and is current, not outdated. AWS docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/http-api-develop-integrations-aws-services.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/services-sqs-configure.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/appsync/latest/eventapi/publish-http.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/appsync/latest/eventapi/event-api-websocket-protocol.html . Exact third-party question copy: https://www.dumpspedia.com/sap-c02-aws-certified-solutions-architect-professional-dumps.html (question 179).
wrongOptionsExplanation: A: API Gateway REST+Lambda can accept input, but Step Functions state machines cannot use arbitrary WebSocket clients as direct targets or deliver live WebSocket broadcasts. B: CORRECT: HTTP API->SQS->Lambda->AppSync Events channel->WebSocket subscribers, with fully managed scalable ingestion and broadcasting. C: AppSync API does not directly consume SQS as described, and EventBridge rules cannot use arbitrary WebSocket clients as targets. D: CloudFront Functions cannot serve as CloudFront origins or act as general-purpose backend to publish to IoT Core MQTT; although IoT Core supports MQTT over WebSockets, proposed integration is invalid.
plainWords: Receive client data through API Gateway, queue it to handle spikes, process it with Lambda, then broadcast updates through AppSync Events WebSockets.
keyPoints: HTTP API has native SQS-SendMessage integration; Lambda event source mapping polls SQS (SQS does not push-invoke Lambda); AWS AppSync Events Event API supports HTTP publishing and WebSocket subscriptions; configure channel namespace and IAM/auth permissions; at-least-once queue processing needs idempotency. Step Functions/EventBridge cannot directly target WebSocket clients; CloudFront Functions cannot be origins. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/http-api-develop-integrations-aws-services.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/services-sqs-configure.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/appsync/latest/eventapi/publish-http.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/appsync/latest/eventapi/event-api-websocket-protocol.html .
sourceWarning: Option B shorthand 'Use the SQS queue to invoke the Lambda function' is technically imprecise: Lambda polls SQS using an event source mapping. AppSync Events publishing requires a configured Event API, channel namespace, authorization and HTTP publish call; the source omits details but architecture is valid. SQS/Lambda is at-least-once, so idempotency and DLQ/error handling should be considered. Exact third-party question found as DumpsPedia question 179; source answer B matches AWS service capabilities. AppSync Events was introduced March 2025, so not outdated.

defects: SQS does not push-invoke Lambda; Lambda event source mapping polls queue
AppSync Events channel/auth/HTTP publishing configuration omitted
At-least-once SQS Lambda delivery requires idempotency
review.notes: AWS docs and exact third-party wording corroborate B. No obsolete service identified.

stem: A company has a website that runs on four Amazon EC2 instances that are behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). When the ALB detects that an EC2 instance is no longer available, an Amazon CloudWatch alarm enters the ALARM state. A member of the company's operations team then manually adds a new EC2 instance behind the ALB. A solutions architect needs to design a highly available solution that automatically handles the replacement of EC2 instances. The company needs to minimize downtime during the switch to the new solution. Which set of steps should the solutions architect take to meet these requirements?

options.text: Delete the existing ALB. Create an Auto Scaling group that is configured to handle the web application traffic. Attach a new launch template to the Auto Scaling group. Create a new ALB. Attach the Auto Scaling group to the new ALB. Attach the existing EC2 instances to the Auto Scaling group.

Create an Auto Scaling group that is configured to handle the web application traffic. Attach a new launch template to the Auto Scaling group. Attach the Auto Scaling group to the existing ALB. Attach the existing EC2 instances to the Auto Scaling group.

Delete the existing ALB and the EC2 instances. Create an Auto Scaling group that is configuredto handle the web application traffic. Attach a new launch template to the Auto Scaling group. Create a new ALB. Attach the Auto Scaling group to the new ALB. Wait for the Auto Scaling group to launch the minimum number of EC2 instances.

Create an Auto Scaling group that is configured to handle the web application traffic. Attach a new launch template to the Auto Scaling group. Attach the Auto Scaling group to the existing ALB. Wait for the existing ALB to register the existing EC2 instances with the Auto Scaling group.

stem: A company runs payment gateways in multiple AWS Regions. The company also operates on-premises data centers where the company manages hardware security modules (HSMs) to tokenize sensitive payment data to comply with security regulations. To process payment transactions within the company's performance SLA, the company requires an automated and centrally managed solution that can provide dedicated private connectivity between the on-premises HSMs and AWS payment services. Which solution will meet this requirement?

options.text: Use a centrally managed accelerator in AWS Global Accelerator to route traffic from each data center the nearest AWS Region.
Establish AWS Site-to-Site VPN connections between the data centers and AWS. Set up a centrally managed transit gateway and set appropriate routes.
Use AWS CloudHSM to tokenize the sensitive payment data. Deploy CloudHSM in the same private subnet as the payment services workload.
Set up AWS Cloud WAN with AWS Direct Connect attachments between on-premises data centers and AWS.

explanation: VERIFIED D. AWS Cloud WAN centrally manages multi-Region hybrid routing, segmentation and attachment policy; AWS Direct Connect provides dedicated private physical connectivity between on-premises HSM networks and AWS VPC workloads. Native Cloud WAN Direct Connect gateway attachments support BGP route propagation and remove the formerly required intermediate Transit Gateway (launched November 25, 2024). Exact external SAP-C02 Q15 selects D: https://www.certensure.com/amazon-web-services/sap-c02-cert-practice-test.html . AWS: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/network-manager/latest/cloudwan/cloudwan-dxattach-about.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/direct-connect-cloud-wan.html ; https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2024/11/aws-cloud-wan-on-premises-connectivity-direct-connect/ .
wrongOptionsExplanation: A: Global Accelerator optimizes routing to internet-facing/public application endpoints and does not create dedicated private connectivity from on-premises HSMs. B: Standard Site-to-Site VPN plus Transit Gateway provides encrypted connectivity and centralized routing but not a dedicated private circuit; typical VPN runs over public Internet. C: CloudHSM relocates HSM functionality to AWS instead of connecting the company's existing on-premises HSMs; not the requested networking solution. D: CORRECT; Direct Connect dedicated network connection with Cloud WAN centralized global core-network policy, segmentation, multi-Region routing, and native Direct Connect gateway attachment.
plainWords: Keep the regulated HSMs in the company's data centers, connect them privately through AWS Direct Connect, and manage routing across AWS Regions centrally with Cloud WAN.
keyPoints: Cloud WAN + Direct Connect gateway native attachment (November 2024) supports BGP route propagation, policy-based segmentation and central management without mandatory intermediate TGW. Configure actual Direct Connect circuits, transit VIF, DX gateway, core network attachment, and VPC attachments. Direct Connect dedicated private link does not by itself ensure end-to-end encryption; use TLS/MACsec as appropriate, redundancy, and monitor latency. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/network-manager/latest/cloudwan/cloudwan-dxattach-about.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/direct-connect-cloud-wan.html .
sourceWarning: Option D is architecturally correct but underspecified: native Cloud WAN attachment attaches a Direct Connect GATEWAY, not a raw physical Direct Connect connection; requires existing DX circuit, transit VIF, DX gateway, Cloud WAN core network, attachment and BGP route configuration. Native support was released November 25, 2024; older AWS blogs claiming TGW is mandatory are stale. Direct Connect is not encryption by default; PCI/payment use case needs transport security and redundancy. External exact-match SAP-C02 Q15 independently supports D.

defects: Option D abbreviates DX gateway and transit VIF prerequisites
Older AWS docs/blogs requiring intermediate TGW are obsolete since November 2024
Dedicated DX does not inherently encrypt sensitive payment traffic
review.notes: D independently confirmed by AWS documentation and exact third-party Q15. Native Direct Connect gateway attachment to Cloud WAN core network is current.

stem: A company wants to modernize a monolithic application in the company's data center and deploy the application on AWS. The monolithic application consists of an event broker in a central account and multiple microservices in individual AWS accounts. The event broker and the microservices are deployed on Amazon ECS clusters that use the Fargate launch type. Multiple microservices need access to the same events from the event broker. The company wants to distribute events from the central event broker to each microservice across accounts. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Create an Amazon SNS topic in the central account. Add a topic policy to allow other accounts to subscribe to the topic. Create an Amazon SQS queue in each individual AWS account. Subscribe the SQS queue to the SNS topic. Configure the microservices to read events from their own SQS queue.

Create a new Amazon EventBridge event bus in the central account with the required permissions. Add EventBridge rules filtered by service for each microservice. Invoke the rules to route events to other accounts.

Create a data stream in Amazon Kinesis Data Streams in the central account. Create an IAM policy to grant the necessary permissions to access the data stream. Set each of the microservices as an event source on the Kinesis stream. Configure the stream to invoke each microservice.
Create a new Amazon SQS queue as the event broker in the central account. Grant the required permissions. Configure each of the microservices to read messages from the central SQS queue.

explanation: SOURCE KEY B (intended), but question is ambiguous: both B and A satisfy the stated requirements. EventBridge central event bus and rules route matching events to cross-account targets/buses with appropriate IAM execution roles and target resource policies. A cross-account SNS topic -> one SQS queue per service also fans out copies of each event independently and meets the requirements. Do not claim B uniquely correct without an additional requirement for content-based event routing. AWS: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-cross-account.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-service-cross-account.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sns/latest/dg/sns-send-message-to-sqs-cross-account.html . Exact external matches https://www.certensure.com/amazon-web-services/sap-c02-cert-practice-test.html (Q7), https://www.freecram.net/question/Amazon.SAP-C02.v2026-08-19.q305/a-company-wants-to-modernize-a-monolithic-application-in-the-company-s-data-center-and-deploy-the-application (source key B).
wrongOptionsExplanation: A: ALSO TECHNICALLY CORRECT—SNS fan-out to one cross-account SQS queue per microservice independently delivers each published event. Requires topic subscription permission and destination queue access policies. B: SOURCE-INTENDED—EventBridge event patterns and rules can route matching events to cross-account event buses or supported services (including SQS) with execution role and resource-based permissions; wording omits destinations and permissions detail. C: As written incorrect: Kinesis streams do not automatically invoke ECS Fargate microservices merely by setting each microservice as an event source; application consumers would need stream-reading logic. D: Incorrect: a single SQS queue implements competing consumers and does not distribute independent copies of each event to every microservice.
plainWords: Several microservices in separate AWS accounts need their own copy of events emitted centrally. EventBridge rule routing is a valid approach, and SNS fan-out to per-service SQS queues also works.
keyPoints: B is the third-party answer key but NOT unique. EventBridge supports filtered cross-account delivery, requiring a receiving target plus role/resource permissions. SNS topic + one SQS queue per service also provides cross-account fan-out. Single shared SQS queue delivers messages to competing consumers; Kinesis does not automatically invoke ECS Fargate services.
sourceWarning: DEFECTIVE SINGLE-ANSWER ITEM: BOTH A and B meet the literal requirements. Third-party keys choose B but AWS explicitly documents SNS->SQS cross-account fan-out. Option B is underspecified (target destinations and IAM/resource policy omitted). Reword to REQUIRE content-based filtered routing or rule-based event-bus integration to make B uniquely best.

defects: A is an equally valid cross-account distribution architecture
B omits destination resources and target IAM/resource-based permission configuration
review.notes: The external answer key says B; independently assessed against AWS documentation, A also satisfies all stated requirements. Retain answer key for compatibility but flag ambiguity for learner.

Deploy an Application Load Balancer (ALB) spanning multiple Availability Zones (AZs) to the VPC in the us-east-1 Region. stem: A company has deployed an application on AWS Elastic Beanstalk. The application uses Amazon Aurora for the database layer. stem: A company uses AWS Organizations to manage more than 1,000 AWS accounts. The company has created a new developer organization. There are 540 developer member accounts that must be moved to the new developer organization. All accounts are set up with all the required information so that each account can be operated as a standalone account. Which combination of steps should a solutions architect take to move all of the developer accounts to the new developer organization? (Select THREE.)

options.text: Call the MoveAccount operation in the Organizations API from the old organization's management account to migrate the developer accounts to the new developer organization.
From the management account, remove each developer account from the old organization using the RemoveAccountFromOrganization operation in the Organizations API.
From each developer account, remove the account from the old organization using the RemoveAccountFromOrganization operation in the Organizations API.
Sign in to the new developer organization's management account and create a placeholder member account that acts as a target for the developer account migration.
Call the InviteAccountToOrganization operation in the Organizations API from the new developer organization's management account to send invitations to the developer accounts.
Have each developer sign in to their account and confirm to join the new developer organization.

explanation: Historical exam answer B,E,F: source management account calls RemoveAccountFromOrganization for each member, destination management account sends InviteAccountToOrganization, and authorized users in member accounts accept invitations (AcceptHandshake). CRITICAL 2026 CHANGE: AWS Organizations now supports direct account transfers. The destination sends an invitation and the existing member accepts it without first leaving the original organization. Therefore B is optional, not mandatory, and this Select THREE item is outdated; E and F describe the current necessary steps.
wrongOptionsExplanation: A: MoveAccount is not a valid cross-organization transfer API (MoveAccount is used within an organization). C: RemoveAccountFromOrganization is callable only from the source management account; a member account uses LeaveOrganization to leave voluntarily. D: A placeholder destination member account is unnecessary. B is historically correct but unnecessary under direct transfer.
plainWords: Old process: remove 540 accounts from the first organization, invite them from the second, then accept each invitation. New process: the second organization invites the accounts directly, and the accounts accept; no standalone intermediate stage.
keyPoints: Historical B,E,F; current direct transfer E,F. RemoveAccountFromOrganization is management-account-only. LeaveOrganization is member-initiated. InviteAccountToOrganization is destination management account. AcceptHandshake is invited account. Confirm 7-day age of destination organization, 4-day minimum age for newly created accounts, Seller of Record compatibility, quotas, SCP/RCP and IAM dependencies, billing reports, and delegated admin roles.
sourceWarning: OUTDATED / DEFECTIVE SELECT THREE: Direct account transfers between AWS Organizations are supported; removal is no longer required. Retain B,E,F for historical practice but do not teach B as mandatory. Corrected OCR punctuation 1.000->1,000 and capitalization. AWS https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_account_migration.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/APIReference/API_RemoveAccountFromOrganization.html ; external exact variant https://www.examsvce.com/sap-c02/a-company-uses-aws-organizations-to-manage-75551-question-answer.html

review.notes: Compared 674 items; related multi-account migration/governance questions but no exact same-stem duplicate. Exact external variant ExamsVCE agrees B,E,F. Direct-transfer feature invalidates mandatory B.

stem: A company wants to migrate its on-premises data center to the AWS Cloud. This includes thousands of virtualized Linux and Microsoft Windows servers, SAN storage, Java and PHP applications with MySQL, and Oracle databases. There are many dependent services hosted either in the same data center or externally. The technical documentation is incomplete and outdated. A solutions architect needs to understand the current environment and estimate the cloud resource costs after the migration. Which tools or services should the solutions architect use to plan the cloud migration? (Choose three.)

options.text: AWS Application Discovery Service
AWS SMS
AWS x-Ray
AWS Cloud Adoption Readiness Tool (CART)
Amazon Inspector
AWS Migration Hub

explanation: A discovers on-premises server configuration, utilization, and dependencies. D assesses cloud adoption readiness and identifies migration gaps. F provides a central migration tracking and discovery view. B (AWS Server Migration Service) is a legacy server migration tool, not the primary assessment tool for this question. C (AWS X-Ray) traces distributed application requests after instrumentation; E (Amazon Inspector) assesses software vulnerabilities rather than mapping migration dependencies and estimating cloud costs. The question does not identify a dedicated cost estimation tool; AWS Pricing Calculator would be needed for a detailed estimate.
wrongOptionsExplanation: B: AWS Server Migration Service (SMS) is a legacy VM migration service, not a discovery/readiness/TCO planning tool. C: AWS X-Ray traces instrumented distributed applications and does not automatically discover on-premises SAN/server estates. E: Amazon Inspector assesses vulnerabilities, not migration inventories, dependency maps, or projected AWS costs.
plainWords: The company does not know exactly what it owns or how systems connect. First discover servers and dependencies, assess whether the organization is ready, and track the migration. Modern new projects should use AWS Transform.
keyPoints: Historical A,D,F. A = Application Discovery Service for server/dependency inventory; D = CART organizational readiness, not dollar-cost estimator; F = Migration Hub tracking and application grouping. Since Nov 7 2025 both ADS and Migration Hub closed to new customers; AWS Transform replaces their discovery/assessment/wave planning and supports cost estimates. For detailed pricing use AWS Pricing Calculator or AWS Transform cost assessment. SMS is legacy, X-Ray traces apps, Inspector scans vulnerabilities.
sourceWarning: OUTDATED: AWS Application Discovery Service and Migration Hub stopped accepting new customers Nov 7, 2025; AWS Transform is recommended for new projects. CART addresses organizational readiness rather than quantitative cloud cost estimates. Question's 'estimate cloud resource costs' is not fully answered by its offered services. Exact variants Cloud Study Exams Q10 and dumpscollection Q208 both A,D,F. Official https://docs.aws.amazon.com/application-discovery/latest/userguide/application-discovery-service-availability-change.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/migrationhub/latest/ug/migrationhub-availability-change.html

review.auditNote: AWS SMS (Server Migration Service) is a legacy migration option. Source key A,D,F retained. Short options B/C are service names, not necessarily truncated.
review.note: Verified entire 674 question bank; no exact stem duplicate. ADS and Migration Hub closed to new customers Nov 7 2025; recommend AWS Transform.

stem: A company is building an automated pipeline that uses AWS Step Functions to orchestrate multiple stages. The pipeline includes a confirmation stage. The company wants to avoid unnecessary compute consumption. The company must ensure that the workflow can remain pending over extended periods without state loss. The confirmation signal originates from a control-plane service that runs in a separate AWS account and is emitted asynchronously after human review. The solution must ensure that only the authorized external system can resume execution. The solution should not expose long-lived credentials. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Configure a Wait state with dynamically extended durations. Invoke an AWS Lambda function that checks approval status from the external system on each retry attempt.
Configure a Task state that uses a callback pattern to provide a unique correlation token and to resume execution only when the external system returns that token after approval.
Configure an activity worker that retrieves tasks and holds the workflow execution open within its own long-running process until approval is observed externally.
Configure an Amazon EventBridge rule that periodically triggers execution resumption by reinvoking the workflow with inputs that reflect approval state and correlation identifiers.

sourceWarning: AWS callback task tokens cannot be used directly by cross-account principals; B is incomplete without same-account bridge. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/step-functions/latest/dg/connect-to-resource.html

review.notes: AWS Step Functions callback tokens must be returned by principals in same AWS account; separate-account approval requires an authorized bridge in workflow account. B gives callback pattern but omits bridge.

stem: A company wants to manage the costs associated with a group of 20 applications that are infrequently used, but are still business-critical, by migrating to AWS. The applications are a mix of Java and Node.js spread across different instance clusters. The company wants to minimize costs while standardizing by using a single deployment methodology. Most of the applications are part of month-end processing routines with a small number of concurrent users, but they are occasionally run at other times Average application memory consumption is less than 1 GB. though some applications use as much as 2.5 GB of memory during peak processing. The most important application in the group is a billing report written in Java that accesses multiple data sources and often runs for several hours. Which is the MOST cost-effective solution?

options.text: Deploy a separate AWS Lambda function tor each application. Use AWS CloudTrail logs and Amazon CloudWatch alarms to verify completion of critical jobs.

Deploy Amazon ECS containers on Amazon EC2 with Auto Scaling configured for memory utilization of 75%. Deploy an ECS task for each application being migrated with ECS task scaling. Monitor services and hosts by using Amazon CloudWatch.
Deploy AWS Elastic Beanstalk for each application with Auto Scaling to ensure that all requests have sufficient resources. Monitor each AWS Elastic Beanstalk deployment by using CloudWatch alarms.

Deploy a new Amazon EC2 instance cluster that co-hosts all applications by using EC2 Auto Scaling and Application Load Balancers. Scale cluster size based on a custom metric set on instance memory utilization. Purchase 3-year Reserved Instance reservations equal to the GroupMaxSize parameter of the Auto Scaling group.

explanation: VERIFIED B. ECS on EC2 supports shared container capacity for Java/Node.js workloads including multi-hour billing jobs; EC2 Auto Scaling and ECS task/service scaling can adapt to sporadic use. AWS ECS capacity provider managed scaling and binpack placement optimize instance utilization. Exact external SAP-C02 CertEmpire demo Q7 selects B. Note 75% memory threshold is illustrative, not guaranteed cost-optimal. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/cluster-auto-scaling.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/managed-scaling-behavior.html ; https://certempire.com/demo-files/sap-c02-demo-certempire.pdf
wrongOptionsExplanation: A: Ordinary Lambda Event Functions run at most 15 minutes, and even eligible Lambda Managed Instances asynchronous/event-source-mapping functions introduced in 2026 max out at 90 minutes; uninterrupted multi-hour billing jobs do not fit. CloudTrail is not a dedicated job-completion monitor. B: CORRECT, standardized ECS container deployments with task scaling and shared autoscaled EC2 cluster; use ECS capacity providers, binpack, and scheduling to avoid idle hosts. C: Per-app Beanstalk environments and their baseline EC2 capacity are less economical for 20 rarely used applications. D: 3-year Reserved Instances sized to Auto Scaling GroupMaxSize overcommit to peak capacity and are wasteful for infrequent use.
plainWords: Twenty rarely used Java/Node.js applications include a critical report that runs for hours. Package them as ECS containers and share an autoscaling EC2 fleet rather than running a separate always-on environment per app.
keyPoints: ECS on EC2 handles long-running containers, shared infrastructure, task/service scaling and EC2 capacity providers. Binpack placement improves utilization. Lambda 15-minute standard timeout; September 2026 eligible Lambda Managed Instances extend asynchronous/ESM runs to 90 minutes, still not multi-hour. Avoid long-term reservations sized to infrequent peaks.
sourceWarning: Source typos: 'tor' should be 'for'; missing punctuation around 'other times Average' and '. though'. Source answer B verified exact-match CertEmpire PDF. 75% memory-based scaling alone does not guarantee lowest cost; scheduled run-task and capacity-provider managed scaling/binpack are implementation refinements. As of Sep 2026, blanket statement 'Lambda maximum 15 minutes' is outdated for eligible Lambda Managed Instances (90 minutes), but does not change answer for jobs running several hours.

defects: Minor original-source transcription errors
2026 Lambda Managed Instances 90-minute exception must be acknowledged
Fixed 75% scaling does not prove global cost minimum

explanation: SOURCE KEY C, best of four: ECR cross-Region replication for images, secondary ECS Fargate, Aurora Global Database for fast low-lag database recovery, AWS Backup Vault Lock compliance mode for immutable backup recovery points, S3 recovery/replication configuration, and Route 53 failover records. AWS Aurora typically replicates within seconds and can recover in minutes, but stated RPO 5m/RTO 15m are targets, not guaranteed merely by selecting services. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-global-database-disaster-recovery.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-backup/latest/devguide/vault-lock.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-global-database.html
wrongOptionsExplanation: A: Multivalue Route 53 answer routing is not a primary/secondary failover policy; regional ECR dependency and weaker database strategy. B: Route 53 failover is right but omits tamper-resistant backup configuration and S3 cross-Region recovery. C: BEST—ECR replication, ECS secondary, Aurora Global Database, Backup Vault Lock compliance, S3 backup/recovery, Route 53 failover; additional operational controls are required to actually meet RPO/RTO. D: Governance vault lock is removable by authorized users, less suitable for anti-tamper; geolocation routing is not disaster failover; S3 replication is missing.
plainWords: Prepare a working copy of the ecommerce site in another Region, replicate database and images, protect backups from tampering, and direct users to the backup Region when primary is unhealthy.
keyPoints: Aurora Global Database RPO typically seconds, RTO minutes with planned/tested failover. Compliance-mode Backup Vault Lock becomes immutable after grace period, unlike governance mode. ECR cross-Region replication removes image pull dependency. Route 53 failover needs health checks. S3 CRR asynchronous; S3 versioning/Object Lock/backup recovery point configuration and testing needed.
sourceWarning: SOURCE QUALITY: No independently confirmed exact external question match located during this review; source key C retained based on AWS documentation. Option C typo 'secondaryrecord'. S3 'enable point-in-time recovery' is imprecise: S3 versioning/AWS Backup continuous backups are distinct mechanisms. S3 CRR does not guarantee 5-minute RPO; consider replication metrics/RTC. Backup Vault Lock protects recovery points, not necessarily live S3 objects; Object Lock may be needed. Aurora Global Database, DNS and app readiness do not alone guarantee RTO 15 minutes; drill and automate.

S3 asynchronous replication does not guarantee 5-minute RPO
Vault Lock immutability applies to backup recovery points, not automatically live S3 objects
15-minute RTO requires operational design and drills
Option C 'secondaryrecord' typo

Deploy existing Docker workloads as Kubernetes pods; migrate MySQL via AWS DMS to managed RDS MySQL with Multi-AZ standby. sourceWarning: No independently verified exact third-party exam-site match found in this pass; answer B independently validated against AWS EKS docs. explanation: VERIFIED C. SQL Server Always On to RDS for MySQL is a heterogeneous engine migration. First convert source SQL Server schema and SQL objects to MySQL-compatible equivalents using AWS Schema Conversion Tool (SCT) or the newer recommended DMS Schema Conversion; then use AWS DMS to move data and optionally replicate changes to minimize downtime. AWS SQL Server to MySQL walkthrough: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/sbs/schema-conversion-sql-server-mysql.html ; https://aws.amazon.com/documentation-overview/dms/ .

B: Snowball Edge transports bulk data to S3 but neither converts SQL Server schema nor makes SQL Server BULK INSERT a MySQL import solution. C: CORRECT; AWS SCT converts schemas and code, AWS DMS migrates rows/CDC to RDS MySQL. D: DataSync is file/object transfer, not heterogeneous relational database migration; SQL Server BULK INSERT is not a valid MySQL conversion path.
plainWords: SQL Server and MySQL speak different SQL dialects. Convert the database structure first with SCT/DMS Schema Conversion, then transfer the actual records with AWS DMS.

AWS SCT (legacy downloadable tool) or recommended DMS Schema Conversion for schema; AWS DMS full load plus CDC for data. Validate SQL Server Always On source/CDC setup, unsupported stored procedures, app SQL compatibility and RDS MySQL HA.

AWS now recommends managed DMS Schema Conversion rather than legacy AWS SCT for new projects, but SCT remains supported/documented, so source answer C is valid. Exact independent third-party exam question match not confirmed. Business-critical migration requires CDC prerequisites, testing and target HA, none specified.

Always On/CDC prerequisites and application compatibility not specified
