stem: A company is planning a one-time migration of an on-premises MySQL database to Amazon Aurora MySQL in the us-east-1 Region. The company's current internet connection has limited bandwidth. The on-premises MySQL database is 60 TB in size The company estimates that it will take a month to transfer the data to AWS over the current internet connection. The company needs a migration solution that will migrate the database more quickly Which solution will migrate the database in the LEAST amount of time?

options.text: Request a 1 Gbps AWS Direct Connect connection between the on-premises data center and AWS Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to migrate the on- premises MySQL database to Aurora MySQL.

Use AWS DataSync with the current internet connection to accelerate the data transfer between the on-premises data center and AWS Use AWS Application Migration Service to migrate the on-premises MySQL database to Aurora MySQL.
Order an AWS Snowball Edge Device Load the data into an Amazon S3 bucket by using the S3 interface Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to migrate the data from Amazon S3 to Aurora MySQL
Order an AWS Snowball Device Load the data into an Amazon S3 bucket by usingthe S3 Adapter for Snowball Use AWS Application Migration Service to migrate the data from Amazon S3 to Aurora MySQL.

explanation: HISTORICAL KEY C, BUT DEFECTIVE IN 2026. Offline Snowball Edge could transfer 60 TB despite slow internet; DMS can migrate FROM S3 to Aurora MySQL only if source data are appropriately formatted CSV or supported Parquet with external table definitions, not raw MySQL backup files. AWS Snowball Edge unavailable to new customers since 2025-11-07 and end of commercial-region support announced for 2026-12-31. No fastest option is provable without shipping/import and Direct Connect provisioning durations. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/snowball/latest/developer-guide/snowball-edge-availability-change.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/userguide/CHAP_Source.S3.html ; https://aws.amazon.com/snowball/
wrongOptionsExplanation: A: Direct Connect 1 Gbps plus DMS is technically valid and raw 60 TB at sustained 1 Gbps takes about 5.6 days, excluding overhead and provisioning; cannot prove slower without provisioning time. B: DataSync file transfer and Application Migration Service server lift-and-shift do not migrate relational database directly into Aurora. C: historical intended offline Snowball Edge + S3 + DMS, but Snowball new-customer closure and missing S3 CSV/Parquet conversion invalidate as unconditional answer. D: older Snowball/S3 Adapter wording plus Application Migration Service cannot import S3 objects as Aurora MySQL database.
plainWords: To move a 60 TB database from a slow network, physical transfer historically avoided internet bottlenecks. Today Snowball is closed to new customers; a dedicated high-speed network or current physical-transfer alternatives must be evaluated with realistic timing.
keyPoints: Snowball Edge no new customers Nov 7 2025; commercial region support ends Dec 31 2026. AWS DMS S3 source supports formatted CSV/Parquet and mapping, not arbitrary database backup files. Direct Connect 1 Gbps ideal lower bound for 60 TB ~5.6 days, plus overhead; lead time unknown. AWS Application Migration Service moves servers, not S3-to-Aurora data.
sourceWarning: MAJOR OUTDATED/DEFECTIVE QUESTION. Original key C preserved as historical only: Snowball Edge unavailable to new customers after 2025-11-07, commercial region support ends 2026-12-31; S3-to-DMS needs formatted CSV/Parquet and schema mappings, absent in option. 'LEAST time' unanswerable without shipping, device order/import, and Direct Connect provisioning timelines; A can be faster depending on lead times. D uses obsolete Snowball Adapter and unsupported MGN S3->Aurora. Typos/missing punctuation in stem and choices. Exact external exam-site match not verified.

defects: Snowball closed to new customers November 2025
Snowball commercial support ends December 2026
S3 DMS requires formatted CSV/Parquet and table mappings, not raw MySQL dump
No timing information proving C faster than A
Typos and obsolete Snowball adapter in D
review.notes: Preserve historical source answer C; current question cannot be scored as unconditionally valid. Exact external exam match not verified.

stem: A company needs to move some on-premises Oracle databases to AWS. The company has chosen to keep some of the databases on premises for business compliance reasons. The on-premises databases contain spatial data and run cron jobs for maintenance. The company needs to connect to the on-premises systems directly from AWS to query data as a foreign table. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Create Amazon DynamoDB global tables with auto scaling enabled. Use AWS SCT and AWS DMS to move the data from on premises to DynamoDB. Create an AWS Lambda function to move the spatial data to Amazon S3. Query the data by using Amazon Athena. Use Amazon EventBridge to schedule jobs in DynamoDB for maintenance. Use Amazon API Gateway for foreign table support.

Create an Amazon RDS for Microsoft SQL Server DB instance. Use native replication to move the data from on premises to the DB instance. Use AWS SCT to modify the SQL Server schema as needed after replication. Move the spatial data to Amazon Redshift. Use stored procedures for system maintenance. Create AWS Glue crawlers to connect to the on-premises Oracle databases for foreign table support.

Launch Amazon EC2 instances to host the Oracle databases. Place the EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. Use AWS Application Migration Service to move the data from on premises to the EC2 instances and for real-time bidirectional change data capture (CDC) synchronization. Use Oracle native spatial data support. Create an AWS Lambda function to run maintenance jobs as part of an AWS Step Functions workflow. Create an internet gateway for foreign table support.

Create an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance. Use AWS SCT and AWS DMS to move the data from on premises to the DB instance. Use PostgreSQL native spatial data support. Run cron jobs on the DB instance for maintenance. Use AWS Direct Connect to connect the DB instance to the on-premises environment for foreign table support.

explanation: VERIFIED D, AWS documentation and exact third-party match. Migrate selected Oracle schemas to Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL using AWS SCT/DMS. Use PostGIS extension for spatial data, pg_cron for scheduled SQL maintenance tasks, and oracle_fdw extension to query Oracle tables that remain on premises via foreign tables. AWS Direct Connect provides private network connectivity, but foreign-table support requires CREATE EXTENSION oracle_fdw, CREATE SERVER, USER MAPPING, FOREIGN TABLE, plus routing/firewall permissions. AWS: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/postgresql-oracle-fdw.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/PostgreSQLReleaseNotes/postgresql-extensions.html ; external exact match https://www.examtopics.cn/exam-aws-certified-solutions-architect-professional-4 (Q36 No1508).
wrongOptionsExplanation: A: DynamoDB/Athena/API Gateway do not provide PostgreSQL-style foreign tables to on-prem Oracle, and EventBridge cannot run cron jobs inside DynamoDB. B: SQL Server native replication cannot directly migrate heterogeneous Oracle schemas as described; Glue crawlers catalog data, not expose on-prem Oracle as SQL foreign tables in RDS SQL Server. C: AWS Application Migration Service replicates servers, not bidirectional Oracle CDC; EC2 Auto Scaling is not a suitable database clustering strategy and internet gateway is not an Oracle foreign-data wrapper. D: CORRECT intended solution; SCT/DMS for heterogeneous migration, RDS PostgreSQL with PostGIS, pg_cron and oracle_fdw over Direct Connect. Clarify 'cron jobs on DB instance' means pg_cron extension SQL jobs, not OS-level crontab.
plainWords: Move some Oracle databases to managed PostgreSQL, keep others on premises, and use PostgreSQL extensions for maps, scheduled database jobs, and live queries to the remaining Oracle databases.
keyPoints: RDS PostgreSQL extensions: PostGIS spatial, pg_cron SQL scheduling, oracle_fdw foreign Oracle tables. Direct Connect is connectivity only. SCT/DMS handles heterogeneous Oracle->PostgreSQL conversion and data transfer. RDS does not grant host OS crontab access. oracle_fdw requires server, user mapping, foreign table and network reachability.
sourceWarning: Exact third-party practice question found, answer D matches (PracticeCF Q36 No1508; CertEnsure Q6). SOURCE IMPRECISION: 'PostgreSQL native spatial' requires PostGIS extension; 'Run cron jobs on DB instance' means pg_cron database extension, NOT OS crontab; Direct Connect alone does not implement foreign tables—oracle_fdw and network/security configuration are necessary. Answer D valid if these implicit configuration steps are supplied. Original text preserved.

defects: Foreign-table support requires oracle_fdw, not Direct Connect alone
RDS cannot run OS cron; use pg_cron
PostGIS is an extension, not built-in native spatial feature

stem: A company has developed a web application. The company is hosting the application on a group of Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The company wants to improve the security posture of the application and plans to use AWS WAF web ACLs. The solution must not adversely affect legitimate traffic to the application. How should a solutions architect configure the web ACLs to meet these requirements?

options.text: Set the action of the web ACL rules to Count. Enable AWS WAF logging Analyze the requests for false positives Modify the rules to avoid any false positive Over time change the action of the web ACL rules from Count to Block.

Use only rate-based rules in the web ACLs. and set the throttle limit as high as possible Temporarily block all requests that exceed the limit. Define nested rules to narrow the scope of the rate tracking.

Set the action o' the web ACL rules to Block. Use only AWS managed rule groups in the web ACLs Evaluate the rule groups by using Amazon CloudWatch metrics with AWS WAF sampled requests or AWS WAF logs.

Use only custom rule groups in the web ACLs. and set the action to Allow Enable AWS WAF logging Analyze the requests tor false positives Modify the rules to avoid any false positive Over time, change the action of the web ACL rules from Allow to Block.

stem: A company is migrating internal business applications to Amazon EC2 and Amazon RDS in a VPC. The migration requires connecting the cloud-based applications to the on-premises internal network. The company wants to set up an AWS 5ite-to-5ite VPN connection. The company has created two separate customer gateways. The gateways are configured for static routing and have been assigned distinct public IP addresses. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Create one virtual private gateway. Associate the virtual private gateway with the VPC. Enable route propagation for the virtual private gateway in all VPC route tables. Create two Site-to-Slte VPN connections with two tunnels for each connection. Configure the Site-to- Slte VPN connections to use the virtual private gateway and to use separate customer gateways.

Create one customer gateway. Associate the customer gateway with the VPC. Enable route propagation for the customer gateway in all VPC route tables. Create two Site-to-Site VPN connections with two tunnels for each connection. Configure the Site-to-Site VPN connections to use the customer gateway.

Create two virtual private gateways. Associate the virtual private gateways with the VPC. Enable route propagation for both customer gateways in all VPC route tables. Create two Site-to-Site VPN connections with two tunnels for each connection. Configure the Site- to-Site VPN connections to use separate virtual private gateways and separate customer gateways.

Create two virtual private gateways. Associate the virtual private gateways with the VPC. Enable route propagation for both customer gateways in all VPC route tables. Create four Site-to-Site VPN connections with one tunnel for each connection. Configure the Site- to-Site VPN connections into groups of two. Configure each group to connect to separate customer gateways and separate virtual private gateways.

explanation: Verified answer A: attach one virtual private gateway to the VPC; create two AWS Site-to-Site VPN connections, each to a separate existing customer gateway with distinct public IP. Each VPN connection has two tunnels. For static routing, define on-premises destination CIDRs as VPN static routes and enable virtual private gateway route propagation on relevant VPC route tables. AWS: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpn/latest/s2svpn/vpn-redundant-connection.html and https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpn/latest/s2svpn/vpn-edit-static-routes.html
wrongOptionsExplanation: A CORRECT: one VPC-associated virtual private gateway, two VPN connections to separate customer gateways, two tunnels each; configure static remote CIDRs. B INCORRECT: customer gateway is on premises, cannot attach to VPC or propagate routes as VGW. C INCORRECT: two virtual private gateways cannot both attach to same VPC; propagation is not configured for customer gateways. D INCORRECT: same invalid dual-VGW topology; VPN connections have two tunnels, not one.
plainWords: Use one AWS-side VPN gateway connected to both on-premises VPN devices, with two tunnels for each VPN connection.
keyPoints: Virtual private gateway = AWS VPC side; customer gateway = on-premises side. Two Site-to-Site VPN connections to two customer gateways provide four tunnels. Static routing requires remote CIDRs on VPN connections; propagate only to relevant VPC route tables. VGW does not provide ECMP.
sourceWarning: Original question contains OCR errors ('5ite-to-5ite', 'Site-to-Slte'). Source A is AWS-supported but 'all VPC route tables' propagation is overbroad; static VPN remote CIDR configuration omitted. No exact third-party practice-question match verified.

defects: Site-to-Site OCR typos
All route tables propagation overbroad
Static VPN routes not specified

stem: A company wants to migrate an Amazon Aurora MySQL DB cluster from an existing AWS account to a new AWS account in the same AWS Region. Both accounts are members of the same organization in AWS Organizations. The company must minimize database service interruption before the company performs DNS cutover to the new database. Which migration strategy will meet this requirement?

options.text: Take a snapshot of the existing Aurora database. Share the snapshot with the new AWS account. Create an Aurora DB cluster in the new account from the snapshot.
Create an Aurora DB cluster in the new AWS account. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to migrate data between the two Aurora DB clusters.
Use AWS Backup to share an Aurora database backup from the existing AWS account to the new AWS account. Create an Aurora DB cluster in the new AWS account from the snapshot.
Create an Aurora DB cluster in the new AWS account. Use AWS Application Migration Service to migrate data between the two Aurora DB clusters.

explanation: ANSWER B VERIFIED: provision Aurora MySQL target cluster in second account, establish cross-account network connectivity, configure AWS DMS full-load plus CDC to copy data and continuously apply source changes. Monitor replication lag, briefly stop source writes, allow CDC to catch up, validate target and perform DNS cutover. AWS DMS MySQL CDC requires row-based binlogs and appropriate privileges; DMS does not guarantee zero latency and does not replicate all schema objects. AWS documentation https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/userguide/CHAP_Task.CDC.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/userguide/CHAP_Source.MySQL.html ; https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/database/perform-cross-account-amazon-aurora-mysql-migration-with-minimal-downtime/ . Exact independent exam question + B answer: https://www.p2pexams.com/free-questions/amazon-sap-c02-dumps-by-holden-24-05-2024-12qa-certsdeals.pdf
wrongOptionsExplanation: A: Cross-account manual Aurora snapshot sharing/restoration is valid for initial data copy, but does not capture subsequent writes, so alone cannot minimize interruption at final DNS cutover. B: CORRECT: DMS full load and CDC keeps destination nearly current while source serves traffic; pause writes and catch up before cutover. C: AWS Backup cross-account sharing/restoration can restore a point-in-time copy but no continuous changes are replicated by this option; AWS Organizations membership enables sharing eligibility but not live replication. D: AWS Application Migration Service is for server lift-and-shift, not Aurora DB-to-DB logical replication.
plainWords: Copy the database to the new AWS account while the original keeps running, replicate every subsequent change with AWS DMS, and switch the application's DNS after the copies have caught up.
keyPoints: AWS DMS full-load + CDC minimizes migration downtime; MySQL row-based binary logs and permissions are required; DMS CDC is asynchronous, no zero-lag guarantee. Cross-account network path/security groups needed. Snapshots alone are point-in-time; AWS Backup cross-account backup is not continuous database replication. AWS blog also recommends snapshot or Aurora clone initial load plus CDC/native binlog replication for some homogeneous migrations.
sourceWarning: SOURCE VARIANT CONFLICT (2026-10-29): The repository and single-answer copies (ExamsVCE, P2PExams) key B; other external versions of this exact stem explicitly say '(Choose two)' and key A+B (ExamTopics reproduction / exam-tests.com). Therefore the single-answer classification is disputed and the 'original text preserved' assertion cannot be established across versions. For THIS four-option single-answer variant B is best: configure cross-account network, DMS full-load plus CDC or snapshot restore followed by CDC to minimize downtime. A alone is a valid initial copy but doesn't replicate later writes. AWS cross-account Aurora guidance explicitly combines snapshot and replication, making A+B logical in a choose-two variant. DMS CDC is asynchronous and doesn't guarantee zero downtime. See https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/userguide/CHAP_Task.CDC.html ; https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/database/perform-cross-account-amazon-aurora-mysql-migration-with-minimal-downtime/ ; https://www.examsvce.com/sap-c02/a-company-wants-to-migrate-an-amazon-question-answer.html ; https://www.exam-tests.com/SAP-C02-exam/Amazon.SAP-C02.v2026-06-29.q712.html?p=2 . FLAG FOR MANUAL ORIGINAL-PDF PROMPT VERIFICATION.

defects: B omits explicit CDC setup and prerequisites
DMS does not guarantee zero replication lag
Conflicting original prompt cardinality: exact stem also published as Choose two, answer A+B
A (snapshot share and restore) is a legitimate initial step when paired with replication; alone insufficient for minimal interruption
review.notes: The technical single-answer B is AWS-supported; flag conflicting two-answer version A+B. Preserve source version until authoritative original exam prompt can be verified.

stem: A company uses a software package for surveys. During surveys, data is uploaded from a field operator's device to an Amazon S3 bucket. A custom application that runs on several Amazon EC2 instances polls the S3 bucket for new data. When new data is available, the software processes the data. The data uploads are infrequent. The processing software can take up to 25 minutes to analyze each data upload. The company wants to optimize the application workflow to process the S3 data. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Modify the application to accept new S3 object keys as inputs. Containerize the application. Deploy the container to an Amazon ECS cluster that uses the AWS Fargate launch type. Configure S3 bucket notifications to send events to Amazon EventBridge when new objects are uploaded. Create an EventBridge rule that invokes an ECS task to run the application when a new S3 object event occurs.

Modify the application to accept new S3 object keys as inputs. Containerize the application. Deploy the container image to AWS Lambda functions. Create a new AWS Step Functions state machine to invoke the Lambda functions. Configure the state machine with a Task state that calls the Lambda functions. Set the Task state's Timeout property to 30 minutes.

Modify the application to accept new S3 object keys as inputs. Move the application from EC2 instances to Amazon ECS by using the EC2 capacity provider. Create an AWS Glue crawler to check the S3 bucket and invoke the application. Configure the application to process the data when the data is uploaded to Amazon S3.

Modify the application to use HTTP to poll new S3 object keys that reference data to process. Containerize the application. Deploy the container image to AWS Lambda functions. Configure S3 bucket notifications to send events to Amazon EventBridge when new objects are uploaded. Create an EventBridge rule that invokes the Lambda functions to post the new objects to HTTP endpoints by using fan-out.

stem: A company stores all its infrastructure code in a central Git repository that is hosted on GitHub Enterprise. The company wants to implement a process that submits every infrastructure update by using a pull request. Each pull request must automatically receive an AWS CloudFormation change set. After the pull request is approved, CloudFormation must apply the updates directly. The process must not require custom pipelines or manual template processing. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Use CloudFormation to invoke an AWS CodePipeline action. Configure the CodePipeline action to validate the template and publish the validation results as pull request comments.

Use CloudFormation Git sync to link CloudFormation with the repository. Configure automatic change set creation for pull request updates. Configure CloudFormation to post the change set summary and apply the update when the pull request is approved and merged.

Use CloudFormation drift detection. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that reacts to pull request updates. Configure the EventBridge rule to produce drift comparison results and send the results as comments before the stack is updated.
Use CloudFormation Lambda Hooks. Configure Lambda Hooks to evaluate the updated template and write the planned changes into the pull request when a stack update is requested.

stem: A company is planning a migration from an on-premises data center to the AWS cloud. The company plans to use multiple AWS accounts that are managed in an organization in AWS organizations. The company will cost a small number of accounts initially and will add accounts as needed. A solution architect must design a solution that turns on AWS accounts. What is the MOST operationally efficient solution that meets these requirements.

options.text: Create an AWS Lambda function that creates a new cloudTrail trail in all AWS account in the organization. Invoke the Lambda function dally by using a scheduled action in Amazon EventBridge.
Create a new CloudTrail trail in the organizations management account. Configure the trail to log all events for all AYYS accounts in the organization.
Create a new CloudTrail trail in all AWS accounts in the organization. Create new trails whenever a new account is created.
Create an AWS systems Manager Automaton runbook that creates a cloud trail in all AWS accounts in the organization. Invoke the automation by using Systems Manager State Manager.

explanation: B VERIFIED. Create a CloudTrail organization trail in the AWS Organizations management account (or via a delegated administrator). The trail applies to all existing member accounts and automatically to newly added accounts, avoiding custom automation and account-by-account maintenance. AWS: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/creating-trail-organization.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/services-that-can-integrate-cloudtrail.html
wrongOptionsExplanation: A: Lambda with daily EventBridge schedule adds code, maintenance and possible logging gaps. B: Correct; centrally managed organization trail propagates automatically. C: Per-account trails require ongoing manual provisioning and management. D: Systems Manager Automation/State Manager is unnecessary custom orchestration for native CloudTrail organization-wide functionality.
plainWords: Turn on CloudTrail once for the whole AWS Organization, including new accounts automatically.
keyPoints: CloudTrail organization trail; AWS Organizations all-features requirement; management or delegated administrator; automatic coverage of new accounts; member accounts cannot modify organization trail; verify event selectors, Region coverage, S3 permissions and KMS configuration.
sourceWarning: Original stem and options contain transcription defects ('will cost' likely 'will create'; 'turns on AWS accounts' likely 'turns on CloudTrail for AWS accounts'; 'AYYS', 'dally', 'Automaton'). Preserve original text, mark corrected interpretation separately. Exact matching external single-answer copies found; no Choose TWO/THREE conflict in searched sources. External sites may duplicate the same erroneous transcription; not independent technical authority.

defects: Malformed question stem and multiple typographical errors
External practice sites appear to replicate same malformed wording
review.notes: B confirmed by AWS organization-trail auto-enrollment behavior; no multi-answer variant found in checked sources.

stem: A solutions architect is importing a VM from an on-premises environment by using the Amazon EC2 VM Import feature. The imported instance has a public IP and runs in a public subnet in a VPC. However, the instance doesnot appearin the AWS Systems Manager (SSM) console as a managed instance. Which combination of steps should the architect take to resolve the issue? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Verify that Systems Manager Agent is installed on the instance and is running.
Verify that the instance is assigned an appropriate IAM role for Systems Manager.
Verify the existence of a VPC endpoint on the VPC.
Verify that the AWS Application Discovery Agent is configured.
Verify the correct configuration of service-linked roles for Systems Manager.

stem: A company is using GitHub Actions to run a CI/CD pipeline that accesses resources on AWS. The company has an IAM user that uses a secret key in the pipeline to authenticate to AWS. An existing IAM role with an attached policy grants the required permissions to deploy resources. The company's security team implements a new requirement that pipelines can no longer use long-lived secret keys. A solutions architect must replace the secret key with a short- lived solution. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Create an IAM SAML 2.0 identity provider (IdP) in IAM. Create a new IAM role with the appropriate trust policy that allows the sts:AssumeRole API call. Attach the existing IAM policy to the new IAM role. Update GitHub to use SAML authentication for the pipeline.

Create an IAM OpenID Connect (OIDC) identity provider (IdP) in IAM. Create a new IAM role with the appropriate trust policy that allows the sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity API call from the GitHub OIDC IdP. Update GitHub to assume the role for the pipeline.

Create an Amazon Cognito identity pool. Configure the authentication provider to use GitHub. Create a new IAM role with the appropriate trust policy that allows the sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity API call from the GitHub authentication provider. Configure the pipeline to use Cognito as its authentication provider.

Create a trust anchor to AWS Private CA. Generate a client certificate to use with AWS IAM Roles Anywhere. Create a new IAM role with the appropriate trust policy that allows the sts:AssumeRole API call. Attach the existing IAM policy to the new IAM role. Configure the pipeline to use the credential helper tool and to reference the client certificate public key to assume the new IAM role.

stem: A large mobile gaming company has successfully migrated all of its on-premises infrastructure tothe AWS Cloud. A solutions architect is reviewing the environment to ensure that it was built according to the design and that it is running in alignment with the Well-Architected Framework. While reviewing previous monthly costs in Cost Explorer, the solutions architect notices that the creation and subsequent termination of several large instance types account for a high proportion of the costs. The solutions architect finds out that the company's developers are launching new Amazon EC2 instances as part of their testing and that the developers are not using the appropriate instance types. The solutions architect must implement a control mechanism to limit the instance types that only the developers can launch. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Create a desired-instance-type managed rule in AWS Config. Configure the rule with the instance types that are allowed. Attach the rule to an event to run each time a new EC2 instance is launched.
In the EC2 console, create a launch template that specifies the instance types that are allowed. Assign the launch template to the developers' IAM accounts.
Create a new IAM policy. Specify the instance types that are allowed. Attach the policy to an IAM group that contains the IAM accounts for the developers
Use EC2 Image Builder to create an image pipeline for the developers and assist them in the creation of a golden image.

explanation: C VERIFIED: use an identity-based IAM policy scoped to developers (group or preferably role) that restricts ec2:RunInstances with the ec2:InstanceType condition key. AWS explicitly documents allowing t2.micro/t2.small and denying other types to control cost: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ExamplePolicies_EC2.html . Explicit deny for non-approved instance types on instance/* avoids bypass by other allows; existing launch permissions still needed.
wrongOptionsExplanation: A: AWS Config desired-instance-type detects instance-type compliance after launch, not preventive IAM authorization. B: A launch template alone is not a mandatory security boundary; an IAM policy must require use of an approved template to enforce it. C: Correct; attach a condition-based IAM policy to developer identities (group or roles). D: EC2 Image Builder creates AMIs, not restrictions on instance types.
plainWords: Developers are choosing expensive EC2 sizes. Block launches of unapproved sizes using IAM before the cost occurs.
keyPoints: ec2:RunInstances; ec2:InstanceType; StringEquals allowlist or explicit Deny StringNotEquals; attach to developer IAM group/role; AWS Config detective vs IAM preventive; launch templates not enforced without IAM.
sourceWarning: Source transcription typo 'tothe' and awkward phrase 'limit the instance types that only the developers can launch'; source option C says 'IAM accounts' but IAM groups contain IAM users, not accounts. Preserve original question/options, annotate corrected terminology. Exact external single-answer variants located at ExamsReviews, FreeCram, AllFreeDumps/Scribd; no explicit Choose TWO/THREE variant found in searches, but external copies are not authoritative exam originals.

defects: 'tothe' transcription typo
Option C incorrectly says 'IAM accounts' inside an IAM group; IAM groups contain users
Launch templates can be enforced through IAM, but option B does not describe that control
review.notes: AWS explicit EC2 example verifies IAM ec2:InstanceType condition. External exact-stem copies show single-answer form; no multi-select source found in limited searches.

stem: A company has more than 10.000 sensors that send data to an on-premises Apache Kafka server by using the Message Queuing Telemetry Transport (MQTT) protocol. The on- premises Kafka server transforms the data and then stores the results as objects in an Amazon S3 bucket. Recently, the Kafka server crashed. The company lost sensor data while the server was being restored. A solutions architect must create a new design on AWS that is highly available and scalable to prevent a similar occurrence. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Launch two Amazon EC2 instances to host the Kafka server in an active/standby configuration across two Availability Zones. Create a domain name in Amazon Route 53. Create a Route 53 failover policy. Route the sensors to send the data to the domain name.

Migrate the on-premises Kafka server to Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK). Create a Network Load Balancer (NLB) that points to the Amazon MSK broker Enable NL8 health checks. Route the sensors to send the data to the NLB.
Deploy AWS loT Core, and connect it to an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream. Use an AWS Lambda function to handle data transformation. Route the sensors to send the data to AWS loT Core.
Deploy AWS loT Core, and launch an Amazon EC2 instance to host the Kafka server. Configure AWS loT Core to send the data to the EC2 instance. Route the sensors to send the data to AWS loT Core.

explanation: C VERIFIED. AWS IoT Core ingests MQTT messages from sensors, an IoT rule action sends them to Amazon Data Firehose (formerly Kinesis Data Firehose), Firehose can invoke AWS Lambda to transform records and deliver to S3. AWS reference implementation: https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/iot/ingesting-enriched-iot-data-into-amazon-s3-using-amazon-kinesis-data-firehose/ ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/iot/latest/developerguide/kinesis-firehose-rule-action.html ; https://aws.amazon.com/firehose/faqs/ . Managed ingestion and delivery avoid a single self-managed Kafka server. Configure IoT retry/QoS, monitoring, error handling and raw record backup for resilience; no absolute zero-loss guarantee.
wrongOptionsExplanation: A: Active/standby EC2 plus Route 53 reduces one failure but is self-managed, has DNS/failover and Kafka replication gaps, and does not inherently prevent lost records. B: MSK provides managed Kafka, but a single broker behind NLB is not a proper MQTT-native ingest and S3-transform design; the claim that MSK categorically cannot handle 10,000 devices is unsubstantiated. C: Correct; IoT Core MQTT -> IoT rule -> Firehose -> Lambda transform -> S3. D: One EC2 Kafka server recreates the single-point-of-failure.

stem: A company has a legacy application that runs on multiple .NET Framework components. The components share the same Microsoft SQL Server database and communicate with each other asynchronously by using Microsoft Message Queueing (MSMQ). The company is starting a migration to containerized .NET Core components and wants to refactor the application to run on AWS. The .NET Core components require complex orchestration. The company must have full control over networking and host configuration. The application's database model is strongly relational. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Host the .NET Core components on AWS App Runner. Host the database on Amazon RDS for SQL Server. Use Amazon EventBridge for asynchronous messaging.

Host the .NET Core components on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with the AWS Fargate launch type. Host the database on Amazon DynamoDB. Use Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) for asynchronous messaging.

Host the .NET Core components on AWS Elastic Beanstalk. Host the database on Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL Serverless v2. Use Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK) for asynchronous messaging.

Host the .NET Core components on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with the Amazon EC2 launch type. Host the database on Amazon Aurora MySQL Serverless v2. Use Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) for asynchronous messaging.

explanation: D VERIFIED as best of supplied options. ECS with EC2 launch type provides managed container orchestration while retaining control of the EC2 host OS, networking, and instance configuration. Aurora MySQL Serverless v2 is relational and automatically scales capacity; Amazon SQS is managed asynchronous queueing suitable for replacing MSMQ patterns. AWS ECS launch types: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/launch_types.html ; Aurora Serverless v2: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-serverless-v2.html ; SQS: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/welcome.html . NOTE: SQL Server to Aurora MySQL is a heterogeneous database migration requiring schema, SQL and application compatibility conversion, not automatic SQL Server engine compatibility.
wrongOptionsExplanation: A: App Runner abstracts the underlying hosts and does not provide full host/network configuration control; RDS SQL Server is relational and EventBridge asynchronous, but host-control requirement fails. B: ECS Fargate does not give full host OS control, and DynamoDB is NoSQL rather than a strongly relational SQL schema; SNS pub/sub does not provide MSMQ-like durable per-consumer queue semantics by itself. C: Elastic Beanstalk is not the best fit for complex container orchestration; Aurora PostgreSQL is relational and MSK is asynchronous streaming but adds Kafka complexity instead of simple queue semantics; EC2 host control can exist under Beanstalk, so do not claim it is categorically impossible. D: ECS EC2 + Aurora MySQL Serverless v2 + SQS satisfies orchestration, host/network control, relational data and async queue requirements.
plainWords: Use ECS on EC2 when you need container orchestration plus control of the machines. Choose a relational Aurora database and SQS queues for asynchronous component communication.
keyPoints: ECS EC2 launch type vs Fargate; EC2 host OS and network control; Aurora MySQL Serverless v2 relational; SQS asynchronous durable queues vs SNS pub/sub and MSK streaming; SQL Server-to-MySQL heterogeneous migration and schema conversion.

SQL Server and MySQL are different engines and require heterogeneous schema/code migration. Original stem/options preserved.

Migration requires heterogeneous schema/code conversion and testing

stem: An online retail company hosts its stateful web-based application and MySQL database in an on-premises data center on a single server. The company wants to increase its customer base by conducting more marketing campaigns and promotions. In preparation, the company wants to migrate its application and database to AWS to increase the reliability of its architecture. Which solution should provide the HIGHEST level of reliability?

options.text: Migrate the database to an Amazon RDS MySQL Multi-AZ DB instance. Deploy the application in an Auto Scaling group on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. Store sessions in Amazon Neptune.

Migrate the database to Amazon Aurora MySQL. Deploy the application in an Auto Scaling group on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. Store sessions in an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis replication group.

Migrate the database to Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility). Deploy the application in an Auto Scaling group on Amazon EC2 instances behind a Network Load Balancer. Store sessions in Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose.

Migrate the database to an Amazon RDS MariaDB Multi-AZ DB instance. Deploy the application in an Auto Scaling group on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. Store sessions in Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached.

explanation: B VERIFIED. Amazon Aurora MySQL retains MySQL compatibility with six storage copies across three AZs; an ALB with an EC2 Auto Scaling group distributes requests across multiple web instances; an ElastiCache for Redis OSS replication group allows shared stateful sessions with replication and (when Multi-AZ/automatic failover is configured) failover. AWS: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Concepts.AuroraHighAvailability.html and https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/dg/AutoFailover.html . For true high availability deploy Aurora readers in distinct AZs and enable Redis Multi-AZ/auto failover; those configurations are not expressly specified in B.
wrongOptionsExplanation: A: RDS MySQL Multi-AZ and ALB/ASG are resilient, but Amazon Neptune is a graph database and unsuitable for session storage. B: Correct; Aurora MySQL, ALB/ASG and replicated Redis provide the most suitable resilient combination. C: DocumentDB is document-oriented rather than MySQL-relational; Firehose is not a session store. D: RDS MariaDB Multi-AZ and ALB/ASG are plausible, but ElastiCache Memcached has no native multi-node replication or automatic failover, making it less reliable for sessions than Redis replication.
plainWords: Run multiple web servers behind an ALB, keep MySQL data in Aurora, and share login/session state in a replicated Redis cache.
keyPoints: Aurora MySQL 6 copies across 3 AZs; Aurora readers for compute failover; ALB + EC2 Auto Scaling; externalize web session state; ElastiCache Redis replication group Multi-AZ automatic failover; Memcached lacks native replication; Neptune graph DB; Firehose streaming delivery.
sourceWarning: Exact single-choice answer B on FreeCram and DumpsTech; Actual4Exams rearranges options but picks same Aurora/Redis design (C in that source). No Choose TWO/THREE variant found in checked sources. Some third-party PDFs corrupt formatting by splitting compound options into separate lettered fragments; these are not genuine multi-answer variants. Technical caveat: option B does not explicitly enable Aurora multi-AZ reader instances or Redis Multi-AZ automatic failover, so highest reliability requires those configuration details.

Option B omits explicit Aurora cross-AZ replicas and Redis Multi-AZ automatic failover configuration
review.notes: Verified B as best choice; external single-answer versions agree on architecture despite shuffled option labels. Do not claim that Aurora six-copy storage alone ensures DB compute HA.

stem: A manufacturing company is building an inspection solution for its factory. The company has IPcameras at the end of each assembly line. The company has used Amazon SageMaker to train a machine learning (ML) model to identify common defects from still images. The company wants to provide local feedback to factory workers when a defect is detected. The company must be able to provide this feedback even if the factory’s internet connectivity is down. The company has a local Linux server that hosts an API that provides local feedback to the workers. How should the company deploy the ML model to meet these requirements?

options.text: Set up an Amazon Kinesis video stream from each IP camera to AWS. Use Amazon EC2 instances to take still images of the streams. Upload the images to an Amazon S3 bucket. Deploy a SageMaker endpoint with the ML model. Invoke an AWS Lambda function to call the inference endpoint when new images are uploaded. Configure the Lambda function to call the local API when a defect is detected.

Deploy AWS IoT Greengrass on the local server. Deploy the ML model to the Greengrass server. Create a Greengrass component to take still images from the cameras and run inference. Configure the component to call the local API when a defect is detected.

Order an AWS Snowball device. Deploy a SageMaker endpoint the ML model and an Amazon EC2 instance on the Snowball device. Take still images from the cameras. Run inference from the EC2 instance. Configure the instance to call the local API when a defect is detected.

Deploy Amazon Monitron devices on each IP camera. Deploy an Amazon Monitron Gateway on premises. Deploy the ML model to the Amazon Monitron devices. Use Amazon Monitron health state alarms to call the local API from an AWS Lambda function when a defect is detected.

explanation: B VERIFIED by AWS. AWS IoT Greengrass V2 deploys custom ML model, runtime and inference components to an on-premises Linux core device, enabling local still-image inference and calls to the local API without internet access once deployed. AWS: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/greengrass/v2/developerguide/perform-machine-learning-inference.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/greengrass/v2/developerguide/machine-learning-components.html . Requires local power, camera/LAN connectivity, downloaded model and dependencies.
wrongOptionsExplanation: A: Cloud Kinesis Video Streams, EC2, S3, SageMaker endpoint and Lambda require internet, violating outage requirement. B: Correct; Greengrass runs local inference and local API integration. C: Snowball is not the simple durable deployment for an existing Linux server and the proposed conventional SageMaker endpoint hosted on Snowball is technically defective. D: Amazon Monitron is condition monitoring for industrial machinery, not custom camera ML inference, and Monitron closed to new customers Oct 31 2024.
plainWords: Put the trained defect-detection model on the factory's Linux server with AWS IoT Greengrass, so it works even without internet.
keyPoints: Greengrass V2 edge ML model/runtime/inference components; SageMaker-trained model artifacts; local camera processing and local API; offline inference after deployment; cloud SageMaker endpoints depend on network; Monitron closed to new customers Oct 31 2024.

Conflicting external ANSWER KEY: Scribd SAP-C02 CSL 09-26-341 marks D for exact same four-choice stem; this is technically wrong versus AWS Greengrass docs and two other exact-match exam sites answering B. No conflicting Choose TWO/THREE variant identified in checked sources. Amazon Monitron unavailable to new customers since Oct 31 2024. Preserve original text and explicitly flag external answer-key defect.

stem: A company wants to establish a dedicated connection between its on-premises infrastructure and AWS. The company is setting up a 1 Gbps AWS Direct Connect connection to its account VPC. The architecture includes a transit gateway and a Direct Connect gateway to connect multiple VPCs and the on-premises infrastructure. The company must connect to VPC resources over a transit VIF by using the Direct Connect connection. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Update the 1 Gbps Direct Connect connection to 10 Gbps.
Advertise the on-premises network prefixes over the transit VIF.
Advertise the VPC prefixes from the Direct Connect gateway to the on-premises network over the transit VIF.
Update the Direct Connect connection's MACsec encryption mode attribute to must encrypt.
Associate a MACsec Connection Key Name-Connectivity Association Key (CKN/CAK) pair with the Direct Connect connection.

explanation: B and C. Bidirectional BGP reachability over the transit VIF requires the on-premises BGP router to advertise on-prem CIDRs to AWS (B) and the Direct Connect gateway to advertise the allowed AWS/VPC prefixes to on premises (C). For a transit gateway association, the Direct Connect gateway allowed-prefix list controls the prefixes AWS originates, which can include VPC CIDRs or aggregates. Transit VIFs are supported at 1 Gbps; MACsec does not replace routing.
wrongOptionsExplanation: A: 1 Gbps is supported for transit VIFs, so upgrading to 10 Gbps is unnecessary. D: MACsec must-encrypt concerns link encryption, not routing; MACsec availability depends on dedicated connection capabilities. E: MACsec CKN/CAK provides encryption keys, not BGP reachability.
plainWords: Both sides must know the way back: tell AWS which IP networks live in your data center, and tell your data center which IP networks live in AWS.
keyPoints: Transit VIF -> Direct Connect gateway -> Transit Gateway -> multiple VPCs. BGP announces on-prem routes to AWS (B) and DX gateway allowed AWS-side prefixes to on-prem (C). A transit VIF supports 1 Gbps; no 10 Gbps requirement. MACsec is optional encryption, not routing. Check TGW route tables and VPC routes. Transit VIF BGP max 100 advertised routes per session (hard quota).
sourceWarning: Original option C typo 'Adverse' corrected to 'Advertise' and original snapshot retained. Stem says 'account VPC' singular while multiple VPCs are intended; topology is otherwise technically valid. Actual configuration also requires Direct Connect gateway association to transit gateway, transit VIF attachment, allowed-prefix list, BGP session, and TGW/VPC routes. External identical variants https://www.freepdfdumps.com/Amazon.SAP-C02.v2025-06-02.q210.html?p=22 and https://www.dumpstech.com/free-amazon-web-services/sap-c02-practice-4.html agree B,C. AWS https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/direct-connect-transit-gateways.html and https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/direct-connect-fix-connectivity-to-vpc

review.notes: Reviewed 674; no exact stem duplicate; related Direct Connect/VIF/TGW questions test different requirements. Two independent external exam mirrors agree B,C; official AWS confirms 1Gbps and bidirectional BGP.

stem: A company implements a containerized application by using Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) and Amazon API Gateway. The application data is stored in Amazon Aurora databases and Amazon DynamoDB databases The company automates infrastructure provisioning by using AWS CloudFormation The company automates application deployment by using AWS CodePipeline. A solutions architect needs to implement a disaster recovery (DR) strategy that meets an RPO of 2 hours and an RTO of 4 hours. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively'?

options.text: Set up an Aurora global database and DynamoDB global tables to replicate the databases to a secondary AWS Region. In the primary Region and in the secondaryRegion, configure an API Gateway API with a Regional Endpoint Implement Amazon CloudFront with origin failover to route traffic to the secondary Region during a DR scenario

Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS). Amazon EventBridge. and AWS Lambda to replicate the Aurora databases to a secondary AWS Region Use DynamoDB Streams EventBridge, and Lambda to replicate the DynamoDB databases to the secondary Region. In the primary Region and in the secondary Region, configure an API Gateway API with a Regional Endpoint Implement Amazon Route 53 failover routing to switch traffic from the primary Region to the secondary Region.

Use AWS Backup to create backups of the Aurora databases and the DynamoDB databases in a secondary AWS Region. In the primary Region and in the secondary Region, configure an API Gateway API with a Regional endpoint. Implement Amazon Route 53 failover routing to switch traffic from the primary Region to the secondary Region

Set up an Aurora global database and DynamoDB global tables to replicate the databases to a secondary AWS Region. In the primary Region and in the secondaryRegion, configure an API Gateway API with a Regional endpoint Implement Amazon Route 53 failover routing to switch traffic from the primary Region to the secondary Region

explanation: C is the best intended cost-effective answer: AWS Backup scheduled cross-Region copies for Aurora and DynamoDB, restore databases in secondary Region, CloudFormation redeploys ECS infrastructure and CodePipeline deploys code, then Route 53 failover to Regional API Gateway. AWS calls backup-and-restore the lowest-cost DR strategy with RPO hours but typical full-stack RTO up to 24 hours; 4-hour RTO is NOT guaranteed and requires timed restore tests, suitably small datasets, appropriate backup schedules/copy completion and infrastructure automation. AWS docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/strategy-database-disaster-recovery/defining.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/disaster-recovery-workloads-on-aws/disaster-recovery-options-in-the-cloud.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-backup/latest/devguide/backup-feature-availability.html .
wrongOptionsExplanation: A: Global Aurora and DynamoDB replication is higher recurring cost; CloudFront origin failover is limited to certain HTTP methods and not a general write-API DR failover mechanism. B: DMS plus DynamoDB Streams, EventBridge and Lambda custom replication is complex and operationally expensive compared with backup/restore. C: Lowest-cost backup/restore candidate, but Route 53 failover alone does not restore databases or deploy ECS; use CloudFormation/CodePipeline runbooks and validate 4-hour RTO. D: Aurora global database and DynamoDB global tables provide stronger RPO/RTO but at higher ongoing cross-Region replication cost than C.
plainWords: For two hours of acceptable data loss and four hours to recover, backups in another Region are cheaper than continuously running global database replicas—but only if tested restoration fits four hours.

explanation: B VERIFIED best choice: Site-to-Site VPN establishes private hybrid connectivity without waiting to provision a new Direct Connect circuit. AWS DMS full load plus ongoing CDC migrates 2 TB existing MySQL rows and captures subsequent changes via row-based binary logs, enabling minimal-downtime cutover to Aurora after lag reaches zero. AWS docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/userguide/CHAP_Task.CDC.html and https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/userguide/CHAP_Source.MySQL.html . plainWords: Use VPN to connect the private data center quickly, and DMS to copy the database while continuously replaying new changes until cutover.
keyPoints: AWS Site-to-Site VPN private connectivity; DMS full load plus CDC; MySQL row-based binlog and retention; Aurora MySQL-compatible target; replication lag validation and write pause at cutover; new Direct Connect provisioning lead time.

The EC2 instances will run in an Auto Scaling group in a dedicated VPC. The company needs to use the security tool to inspect all packets that come in and out of the VPC. This inspection must occur in real time and must not affect the application's performance. A solutions architect must design a target architecture on AWS that is highly available within an AWS Region. Which combination of steps should the solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Deploy the security tool on EC2 instances in a new Auto Scaling group in the existing VPC.
Deploy the web application behind a Network Load Balancer.
Deploy an Application Load Balancer in front of the security tool instances.
Provision a Gateway Load Balancer for each Availability Zone to redirect the traffic to the security tool.
Provision a transit gateway to facilitate communication between VPCs.

explanation: Historical A,D is the intended exam key: A runs compatible security virtual appliances on EC2 instances in a multi-AZ Auto Scaling group; D names Gateway Load Balancer, which transparently distributes flows to appliances for inline bidirectional packet inspection. However D is imprecisely worded: AWS typically deploys a multi-AZ GWLB with a zonal Gateway Load Balancer endpoint per AZ, not a separate GWLB for every AZ. Set VPC ingress/egress routing symmetrically through zonal endpoints.
wrongOptionsExplanation: B: Network Load Balancer distributes TCP/UDP application traffic but cannot alone provide transparent inline inspection of all inbound/outbound VPC packets. C: Application Load Balancer is L7 HTTP(S) routing, not general IP packet inspection. E: Transit Gateway is appropriate for centralized multi-VPC inspection but is unnecessary for the stated single-VPC architecture; it does not substitute for GWLB.
plainWords: Keep using the security tool by running compatible virtual appliances on scalable EC2 servers. Put a Gateway Load Balancer in the packet path so inbound and outbound traffic gets inspected. Use an endpoint in each AZ, not one separate load balancer per AZ.
keyPoints: Historical A,D. Gateway Load Balancer (GWLB) for transparent inline L3/L4 appliance inspection, GENEVE UDP 6081, health checks and scale. Zonal GWLB endpoints (GWLBe) per AZ; configure symmetric VPC ingress/egress route tables. Deploy security appliance ASG across AZs and confirm GENEVE-capable virtual form of legacy product. NLB/ALB not replacements; TGW for centralized multi-VPC inspection only. Packet inspection always adds some latency; 'no performance impact' is unrealistic.
sourceWarning: TECHNICAL DEFECT: D says 'a Gateway Load Balancer for each Availability Zone' whereas AWS best practice is one multi-AZ Gateway Load Balancer with a GWLB endpoint in each AZ. Requirement 'must not affect application's performance' is absolute and technically unrealistic; inspection adds latency. The vendor has no cloud solution; legacy security tool's virtual-appliance/GENEVE compatibility is unproven. Retain historical A,D but mark architecture conditional. stem: A company is migrating a legacy application from an on-premises data center to AWS. The application consists of a single application server and a Microsoft SQL Server database server. Each server is deployed on a VMware VM that consumes 500 TB of data across multiple attached volumes. The Direct Connect connection is not currently in use by other services. Which combination of steps should a solutions architect take to migrate the application with the LEAST amount of downtime? (Choose two.)

options.text: Use an AWS Server Migration Service (AWS SMS) replication job to migrate the database server VM to AWS.
Use VM Import/Export to import the application server VM.
Export the VM images to an AWS Snowball Edge Storage Optimized device.
Use an AWS Server Migration Service (AWS SMS) replication job to migrate the application server VM to AWS.
Use an AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) replication instance to migrate the database to an Amazon RDS DB instance.

explanation: Historical exam answer A,D: recurring AWS SMS snapshot/incremental replication jobs migrate both the SQL Server VMware VM and the application VMware VM while sources continue running; final coordinated cutover after latest replication. SMS is discontinued and not viable in 2026. For a new project, use AWS Transform MGN (formerly AWS Application Migration Service) continuous block-level replication and coordinated test/cutover for both servers. Even historical SMS used periodic snapshots, with >=1-hour replication intervals, so it does not guarantee near-zero RPO.
wrongOptionsExplanation: B: VM Import/Export is a one-time import, without continuous source changes replicated, so app-server cutover downtime/data drift risk is higher. C: Snowball Edge device shipment and offline VM export do not offer continuous low-downtime cutover, and 10 Gbps Direct Connect is available. E: DMS CDC to RDS may minimize SQL database downtime but changes deployment to managed RDS rather than lift-and-shift of the existing SQL VM; paired with a VM import it still fails to offer the intended synchronized VM cutover.
plainWords: Historically copy both VMs repeatedly, then switch traffic when the latest copies are ready. Today use AWS Transform MGN to replicate each VM continuously, test, and cut over the app and SQL Server together.
keyPoints: Historical A,D = SMS incremental snapshot replication of BOTH VMware VMs; retired March 2022. 2026 = AWS Transform MGN (formerly Application Migration Service, renamed June 2026), continuous block-level replication, test launch, coordinated cutover. 10 Gbps theoretical 500 TB initial transfer ~4.6 days at line rate (decimal); initial sync duration != application downtime. DMS is database-only and RDS modernization, not full VM rehost. Check 500 TB disk/volume feasibility, per-server EBS and MGN limits, SQL consistency, Direct Connect routing, licensing.
sourceWarning: SEVERELY OUTDATED: Both keyed options A,D use AWS SMS, discontinued March 31 2022. New deployments should use AWS Transform MGN, rebranded from AWS Application Migration Service in June 2026. 500 TB 'each server' vs 'VM that consumes' ambiguity; must validate MGN/EBS source-disk constraints and SQL Server consistency. Historical SMS periodic snapshots may produce >=1h RPO and do not guarantee minimum downtime. External variants PassTest Q153 reorders options; FreePDFDumps Q99 reorders; Scribd Q311 A,D; Examlex Q297 A,D. AWS https://aws.amazon.com/application-migration-service/ ; https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/mt/accelerate-your-migration-with-aws-application-migration-service/

This update process also requires frequent changes to the custom application to invoke the new function version ARN. These changes cause interruptions for users. options.text: Directly modify the environment variables of the published Lambda function version. Use the SLATEST version to test image processing parameters.
Create an Amazon DynamoDB table to store the image processing parameters. Modify the Lambda function to retrieve the image processing parameters from the DynamoDB table.
Directly code the image processing parameters within the Lambda function and remove the environment variables. Publish a new function version when the company updates the parameters.
Create a Lambda function alias. Modify the client application to use the function alias ARN. Reconfigure the Lambda alias to point to new versions of the function when the company finishes testing.

stem: A company is serving files to its customers through an SFTP server that is accessible over the internet The SFTP server is running on a single Amazon EC2 instance with an Elastic IP address attached Customers connect to the SFTP server through its Elastic IP address and use SSH for authentication The EC2 instance also has an attached security group that allows access from all customer IP addresses. A solutions architect must implement a solution to improve availability minimize the complexity of infrastructure management and minimize the disruption to customers who access files. The solution must not change the way customers connect Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Disassociate the Elastic IP address from the EC2 instance Create an Amazon S3 bucket to be used for SFTP file hosting Create an AWS Transfer Family server. Configure the Transfer Family server with a publicly accessible endpoint Associate the SFTP Elastic IP address with the new endpoint. Point the Transfer Family server to the S3 bucket Sync all files from the SFTP server to the S3 bucket.

Disassociate the Elastic IP address from the EC2 instance Create an Amazon S3 bucket to be used for SFTP file hosting Create an AWS Transfer Family Server Configure the Transfer Family server with a VPC-hosted, internet-facing endpoint Associate the SFTP Elastic IP address with the new endpoint Attach the security group with customer IP addresses to the new endpoint Point the Transfer Family server to the S3 bucket. Sync all files from the SFTP server to the S3 bucket.

Disassociate the Elastic IP address from the EC2 instance. Create a new Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system to be used for SFTP file hosting. Create an AWS Fargate task definition to run an SFTP server Specify the EFS file system as a mount in the task definition Create a Fargate service by using the task definition, and place a Network Load Balancer (NLB) in front of the service. When configuring the service, attach the security group with customer IP addresses to the tasks that run the SFTP server Associate the Elastic IP address with the NLB Sync all files from the SFTP server to the S3 bucket.

Disassociate the Elastic IP address from the EC2 instance. Create a multi-attach Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume to be used for SFTP file hosting. Create a Network Load Balancer (NLB) with the Elastic IP address attached. Create an Auto Scaling group with EC2 instances that run an SFTP server. Define in the Auto Scaling group that instances that are launched should attach the new multi-attach EBS volume Configure the Auto Scaling group to automatically add instances behind the NLB. configure the Auto Scaling group to use the security group that allows customer IP addresses for the EC2 instances that the Auto Scaling group launches Sync all files from the SFTP server to the new multi-attach EBS volume.

stem: A company uses Amazon S3 to store files and images in a variety of storage classes. The company's S3 costs have increased substantially during the past year.
