stem: A company has an application that uses AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) to encrypt and decrypt data. The application stores data in an Amazon S3 bucket in an AWS Region. Company security policies require that the data is encryptedbeforebeing uploaded to S3, and decryptedwhen read. The S3 bucket isreplicated to other AWS Regions. A solutions architect must design a solution so that the application canencrypt and decrypt data across Regionsusingthe same key.

options.text: Create a KMS multi-Region primary key. Use it to create KMS multi-Region replica keys in each Region. Update application code to use the replica key in each Region.
Create a new customer-managed KMS key in each additional Region. Update application code to use the key in each Region.
Use AWS Private CA to issue TLS certificates and replicate them with AWS RAM.
Export the KMS key material to Systems Manager Parameter Store in each Region. Update the app to use those.

stem: A media storage application uploads user photos to Amazon S3 for processing by AWS Lambda functions. Application state is stored in Amazon DynamoOB tables. Users are reporting that some uploaded photos are not being processed properly. The application developers trace the logs and find that Lambda is experiencing photo processing issues when thousands of users upload photos simultaneously. The issues are the result of Lambda concurrency limits and the performance of DynamoDB when data is saved. Which combination of actions should a solutions architect take to increase the performance and reliability of the application? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Evaluate and adjust the RCUs for the DynamoDB tables.
Evaluate and adjust the WCUs for the DynamoDB tables.
Add an Amazon ElastiCache layer to increase the performance of Lambda functions.
Add an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue and reprocessing logic between Amazon S3 and the Lambda functions.
Use S3 Transfer Acceleration to provide lower latency to users.

stem: A company is planning to migrate its on-premises VMware cluster of 120 VMS to AWS. The VMS have many different operating systems and many custom software packages installed. The company also has an on-premises NFS server that is 10 TB in size. The company has set up a 10 GbpsAWS Direct Connect connection to AWS for the migration Which solution will complete the migration to AWS in the LEAST amount of time?

options.text: Export the on-premises VMS and copy them to an Amazon S3 bucket. Use VM Import/Export to create AMIS from the VM images that are stored in Amazon S3.Order an AWS Snowball Edge device. Copy the NFS server data to the device. Restore the NFS server data to an Amazon EC2 instance that has NFS configured.

Configure AWS Application Migration Service with a connection to the VMware cluster. Create a replication job for the VMS. Create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Configure AWS DataSync to copy the NFS server data to the EFS file system over the Direct Connect connection.

Recreate the VMS on AWS as Amazon EC2 instances. Install all the required software packages. Create an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system. Configure AWS DataSync to copy the NFS server data to the FSx for Lustre file system over the Direct Connect connection.

Order two AWS Snowball Edge devices. Copy the VMS and the NFS server data to the devices. Run VM Import/Export after the data from the devices isloaded to an Amazon S3 bucket. Create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Copy the NFS server data from Amazon S3 to the EFS file system.

explanation: B is correct. AWS Application Migration Service (MGN) performs automated lift-and-shift block-level replication and launch of supported VMware virtual machines as EC2 instances; AWS DataSync migrates the separate 10 TB on-premises NFS share to managed Amazon EFS over the existing 10 Gbps Direct Connect path. This minimizes manual rebuilding and physical device shipping. MGN does not replicate shared NFS NAS mounts; DataSync handles that independently. Check OS compatibility and MGN agentless/agent-based VMware prerequisites.
wrongOptionsExplanation: A: VM Import/Export plus Snowball requires manual exports, device ordering, shipping, and restoring a self-managed NFS server despite available Direct Connect. B: Correct; AWS MGN rehosts supported VMs while DataSync copies NFS to EFS online. C: Manually recreating 120 EC2 VMs and reinstalling packages is slower; FSx for Lustre is not the natural general NFS migration target. D: Two Snowball devices, VM Import/Export, and S3-to-EFS staging add avoidable physical logistics and copying.
plainWords: Use MGN to migrate the 120 VMware servers and DataSync to copy the 10 TB NFS share into EFS through Direct Connect.
keyPoints: MGN = VM rehosting; DataSync = NFS share migration; EFS = managed NFS destination; Direct Connect = existing high-bandwidth network; Snowball = offline shipping; MGN does not copy shared NFS mounts.
sourceWarning: Original question and options have formatting typos (VMS, 10 GbpsAWS, AMIS, on- premises, isloaded). stem: A company recently acquired several other companies. Each company has a separate AWS account with a different billing and reporting method. The acquiring company has consolidated all the accounts into one organization in AWS Organizations. However, the acquiring company has found it difficult to generate a cost report that contains meaningful groups for all the teams. The acquiring company’s finance team needs a solution to report on costs for all the companies through a self-managed application. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Create an AWS Cost and Usage Report for the organization. Define tags and cost categories in the report. Create a table in Amazon Athena. Create an Amazon QuickSight dataset based on the Athena table. Share the dataset with the finance team.

Create an AWS Cost and Usage Report for the organization. Define tags and cost categories in the report. Create a specialized template in AWS Cost Explorer that the finance department will use to build reports.
Create an Amazon QuickSight dataset that receives spending information from the AWS Price List Query API. Share the dataset with the finance team.
Use the AWS Price List Query API to collect account spending information. Create a specialized template in AWS Cost Explorer that the finance department will use to build reports.

stem: A company is running a critical application that uses an Amazon RDS for MySQL database to store data. The RDS DB instance is deployed in Multi-AZ mode. A recent RDS database failover test caused a 40-second outage to the application A solutions architect needs to design a solution to reduce the outage time to less than 20 seconds. Which combination of steps should the solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Select THREE.)

options.text: Use Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached in front of the database
Use Amazon ElastiCache for Redis in front of the database.
Use RDS Proxy in front of the database
Migrate the database to Amazon Aurora MySQL
Create an Amazon Aurora Replica
Create an RDS for MySQL read replica

explanation: C,D,E is the historically intended key: RDS Proxy reduces client DNS/reconnection delay, Aurora MySQL offers faster cluster failover, and an Aurora Replica in another AZ supplies a promotable writer candidate. AWS documents RDS MySQL Multi-AZ typical failover 60–120 seconds and Aurora typical failover about 30 seconds; RDS Proxy can reduce Aurora failover delays by up to 66%. The strict <20-second requirement is NOT guaranteed and must be load-tested.
wrongOptionsExplanation: A Memcached can offload reads but cannot shorten MySQL writer failover or restore writes. B Redis similarly provides caching but does not fix underlying writer failover. C RDS Proxy maintains stable client endpoint, bypasses DNS caches, redirects to new writer; in-flight transactions may fail. D Aurora MySQL supports rapid replica promotion with fault-tolerant shared storage. E Aurora Replica in another AZ is an automatic failover target; without it, recovery is slower. F standard RDS MySQL read replica is asynchronously replicated and requires promotion rather than automatically becoming the Multi-AZ writer.
plainWords: The app loses database access for 40 seconds during a MySQL failover. Move to Aurora with a promotable replica and put RDS Proxy between the application and database to reduce recovery and reconnection delays.
keyPoints: RDS Multi-AZ standby != conventional read replica != Aurora Replica. RDS Proxy hides DNS change and manages connections, but does not guarantee zero downtime or save in-flight transactions. Aurora with cross-AZ replica provides automated failover target. AWS Aurora typical failover ~30s; proxy can reduce delays up to 66%, not guaranteed under 20s. Test actual application outage and retries.
sourceWarning: Strict 'less than 20 seconds' is not guaranteed by C,D,E; AWS provides typical and up-to improvement metrics, not hard SLO. External dumpscollection variant reports conflicting A,B,F, unsupported by failover mechanics. Original punctuation error 'application A' retained in original snapshot.

stem: A company runs a Java application that has complex dependencies on VMs that are in the company's data center. The application is stable. but the company wants to modernize the technology stack. The company wants to migrate the application to AWS and minimize the administrative overhead to maintain the servers. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST code changes?

options.text: Migrate the application to Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) on AWS Fargate by using AWS App2Container. Store container images in Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR). Grant the ECS task execution role permission 10 access the ECR image repository. Configure Amazon ECS to use an Application Load Balancer (ALB). Use the ALB to interact with the application.
Migrate the application code to a container that runs in AWS Lambda. Build an Amazon API Gateway REST API with Lambda integration. Use API Gateway to interact with the application.

Migrate the application to Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) on EKS managed node groups by using AWS App2Container. Store container images in Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR). Give the EKS nodes permission to access the ECR image repository. Use Amazon API Gateway to interact with the application.
Migrate the application code to a container that runs in AWS Lambda. Configure Lambda to use an Application Load Balancer (ALB). Use the ALB to interact with the application.

explanation: Correct A. AWS App2Container inventories and analyzes supported Java applications, creates Docker containers, and generates deployment configurations. AWS documentation explicitly supports Java on Linux for ECS Fargate and makes Fargate the default Java ECS target. ECR hosts images; the ECS task execution role authorizes ECR pulls; ALB routes web requests. Fargate removes EC2 host management, unlike EKS managed node groups. External exact-stem SAP-C02 variants are single-answer and support A.
wrongOptionsExplanation: A: Correct, assuming the source Java app meets App2Container supported-platform prerequisites. B: Lambda container images still require adapting the Java server to Lambda's event-driven runtime and execution constraints. C: App2Container can target EKS, but EKS managed node groups require EC2 node lifecycle administration and API Gateway integration adds complexity. D: ALB supports Lambda targets but Lambda compatibility and potential code changes remain; not the least effort.
plainWords: Package the existing supported Java app with App2Container, push its image to ECR, and run it on ECS Fargate behind an ALB.
keyPoints: App2Container supports Java Linux to ECS Fargate; Fargate avoids managing servers; ECS task execution role pulls from ECR; EKS managed nodes retain node management; Lambda container image does not automatically adapt a traditional server.
sourceWarning: Original stem says 'stable. but' and option A says 'permission 10' instead of 'permission to'. Java source OS, server/framework and dependencies are unspecified; App2Container support must be checked. Option C's API Gateway integration is not impossible but is unnecessary complexity. No confirmed conflicting Choose TWO/THREE version found. Current AWS App2Container docs still describe Java-on-Linux ECS Fargate support; verify tool availability and prerequisites for deployment.

review.notes: Domain 4 68/139, Q326 Select THREE skipped; AWS docs independently validate Java Linux App2Container to ECS Fargate; external exact-stem single-answer copies found; typo and compatibility caveats flagged.

stem: A company built an ecommerce website on AWS using a three-tier web architecture. The application is Java-based and composed of an Amazon CloudFront distribution, an Apache web server layer of Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group, and a backend Amazon Aurora MySQL database. Last month, during a promotional sales event, users reported errors and timeouts while adding items to their shopping carts. The operations team recovered the logs created by the web servers and reviewed Aurora DB cluster performance metrics. Some of the web servers were terminated before logs could be collected and the Aurora metrics were not sufficient for query performance analysis. Which combination of steps must the solutions architect take to improve application performance visibility during peak traffic events? (Choose three.)

options.text: Configure the Aurora MySQL DB cluster to publish slow query and error logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs.
Implement the AWS X-Ray SDK to trace incoming HTTP requests on the EC2 instances and implement tracing of SQL queries with the X-Ray SDK for Java.
Configure the Aurora MySQL DB cluster to stream slow query and error logs to Amazon Kinesis
Install and configure an Amazon CloudWatch Logs agent on the EC2 instances to send the Apache logs to CloudWatch Logs.
Enable and configure AWS CloudTrail to collect and analyze application activity from Amazon EC2 and Aurora.
Enable Aurora MySQL DB cluster performance benchmarking and publish the stream to AWS X-Ray.

stem: A company is currently in the design phase of an application that will need an RPO of less than 5 minutes and an RTO of less than 10 minutes. The solutions architecture team is forecasting that the database will store approximately 10 TB of data. As part of the design, they are looking for a database solution that will provide the company with the ability to fail over to a secondary Region. Which solution will meet these business requirements at the LOWEST cost?

options.text: Deploy an Amazon Aurora DB cluster and take snapshots of the cluster every 5 minutes. Once a snapshot is complete, copy the snapshot to a secondary Region to serve as a backup in the event of a failure.
Deploy an Amazon RDS instance with a cross-Region read replica in a secondary Region. In the event of a failure, promote the read replica to become the primary.
Deploy an Amazon Aurora DB cluster in the primary Region and another in a secondary Region. Use AWS DMS to keep the secondary Region in sync.
Deploy an Amazon RDS instance with a read replica in the same Region. In the event of a failure, promote the read replica to become the primary.

stem: A company hosts a ticketing service on a fleet of Linux Amazon EC2 instances that are in an Auto Scaling group. The ticketing service uses a pricing file. The pricing file is stored in an Amazon S3 bucket that has S3 Standard storage. A central pricing solution that is hosted by a third party updates the pricing file. The pricing file is updated every 1–15 minutes and has several thousand line items. The pricing file is downloaded to each EC2 instance when the instance launches. The EC2 instances occasionally use outdated pricing information that can result in incorrect charges for customers. Which solution will resolve this problem MOST cost-effectively?

options.text: Create an AWS Lambda function to update an Amazon DynamoDB table with new prices each time the pricing file is updated. Update the ticketing service to use DynamoDB to look up pricing.
Create an AWS Lambda function to update an Amazon EFS file share with the pricing file each time the file is updated. Update the ticketing service to use Amazon EFS to access the pricing file.

Load Mountpoint for Amazon S3 onto the AMI of the EC2 instances. Configure Mountpoint for Amazon S3 to mount the S3 bucket that contains the pricing file. Update the ticketing service to point to the mount point and path to access the S3 object.

Create an Amazon EBS volume. Use EBS Multi-Attach to attach the volume to every EC2 instance. When a new EC2 instance launches, configure the new instance to update the pricing file on the EBS volume. Update the ticketing service to point to the new local source.

stem: A company is storing sensitive data in an Amazon S3 bucket. The company must log all activities for objects in the S3 bucket and must keep the logs for 5 years. The company's security team also must receive an email notification every time there is an attempt to delete data in the S3 bucket. options.text: Configure AWS CloudTrail to log S3 data events.
Configure S3 server access logging for the S3 bucket.

Configure Amazon S3 to send object deletion events to an Amazon EventBridge event bus that publishes to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic.

stem: A company has an application that uses Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. The quality assurance (QA) department needs to launch and test the application. The application environments are currently launched by the manager of the department using an AWS CloudFormation template. To launch the stack, the manager uses a role with permission to use CloudFormation, EC2, and Auto Scaling APIs. The manager wants to allow QA to launch environments, but does not want to grant broad permissions to each user. Which set up would achieve these goals?

options.text: Upload the AWS CloudFormation template to Amazon S3. Give users in the QA department permission to assume the manager's role, restricts the permissions to the template and the resources it creates. Train users to launch the template from the CloudFormation console.

Create an AWS Service Catalog product from the environment template. Add a launch constraint to the product with the existing manager's department permission to use AWS Service Catalog APIs only. Train users to launch the template from the AWS Service Catalog console.

Upload the AWS CloudFormation template to Amazon S3. Give users in the QA department permission to use CloudFormation and restrict the permissions to the template and the resources it creates. Train users to launch the template from the CloudFormation console.

Create an AWS Elastic Beanstalk application from the environment template. Give users in the QA department permission to use Elastic Beanstalk only. Train users to launch Elastic Beanstalk environments with the Elastic Beanstalk CLI, passing the existing role to the environment.

stem: A financial services company runs a complex, multi-tier application on Amazon EC2 instances and AWS Lambda functions. The application stores temporary data in Amazon S3. The S3 objects are valid for only 45 minutes and are deleted after 24 hours. The company deploys each version of the application by launching an AWS CloudFormation stack. The stack creates all resources that are required to run the application. When the company deploys and validates a new application version, the company deletes the CloudFormation stack of the old version. The company recently tried to delete the CloudFormation stack of an old application version, but the operation failed. An analysis shows that CloudFormation failed to delete an existing S3 bucket. A solutions architect needs to resolve this issue without making major changes to the application's architecture. Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Implement a Lambda function that deletes all files from a given S3 bucket. Integrate this Lambda function as a custom resource into the CloudFormation stack. Ensure that the custom resource has a DependsOn attribute that points to the S3 bucket's resource.

Modify the CloudFormation template to provision an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system to store the temporary files there instead of in Amazon S3. Configure the Lambda functions to run in the same VPC as the file system. Mount the file system to the EC2 instances and Lambda functions.
Modify the CloudFormation stack to create an S3 Lifecycle rule that expires all objects 45 minutes after creation. Add a DependsOn attribute that points to the S3 bucket's resource.
Modify the CloudFormation stack to attach a DeletionPolicy attribute with a value of Delete to the S3 bucket.

explanation: CloudFormation cannot delete a nonempty S3 bucket; DeletionPolicy Delete does not empty it. Lambda-backed custom resource cleans bucket before deletion.
wrongOptionsExplanation: A correct: Lambda custom resource empties bucket. B requires architecture change. C invalid: S3 lifecycle expiration is not 45-minute granularity. D invalid: Delete policy cannot delete nonempty S3 bucket.
plainWords: CloudFormation cannot delete a nonempty S3 bucket; DeletionPolicy Delete does not empty it. Lambda-backed custom resource cleans bucket before deletion.
keyPoints: CloudFormation S3 buckets must be empty before deletion; DeletionPolicy Delete does not empty buckets.
sourceWarning: Corrected source answer D to A; compare duplicate Q82. AWS sources: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/TemplateReference/aws-resource-s3-bucket.html

review.notes: CloudFormation cannot delete a nonempty S3 bucket; DeletionPolicy Delete does not empty it. Lambda-backed custom resource cleans bucket before deletion.

stem: A company has application services that have been containerized and deployed on multiple Amazon EC2 instances with public IPs. An Apache Kafka cluster has been deployed to the EC2 instances. A PostgreSQL database has been migrated to Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL. The company expects a significant increase of orders on its platform when a new version of its flagship product is released. What changes to the current architecture will reduce operational overhead and support the product release?

options.text: Create an EC2 Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer. Create additional read replicas for the DB instance. Create Amazon Kinesis data streams and configure the application services to use the data streams. Store and serve static content directly from Amazon S3.

Create an EC2 Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer. Deploy theDB instance in Multi-AZ mode and enable storage auto scaling. Create Amazon Kinesis data streams and configure the application services to use the data streams. Store and serve static content directly from Amazon S3.

Deploy the application on a Kubernetes cluster created on the EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. Deploy the DB instance in Multi-AZ mode and enable storage auto scaling. Create an Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka cluster and configure the application services to use the cluster. Store static content in Amazon S3 behind an Amazon CloudFront distribution.

Deploy the application on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) with AWS Fargate and enable auto scaling behind an Application Load Balancer. Create additional read replicas for the DB instance. Create an Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka cluster and configure the application services to use the cluster. Store static content in Amazon S3 behind an Amazon CloudFront distribution.

explanation: D is the best supplied single answer. EKS on AWS Fargate removes EC2 worker node management and can scale pods behind an ALB configured with IP targets; Amazon MSK provides managed Apache Kafka compatible with the existing Kafka clients; RDS PostgreSQL read replicas offload read-heavy traffic; S3 with CloudFront efficiently delivers static content. This reduces operational work while providing scale-out options. The source key D is retained; independent exact-stem exam copies confirm the architecture, including reordered options.
wrongOptionsExplanation: A: EC2 Auto Scaling still requires EC2 maintenance; moving existing Kafka clients to Kinesis increases migration work; no CloudFront for static delivery. B: EC2 maintenance and Kafka-to-Kinesis conversion remain; RDS Multi-AZ improves HA and storage autoscaling capacity, but neither replaces read scaling; direct S3 misses CloudFront. C: Kafka-compatible MSK and CloudFront are appropriate, but self-managed Kubernetes on EC2 retains control-plane/node management; Multi-AZ does not scale reads like read replicas. D: Correct as best option, combining EKS Fargate, MSK, RDS read replicas, and CloudFront.
plainWords: Move containers to EKS Fargate, self-managed Kafka to MSK, add RDS PostgreSQL read replicas for reads, and serve static files through S3 plus CloudFront.
keyPoints: Fargate removes EC2 node operations; ALB for Fargate requires IP targets; MSK preserves Kafka client compatibility; RDS read replicas scale reads not writes; Multi-AZ mainly HA; CloudFront caches S3 static content.
sourceWarning: Option B typo 'theDB'. Stem predicts increased 'orders' but does not specify read/write ratio; read replicas cannot scale database writes, so D is best of listed options rather than a guaranteed solution to all order-processing bottlenecks. Configure Kubernetes HPA/Fargate profiles, AWS Load Balancer Controller IP target mode, MSK client networking, and replica read routing. Independent exact-stem copies reorder options, including one with D text labeled B; no confirmed Select TWO/THREE variant.

review.notes: Domain 4 single-answer 69/139; AWS technical confirmation plus multiple external exact-stem copies; options reordered in one source; no multi-answer variant; read-vs-write caveat.

stem: A company has multiple AWS accounts that are in an organization in AWS Organizations. The company needs to store AWS account activity and query the data from a central location by using SQL. Which solution will meet these requirements?

stem: A company has a legacy monolithic application that is critical to the company's business. The company hosts the application on an Amazon EC2 instance that runs Amazon Linux 2. The company's application team receives a directive from the legal department to back up the data from the instance's encrypted Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume to an Amazon S3 bucket. The application team does not have the administrative SSH key pair for the instance. The application must continue to serve the users. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Attach a role to the instance with permission to write to Amazon S3. Use the AWS Systems Manager Session Manager option to gain access to the instance and run commands to copy data into Amazon S3.

Create an image of the instance with the reboot option turned on. Launch a new EC2 instance from the image. Attach a role to the new instance with permission to write to Amazon S3. Run a command to copy data into Amazon S3.
Take a snapshot of the EBS volume by using Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager (Amazon DLM). Copy the data to Amazon S3.
Create an image of the instance. Launch a new EC2 instance from the image. Attach a role to the new instance with permission to write to Amazon S3. Run a command to copy data into Amazon S3.

stem: A company runs a simple Linux application on Amazon EKS by using nodes of the M6i (general purpose) instance type. The company has an EC2 Instance Savings Plan for the M6i family that will expire soon. A solutions architect must minimize the EKS compute costs when the Savings Plan expires. Which combination of steps will meet this requirement? (Select THREE.)

options.text: Rebuild the application container images to support ARM64 architecture.
Rebuild the application container images to support containers.
Migrate the EKS nodes to the most recent generation of Graviton-based instances.
Replace the EKS nodes with the most recent generation of x86_64 instances.
Purchase a new EC2 Instance Savings Plan for the newly selected Graviton instance family.
Purchase a new EC2 Instance Savings Plan for the newly selected x86_64 instance family.

explanation: A,C,E is the verified historical key. A ensures application container images have Linux/ARM64 compatible binaries/dependencies; C shifts EC2 EKS worker nodes from x86 M6i to compatible Graviton instances; E purchases an EC2 Instance Savings Plan specific to the chosen Graviton family and Region after assessing sustained usage. Graviton price/performance can reduce costs but no exact savings or superiority is guaranteed without benchmarking.
wrongOptionsExplanation: A correct for images not already multi-architecture: ARM64 image is needed for Graviton nodes. B wrong: EKS workloads are already containers. C correct intended: compatible Graviton nodes often provide better price/performance. D not chosen: newest x86_64 may help but misses intended Graviton strategy and is not always more expensive. E correct: discounted committed EC2 usage in selected Graviton family/Region; size flexible within family. F wrong for chosen architecture: x86_64 family commitment does not cover Graviton family.
plainWords: The existing EKS cluster uses x86 M6i EC2 nodes and its discount commitment is ending. Switch to ARM64-ready application images and Graviton EC2 nodes, then commit the expected stable Graviton usage under a new matching Savings Plan.
keyPoints: EKS supports ARM64 Graviton nodes; validate image manifest, native dependencies, DaemonSets, drivers and rollout. EC2 Instance Savings Plans lock to instance family plus Region, not size/AZ; Compute Savings Plans offer more flexibility. Savings Plans cover EC2 worker node usage, not EKS control-plane charges. Existing M6i plan cannot cover Graviton and does not transfer. Benchmark cost per workload and avoid overcommitment. 'Latest' instance generation and rebuilding images are not universally mandatory.
sourceWarning: Minor source overstatement: already ARM64-compatible/multi-architecture images need not be rebuilt, and newest Graviton plus a new Savings Plan is not mathematically guaranteed to minimize total cost without benchmark/commitment sizing. Existing EKS containers make B nonsensical. Duplicate Q45 is a near-verbatim compressed restatement of Q337 with identical A,C,E answer, not a separate independent exam concept.

stem: A company operates an API service in the AWS Cloud. The service is based on an Amazon API Gateway REST API that is integrated with an AWS Lambda function. stem: A company is expanding. The company plans to separate its resources into hundreds of different AWS accounts in multiple AWS Regions. stem: A multinational insurance company is deploying an internal claims processing AI assistant that is powered by Amazon Bedrock FMs. The AI assistant must use several internal APIs to retrieve claim records, perform fraud checks, and update policy data. The company already exposes the APIs through a centralized Amazon Bedrock AgentCore gateway where enterprise policies enforce IAM authorization, request validation, and tool-level access controls. stem: A company has a multi-tier web application that runs on a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The instances are in an Auto Scaling group. The ALB and the Auto Scaling group are replicated in a backup AWS Region. The minimum value and the maximum value for the Auto Scaling group are set to zero. The application presents an endpoint to end users by using an Amazon Route 53 record. The company does not have a large enough budget for an active-active strategy. What should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?

options.text: Reconfigure the application’s Route 53 record with a latency-based routing policy that load balances traffic between the two ALBs. Create an AWS Lambda function in the backup Region to promote the read replica and modify the Auto Scaling group values. Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm that is based on the HTTPCode_Target_5XX_Count metric for the ALB in the primary Region. Configure the CloudWatch alarm to invoke the Lambda function.

Create an AWS Lambda function in the backup Region to promote the read replica and modify the Auto Scaling group values. Configure Route 53 with a health check that monitors the web application and sends an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) notification to the Lambda function when the health check status is unhealthy. Update the application’s Route 53 record with a failover policy that routes traffic to the ALB in the backup Region when a health check failure occurs.

Reconfigure the application’s Route 53 record with a latency-based routing policy that load balances traffic between the two ALBs. Remove the read replica. Create an AWS Lambda function in the backup Region to promote the read replica and modify the Auto Scaling group values. Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm that is based on the HTTPCode_Target_5XX_Count metric for the ALB in the primary Region. Configure the CloudWatch alarm to invoke the Lambda function.

explanation: B is the intended best single answer: Route 53 health-check-based failover records implement active/passive DNS, and a CloudWatch alarm on Route 53 health check status can publish SNS to invoke Lambda, which promotes the cross-Region RDS read replica and raises standby Auto Scaling group capacity. AWS RDS documents replica promotion as a recovery mechanism; AWS Route 53 documents DNS failover and CloudWatch/SNS notifications. However, Route 53 does NOT send SNS directly; CloudWatch alarm mediates it, and the DNS failover may occur before the zero-capacity standby is ready. This option does not guarantee RTO <15 minutes without orchestration, readiness gating, and drills. Independent exact-stem exam copies key B.
wrongOptionsExplanation: A: Latency routing is not the desired active/passive primary/standby strategy, and ALB 5XX alarm can miss failures or be noisy; secondary ASG is zero. B: Best: Route 53 health-check failover plus CloudWatch alarm/SNS/Lambda promotion and standby ASG scale-out, with missing sequencing caveat. C: Fully sized secondary compute raises costs; latency routing creates active-active behavior; snapshot/S3 is not continuous RDS cross-Region replication. D: Equal-weight Global Accelerator endpoints are inconsistent with cold standby and may route before readiness; ALB 5XX alarm alone is insufficient.
plainWords: Keep backup compute off, monitor the primary web app with Route 53, and use CloudWatch alarm → SNS → Lambda to promote the standby database and start backup servers. Route 53 switches DNS when standby is ready.
keyPoints: Active/passive uses Route 53 failover routing, not latency; health check notifications require CloudWatch alarm to SNS; SNS can invoke Lambda; RDS cross-Region read replica can be promoted; standby ASG zero saves cost but slows RTO; DNS failover must be sequenced with readiness.
sourceWarning: Original option B incorrectly implies Route 53 health check directly sends SNS; actual chain is health check → CloudWatch alarm → SNS → Lambda. Route 53 DNS failover can precede promotion and ASG warm-up, creating outage; 15-minute RTO not guaranteed. RDS promotion can take several minutes or longer and replication is asynchronous (potential data loss). Need readiness-gated traffic cutover, IAM permissions, database endpoint update, safe failback and tested RTO. Option C typo 'Replicationbetween'. No confirmed Choose TWO/THREE exact-stem variant; external exact copies single-answer B.

review.notes: Domain 4 70/139; Q337 Select THREE skipped; intended B confirmed by AWS plus external exact copies. Technically incomplete SNS chain, readiness sequencing, RTO guarantee flagged.

stem: A company hosts a game player-matching service on a public-facing, physical, on-premises instance that all users are able to access over the internet. All traffic to the instance uses UDP. Which combination of steps should the solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Select THREE.)

options.text: Use a Network Load Balancer (NLB) in front of the player-matching instance. Use a friendly DNS entry in Amazon Route 53 pointing to the NLB's Elastic IP address.
Use an Application Load Balancer (ALB) in front of the player-matching instance. Use a friendly DNS entry in Amazon Route 53 pointing to the ALB's internet-facing fully qualified domain name (FQDN).
Define an AWS WAF rule to explicitly drop non-UDP traffic, and associate the rule with the load balancer.
Configure a network ACL rule to block all non-UDP traffic. Associate the network ACL with the subnets that hold the load balancer instances.
Use Amazon CloudFront with an Elastic Load Balancer as an origin.
Enable AWS Shield Advanced on all public-facing resources.

explanation: Historical source intended A,D,F in the GitHub option order. NLB supports UDP for game matchmaking; subnet network ACL can restrict traffic by protocol; Shield Advanced adds advanced DDoS protection for supported public resources including NLB. Note that NLB DNS should be mapped using a Route 53 alias to its DNS name, not to one Elastic IP, and a blanket non-UDP NACL deny can break health checks. NLB security groups also support UDP restrictions and should be considered in a modern design.
wrongOptionsExplanation: A intended correct: UDP capable NLB, but DNS wording pointing to one EIP is fragile; Route 53 alias to NLB DNS preferred. B wrong: ALB cannot carry arbitrary UDP. C wrong: WAF is HTTP(S) L7 and cannot directly filter UDP on NLB. D intended correct: subnet NACL can filter protocols but stateless rules must preserve return traffic, TCP health checks and required operational access; 'all non-UDP' overbroad. E wrong: CloudFront is HTTP(S) delivery, not arbitrary UDP transport. F correct: Shield Advanced protects supported public NLB resources against DDoS; scope to eligible public resources.
plainWords: A game server uses UDP. Move it behind an internet-facing NLB, filter unnecessary network traffic with carefully designed network ACL/security group rules, and protect the public endpoint with Shield Advanced.
keyPoints: UDP -> NLB, not ALB/CloudFront. WAF -> HTTP(S), not UDP on NLB. Route 53 alias targets NLB DNS, not one EIP. NACLs stateless: allow response ephemeral ports and health checks; modern NLB supports security groups. Shield Advanced can protect supported NLBs. The game service must actually migrate onto suitable AWS targets; an on-prem UDP target is not interchangeable with a normal EC2 target.
sourceWarning: RESTORED CORRUPTED SOURCE: original had only A-D and answer A,D despite Select THREE. Restored E CloudFront and F Shield Advanced from two external variants; new historical key A,D,F (corresponds to reordered FreeCram A,B,E). Original snapshot preserved. Older SAP-C01 era item; A's EIP DNS target and D's all-non-UDP ACL are technically overbroad. AWS WAF cannot protect UDP. Do not claim that NLB UDP directly targeting a remote on-prem IP works during migration.

technicalCaveats: Route 53 alias to NLB DNS rather than one EIP
NACL blanket deny breaks health checks without exceptions

options.text: Create an Amazon RDS DB instance with separate schemas to host the product data and the user session data. Configure a read replica for the DB instance in another Region.

Create an Amazon RDS DB instance to host the product data. Configure a read replica for the DB instance in another Region. Create a global datastore in Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached to host the user session data.
Create two Amazon DynamoDB global tables. Use one global table to host the product data Use the other global table to host the user session data. Use DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) for caching.
Create an Amazon RDS DB instance to host the product data. Configure a read replica for the DB instance in another Region. Create an Amazon DynamoDB global table to host the user session data

explanation: Corrected to C from invalid source B. B proposes an ElastiCache Global Datastore for Memcached, which AWS does not support: Global Datastore is for Valkey or Redis OSS. C separates product and temporary session data into two DynamoDB global tables with cross-Region replication and adds DAX for eligible low-latency read caching, making it the strongest supported performance-focused option if the product model is suitable for DynamoDB. D is a viable relational-product/session-separation alternative but lacks DAX caching. DAX is regional and global table replication bypasses DAX, potentially causing stale cached reads in the DR Region. Exact-stem external exam copy keys B incorrectly.
wrongOptionsExplanation: A: Two schemas share one RDS DB instance and do not isolate session and product storage/throughput; cross-Region replica alone does not decouple workloads. B: Invalid; Memcached does not support ElastiCache Global Datastore, which requires Valkey or Redis OSS. C: Corrected best valid answer, assuming product data access patterns fit DynamoDB; two global tables isolate workloads and replicate to DR Region, with regional DAX caches for read acceleration. D: Technically valid for relational product data plus DynamoDB session data and cross-Region replication, but no DAX caching, so C has the strongest stated performance feature.
plainWords: The old answer B cannot be deployed because Memcached has no Global Datastore. Use separate DynamoDB global tables for product and session records and DAX for fast cached reads, if the product data model fits DynamoDB.
keyPoints: ElastiCache Global Datastore = Valkey/Redis OSS only, NOT Memcached; DynamoDB global tables replicate cross-Region; DAX caches are regional, do not replicate, and may become stale after cross-Region writes; DynamoDB product modeling needs appropriate access patterns.
sourceWarning: CRITICAL source-key defect: exact external question keys B, but ElastiCache Global Datastore for Memcached is unsupported. Correct answer changed B→C based on AWS documentation. C is contingent on suitability of product data for DynamoDB; if relational queries are required, D is a reasonable alternative and 'highest performance' is underspecified. DAX is Region-specific and cross-Region replication bypasses it, so stale cached reads possible. Source C/D punctuation defects preserved. review.notes: Domain 4 71/139. Q346 Select THREE skipped and internally inconsistent. Exact-stem exam copy keys invalid B. AWS Global Datastore does not support Memcached. Correct to C with DynamoDB data model and DAX staleness caveats.

A Solutions Architect must create a containerized architecture that meets the security requirements and has deployed the application to an Amazon ECS cluster. What steps are required after the deployment to meet the requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: Create tasks using the bridge network mode.
Create tasks using the awsvpc network mode.
Apply security groups to Amazon EC2 instances, and use IAM roles for EC2 instances to access other resources.
Apply security groups to the tasks, and pass IAM credentials into the container at launch time to access other resources.
Apply security groups to the tasks, and use IAM roles for tasks to access other resources.

explanation: B,E independently confirmed by AWS ECS documentation and external exam mirrors. B awsvpc allocates task-specific ENI/IP and enables security groups directly on ECS tasks, allowing per-microservice ingress/egress control. E combines task security groups with IAM task roles for workload-specific temporary AWS credentials. Task role is distinct from ECS task execution role (agent pulls ECR images/writes logs) and EC2 instance profile.
wrongOptionsExplanation: A bridge mode is valid for Linux ECS on EC2 but tasks share host networking context and cannot directly attach per-task security groups; it is not the least-privilege network choice. B correct: awsvpc gives task ENI/IP and SG. C EC2 host SG and instance profile permissions apply at host scope and can be shared by multiple tasks, violating granular least privilege. D per-task SG is good but injecting long-lived IAM credentials into containers is insecure and unnecessary; ECS task roles provide temporary credentials. E correct: task SG + IAM task role isolates both network and API permissions.
plainWords: Each ECS microservice needs its own network firewall and its own AWS permissions. Use awsvpc networking to attach security groups to each task, and give each task a least-privilege IAM task role instead of using the EC2 host role or hardcoded credentials.
keyPoints: awsvpc is only ECS network mode allowing task-level security groups; mandatory for Fargate. Each task gets ENI/IP, SG, and ALB/NLB ip target type. Task IAM role for app API calls; execution role for agent ECR/CloudWatch operations; EC2 instance profile for host/agent. Bridge network mode can still use task IAM roles, but lacks per-task SG. EC2-hosted ECS tasks may need IMDS isolation ECS_AWSVPC_BLOCK_IMDS=true to avoid exposure of host instance profile. Configure networking/roles in task definition and ECS service/task network configuration, generally before launching/redeploying tasks.
sourceWarning: Minor chronology ambiguity: stem says app already deployed to ECS, but awsvpc network mode is defined in the task definition and SG is assigned when running tasks/services; changing requires new task definition/service deployment, not a post-deployment in-place toggle. No material AWS deprecation. External mirrors may share common source; AWS docs are authority.

review.examVariantStatus: Three exact five-option mirrors; one explicitly keys B,E. Exam mirrors not independent technical authority.

explanation: C is verified. Existing backend services already run on EC2 behind an ALB, so EC2 Auto Scaling groups increase/decrease instances with traffic without rewriting the backend. DynamoDB auto scaling adjusts provisioned read and write throughput of tables and GSIs using target utilization, addressing seasonal database throttling with minimal development. wrongOptionsExplanation: A: Lambda migration requires code and deployment changes; manually increasing DynamoDB read/write capacity does not automatically adapt to seasonal demand. B: Lambda migration adds development work; DynamoDB global tables are for multi-Region replication, not a direct remedy for existing single-Region read/write capacity. C: Correct; existing EC2 application and DynamoDB provisioned throughput can both scale without rewriting application architecture. D: SQS plus Lambda can buffer asynchronous writes, but changes application semantics/integration and does not directly address synchronous reads; more development than C.
plainWords: Keep the existing EC2 backend, put it in an Auto Scaling group behind the ALB, and enable DynamoDB auto scaling for reads and writes.
keyPoints: EC2 ASG scales application instances; DynamoDB auto scaling scales provisioned RCU/WCU and GSIs; DynamoDB on-demand is a different capacity mode; DynamoDB auto scaling can lag sharp spikes; global tables solve multi-Region replication, not baseline capacity.
sourceWarning: No substantive source-answer defect. Option C assumes DynamoDB provisioned capacity mode; on-demand capacity is a viable modern alternative but not an offered answer. Target-tracking DynamoDB auto scaling responds to sustained load with CloudWatch evaluation and capacity-update lag, so scheduled scaling/pre-warming may help predictable seasonal spikes. stem: A company has developed a hybrid solution between its data center and AWS. The company uses Amazon VPC and Amazon EC2 instances that send application togs to Amazon CloudWatch. The EC2 instances read data from multiple relational databases that are hosted on premises. The company wants to monitor which EC2 instances are connected to the databases in near-real time. The company already has a monitoring solution that uses Splunk on premises. A solutions architect needs to determine how to send networking traffic to Splunk. How should the solutions architect meet these requirements?

options.text: Enable VPC flows logs, and send them to CloudWatch. Create an AWS Lambda function to periodically export the CloudWatch logs to an Amazon S3 bucket by using the pre-defined export function. Generate ACCESS_KEY and SECRET_KEY AWS credentials. Configure Splunk to pull the logs from the S3 bucket by using those credentials.

Create an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream with Splunk as the destination. Configure a pre-processing AWS Lambda function with a Kinesis Data Firehose stream processor that extracts individual log events from records sent by CloudWatch Logs subscription filters. Enable VPC flows logs, and send them to CloudWatch. Create a CloudWatch Logs subscription that sends log events to the Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream.

Ask the company to log every request that is made to the databases along with the EC2 instance IP address. Export the CloudWatch logs to an Amazon S3 bucket. Use Amazon Athena to query the logs grouped by database name. Export Athena results to another S3 bucket. Invoke an AWS Lambda function to automatically send any new file that is put in the S3 bucket to Splunk.

Send the CloudWatch logs to an Amazon Kinesis data stream with Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics for SOL Applications. Configure a 1 -minute sliding window to collect the events. Create a SQL query that uses the anomaly detection template to monitor any networking traffic anomalies in near-real time. Send the result to an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream with Splunk as the destination.

explanation: B is the best source answer. VPC Flow Logs capture IP connection metadata for EC2 network interfaces, including source/destination addresses and ports for connections to on-premises databases. CloudWatch Logs subscription filters stream flow logs to Amazon Data Firehose, which delivers to on-prem Splunk via HTTP Event Collector (HEC), with optional decompression/transformation and S3 failure backup. This meets near-real-time monitoring with little application change. AWS now supports direct VPC Flow Logs to Firehose and built-in CloudWatch log decompression, making option B's Lambda transformation optional depending on Splunk add-on and format. Independent exact-stem single-answer exam copies key B.
wrongOptionsExplanation: A: Periodic CloudWatch export to S3 and Splunk polling introduce batch latency and unnecessary static access-key management. B: Correct; VPC Flow Logs→CloudWatch subscription→Data Firehose→Splunk HEC streams network metadata near real time. C: Requires instrumenting every database request, Athena batch queries, and multiple S3/Lambda transfers, increasing delay and complexity. D: Detects anomalies instead of reporting all EC2/database connections, adds unnecessary Kinesis processing, and Kinesis Data Analytics for SQL Applications was discontinued effective January 27, 2026.
plainWords: Stream VPC Flow Logs through CloudWatch Logs and Amazon Data Firehose to the existing Splunk HEC endpoint to see which EC2 IPs connect to on-premises database IPs.
keyPoints: VPC Flow Logs provide connection metadata not packet payloads; CloudWatch Logs subscriptions deliver near real time; Amazon Data Firehose (renamed from Kinesis Data Firehose) supports Splunk HEC and decompression; direct Flow Logs→Firehose now supported; Kinesis Data Analytics for SQL discontinued Jan 27 2026.
sourceWarning: Original stem typo 'application togs' (logs); option A 'VPC flows logs'; option D 'SOL Applications' (SQL) and '1 -minute'. D relies on Kinesis Data Analytics for SQL, discontinued Jan 27 2026. B's preprocessing Lambda is no longer universally required: native Firehose decompression and updated Splunk add-ons can handle events, and direct VPC Flow Logs→Firehose is supported. VPC Flow Logs are aggregated network metadata (not SQL statements), near-real-time rather than instantaneous; Splunk HEC must be securely reachable from AWS. External exact-stem versions are single-answer B; no confirmed Choose TWO/THREE variant.

review.notes: Domain 4 73/139; source B retained. Exact external single-answer copies confirm B. AWS docs show direct Firehose ingestion and optional Lambda; option D service discontinued 2026. Typos and limitations flagged.

stem: A company needs to store sensitive and crucial business data in an Amazon S3 bucket. Because of the criticality of the data, the data must be available in a second AWS Region within 15 minutes. If any object is not available within 15 minutes, an operations team must receive a notification. The company has already enabled S3 Versioning on the S3 bucket, and the company creates a second S3 bucket in the second Region. Which combination of solutions will meet these requirements? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Create a new S3 replication rule. Configure the rule to replicate all objects to the second S3 bucket.
Create an AWS DataSync task. Set the appropriate source and destination S3 buckets for the task.

Enable S3 Replication Time Control (S3 RTC), and configure the replication metrics and events. Create an Amazon SNS topic and set it as the target for the OperationMissedThreshold S3 event notification. Use the SNS topic to notify the operations team.

Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration on both S3 buckets. Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm for the S3 5xxErrors metric. Create an Amazon SNS topic and set it as the target for the alarm. Use the SNS topic to notify the operations team.

Enable AWS DataSync enhanced transfer mode. Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm for the DataSync FilesFailed metric. Create an Amazon SNS topic and set it as the target for the alarm. Use the SNS topic to notify the operations team.

explanation: A,C verified against AWS S3 RTC docs and exact external exam variant. A establishes native S3 Cross-Region Replication rule for eligible objects; both source and destination buckets must have versioning enabled, and IAM replication role/permissions are needed. C enables S3 Replication Time Control, metrics, and S3 event s3:Replication:OperationMissedThreshold sent to SNS when a replicated object misses 15 minutes. RTC is SLA-backed, not absolute per-object guarantee.
wrongOptionsExplanation: A correct: replication rule copies new eligible objects to second Region; existing objects need S3 Batch Replication backfill. B wrong: DataSync task is batch/scheduled transfer, no per-object 15-minute RTC threshold event. C correct: S3 RTC plus OperationMissedThreshold event and SNS exactly match threshold alert. D wrong: Transfer Acceleration speeds client uploads, S3 5xxErrors are API/server errors, not replica lag. E wrong: DataSync enhanced mode and FilesFailed report transfer failures, not native continuous S3 replication lag threshold.
plainWords: Automatically copy new S3 objects to a bucket in another Region. Turn on S3 Replication Time Control and send an SNS alert when any eligible object misses the 15-minute deadline.
keyPoints: CRR rule + S3 RTC + s3:Replication:OperationMissedThreshold -> SNS. RTC targets 15-minute replication with SLA, not absolute 100% per-object guarantee. Versioning required on BOTH buckets. Existing objects need S3 Batch Replication; standard live replication only applies to new/updated eligible objects. SSE-KMS objects need correct replication encryption configuration/KMS permissions. OperationFailedReplication is a separate failure event; optionally monitor it too. Transfer Acceleration/5xxErrors do not measure replication latency.
sourceWarning: The stem says data 'must be available' in 15 minutes, but RTC is SLA-backed rather than 100% guarantee. It says source versioning enabled but does not explicitly confirm destination versioning; must enable destination versioning. A says replicate 'all objects', but existing pre-rule objects are not automatically backfilled by live replication; use S3 Batch Replication. SNS threshold notifications may be delayed and require destination policy/subscription setup.

Store the output in Amazon S3. Parse this output by extracting the data that is required within the application tier. Submit the data to the target system's API.

Use this tier to call endpoints that host artificial intelligence and machine learning (Al/ML) models that are trained and hosted in Amazon SageMaker to perform optical character recognition (OCR) on the forms. Store the output in Amazon ElastiCache. Parse this output by extracting the data that is required within the application tier. Submit the data to the target system's API.

Parse this output by extracting the data that is required within the application tier. Submit the data to the target system's API.

explanation: D verified. Amazon Textract is managed OCR/document analysis and extracts printed/handwritten text, form key-value pairs and tables. Amazon Comprehend can analyze extracted text (but is NOT the OCR engine). Step Functions and Lambda orchestrate extraction, validation, S3 output, error handling, and downstream API integration without training/hosting custom OCR models or managing servers. Official AWS documentation includes Textract-to-Comprehend processing; exact-stem external single-answer copies identify the same architecture, though letters are reordered.
wrongOptionsExplanation: A: Custom OCR libraries plus EKS and EC2-hosted application tier require extensive model/application development and cluster/node operations, contrary to rapid delivery and low maintenance. B: Step Functions/Lambda are good orchestration, but training and hosting custom OCR models on EC2 adds ML training, deployment and infrastructure overhead. C: SageMaker-hosted custom OCR plus EC2 app tier and ElastiCache introduces training, infrastructure and ephemeral result storage complexity; managed Textract is simpler. D: Correct; Textract extracts text/forms, Comprehend optionally analyzes language, Step Functions/Lambda automate validation and API calls.
plainWords: Use S3 uploads to start a Step Functions/Lambda workflow that calls Textract to read scanned forms, optionally Comprehend to analyze the text, validates extracted fields, and submits them to the destination API.
keyPoints: Textract performs OCR and form key-value extraction; Comprehend performs NLP, NOT OCR; Step Functions/Lambda orchestrate managed processing; confidence thresholds and human review for low-confidence fields; asynchronous Textract for large/multipage documents.
sourceWarning: Option D inaccurately implies both Textract and Comprehend perform OCR; Comprehend performs NLP only and is optional if only form key-value extraction is required. Neither service guarantees accurate extraction without confidence validation/human review. Option C typo 'Al/ML' (AI/ML).
