AWS documents DataBrew PII transforms and Redshift Serverless cross-Region sharing. Exact-stem external exam copy keys B. Implementation must strictly prevent unmasked PII from entering cross-Region analytics; some DataBrew masking methods are reversible and not automatically equivalent to irreversible anonymization.
wrongOptionsExplanation: A: Outposts places AWS infrastructure at customer premises, unnecessary for regional data residency and adds operational complexity; Athena is possible but Outposts does not solve the problem more appropriately than regional managed databases. B: Correct if DataBrew processing occurs in each source Region and only approved anonymized outputs are shared for Redshift Serverless analytics. C: Lambda anonymization could be valid but requires custom logic; PrivateLink alone neither anonymizes data nor guarantees that cross-Region QuickSight queries expose only anonymized data. D: Macie discovers/classifies PII in S3 but does NOT anonymize source records; Block Public Access is unrelated to ensuring no raw PII crosses Regions.
plainWords: Store raw customer PII in an Aurora database in its original AWS Region, anonymize locally with DataBrew, and send only approved anonymized datasets to Redshift Serverless for global analysis.
keyPoints: Data residency applies to raw PII, not necessarily de-identified analytics; DataBrew can mask/redact PII but not all masking is irreversible; Redshift Serverless supports cross-Region data sharing; Macie detects sensitive data, not anonymizes it; Outposts is on-prem AWS hardware.
sourceWarning: Option B is conceptually correct but underspecified: it does not explicitly require in-Region DataBrew jobs, restricted output locations, only anonymized Redshift ingestion/sharing, or prevention of cross-Region raw PII access. Masking/encryption/pseudonymization may be reversible and may not satisfy legal anonymization; validate re-identification risk. Redshift cross-Region sharing availability depends on Region. External exact-stem copy keys B; no confirmed Choose TWO/THREE variant.

review.notes: Domain 4 75/139. AWS DataBrew, Redshift Serverless, Macie docs and exact-stem exam copy support B. In-Region masking, irreversible anonymization validation and access restrictions required.

stem: A company is deploying a third-party firewall appliance solution from AWS Marketplace to monitor and protect traffic that leaves the company's AWS environments. The company wants to deploy this appliance into a shared services VPC and route all outbound internet- bound traffic through the appliances. A solutions architect needs to recommend a deployment method that prioritizes reliability and minimizes failover time between firewall appliances within a single AWS Region. The company has set up routing from the shared services VPC to other VPCs. Which steps should the solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements? (Select THREE.)

options.text: Deploy two firewall appliances into the shared services VPC, each in a separate Availability Zone.

Create a new Network Load Balancer in the shared services VPC. Create a new target group, and attach it to the new Network Load Balancer. Add each of the firewall appliance instances to the target group.

Create a new Gateway Load Balancer in the shared services VPC. Create a new target group, and attach it to the new Gateway Load Balancer. Add each of the firewall appliance instances to the target group.
Create a VPC interface endpoint. Add a route to the route table in the shared services VPC. Designate the new endpoint as the next hop for traffic that enters the shared services VPC from other VPCs.
Deploy two firewall appliances into the shared services VPC. each in the same Availability Zone.

Create a VPC Gateway Load Balancer endpoint. Add a route to the route table in the shared services VPC. Designate the new endpoint as the next hop for traffic that enters the shared services VPC from other VPCs.

stem: A global manufacturing company plans to migrate the majority of its applications to AWS. However, the company is concerned about applications that need to remain within a specific country or in the company's central on-premises data center because of data regulatory requirements or requirements for latency of single-digit milliseconds. The company also is concerned about the applications that it hosts in some of its factory sites, where limited network infrastructure exists. The company wants a consistent developer experience so that its developers can build applications once and deploy on premises, in the cloud, or in a hybrid architecture. The developers must be able to use the same tools, APIs, and services that are familiar to them. Which solution will provide a consistent hybrid experience to meet these requirements?

options.text: Migrate all applications to the closest AWS Region that is compliant. Set up an AWS Direct Connect connection between the central on-premises data center and AWS. Deploy a Direct Connect gateway.

Use AWS Snowball Edge Storage Optimized devices for the applications that have data regulatory requirements or requirements for latency of single-digit milliseconds. Retain the devices on premises. Deploy AWS Wavelength to host the workloads in the factory sites.

Install AWS Outposts for the applications that have data regulatory requirements or requirements for latency of single-digit milliseconds. Use AWS Snowball Edge Compute Optimized devices to host the workloads in the factory sites.

Migrate the applications that have data regulatory requirements or requirements for latency of single-digit milliseconds to an AWS Local Zone. Deploy AWS Wavelength to host the workloads in the factory sites.

explanation: C is the intended historical single answer. AWS Outposts extends AWS-managed infrastructure, supported services, APIs and developer tooling into the company's central on-premises data center, supporting low-latency local processing, local data residency and hybrid consistency. Snowball Edge Compute Optimized historically supplied local EC2-style compute for remote factory sites with restricted/intermittent connectivity. The exact-stem practice copies key the Outposts + Snowball Edge Compute Optimized combination (option lettering varies). IMPORTANT 2026 LIFECYCLE DEFECT: Snowball Edge has not been offered to new customers since November 7, 2025, and AWS has announced the end of support in commercial AWS Regions on December 31, 2026. Thus C is exam-historical, not a fully deployable recommendation for a new customer in 2026; rearchitect remote factory compute using currently available edge/on-premises solutions after checking supported form factors, network requirements and relevant region/country restrictions.
wrongOptionsExplanation: A: Direct Connect provides dedicated connectivity to an AWS Region, but does not place compute in the local data center or reliably achieve single-digit-millisecond local application interactions; it also does not address disconnected factory compute. B: Storage Optimized is intended primarily for high-capacity storage/data transfer, while Wavelength runs at telecommunications providers' 5G edge rather than installing locally at disconnected factories. C: Correct historically because Outposts provides consistent AWS APIs and locally hosted workloads at the central data center, and Snowball Edge Compute Optimized formerly provided compute at poorly connected factory sites; now lifecycle-obsolete for new customers. D: Local Zones are AWS-operated extensions closer to end users rather than resources installed at the customer's specified on-premises data center; Wavelength is built for carrier 5G mobile-edge workloads, not factory offline processing.
plainWords: Historically, put AWS Outposts in the main company data center and Snowball Edge Compute Optimized boxes at disconnected factories. As of 2026, retain C only as the legacy exam answer because new customers can no longer obtain Snowball Edge.
keyPoints: Outposts = managed AWS compute on premises with AWS tools/APIs, data-locality and low latency, but normally requires a service link to a home AWS Region. Snowball Edge Compute Optimized = historical offline/remote edge compute, NOT currently available to new customers. Snowball Edge Storage Optimized primarily emphasizes storage capacity. Local Zones = AWS-operated nearby compute. Wavelength = telecom 5G edge. Direct Connect = private connection, not local compute.
sourceWarning: HIGH — OUTDATED/NO LONGER NEWLY DEPLOYABLE: AWS Snowball Edge stopped accepting new customers effective November 7, 2025; AWS announces commercial-Region support ending December 31, 2026. Option C remains the original correct answer, but the question does not distinguish existing customers or historic timing, so it should not be taught as a current greenfield solution. Also Outposts requires site readiness and sustained Region service-link connectivity; country-specific residency and available form factors must be validated. Cross-source option letters differ: Pupuweb lists C, GoShiken has identical solution at D. Checked exact-stem published variants and did not find an authenticated Choose TWO/THREE version.

review.notes: Domain 4 76/139. Q375 skipped (Choose THREE). Exact-stem sources confirm Outposts + Snowball Edge Compute Optimized as the legacy correct answer, despite remapped choice letters. AWS official Nov 2025 new-customer cutoff and Dec 2026 commercial support end make this a high-priority outdated item. No substantiated multi-answer variant located.

stem: A company wants to migrate its website to AWS. The website uses containers that are deployed in an on-premises, self-managed Kubernetes cluster. All data for the website is stored in an on-premises PostgreSQL database. The company has decided to migrate the on-premises Kubernetes cluster to an Amazon EKS cluster. The EKS cluster will use EKS managed node groups with a static number of nodes. The company will also migrate the on-premises database to an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL database. A solutions architect needs to estimate the total cost of ownership (TCO) for this workload before the migration. Which solution will provide the required TCO information?

options.text: Request access to Migration Evaluator. Run the Migration Evaluator Collector and import the data. Configure a scenario. Export a Quick Insights report from Migration Evaluator.
Launch AWS DMS for the on-premises database. Generate an assessment report. Create an estimate in AWS Pricing Calculator for the costs of the EKS migration.
Initialize AWS Application Migration Service. Add the on-premises servers as source servers. Launch a test instance. Output a TCO report from Application Migration Service.
Access the AWS Cloud Economics Center webpage to assess the AWS Cloud Value Framework. Create an AWS Cost and Usage report from the Cloud Value Framework.

explanation: A is the best exam answer. Migration Evaluator inventories on-premises servers and utilization, supports migration scenarios, and produces Quick Insights and more detailed business-case/TCO outputs to compare the on-premises footprint against AWS. AWS official getting-started instructions explicitly describe requesting an assessment, using the collector or inventory upload, and receiving Quick Insights. For a replatforming target of EKS managed node groups plus RDS PostgreSQL, however, Quick Insights is directional and should be supplemented by a service-specific cost model: EKS control-plane fee, static EC2 worker nodes, RDS instance/storage/backups, networking and operating expenses. Do not treat the generic infrastructure report as a complete detailed EKS/RDS TCO.
wrongOptionsExplanation: A: Correct exam selection; Migration Evaluator provides on-prem discovery, scenario analysis and TCO-oriented Quick Insights/business case, though EKS/RDS-specific costs need validation. B: DMS assessment focuses on database migration compatibility/readiness and AWS Pricing Calculator for EKS alone omits on-prem baseline and RDS/other costs; not a full TCO. C: Application Migration Service replicates and migrates source servers; test launches do not produce the proposed TCO report, and lifting servers to EC2 differs from replatforming to EKS/RDS. D: Cloud Value Framework is a business-value methodology; AWS Cost and Usage Reports report actual AWS consumption and are not generated by that framework or a pre-migration estimate.
plainWords: Use Migration Evaluator to measure the current on-premises workload and compare it with projected AWS costs before moving; refine the estimate for EKS and RDS separately.
keyPoints: Migration Evaluator = discovery, utilization, TCO/business case, Quick Insights. DMS = database migration, not full TCO. Application Migration Service = server migration, not TCO reporting. Cloud Value Framework = qualitative/quantitative business benefits; Cost and Usage Report = actual AWS billing data. Quick Insights may not price EKS/RDS modernization precisely.
sourceWarning: MODERATE: The stated target is EKS with static managed nodes and RDS PostgreSQL. Migration Evaluator Quick Insights is a directional infrastructure-level report and may not fully account for EKS control-plane fees, RDS sizing and all migration/operational costs; use detailed pricing/assumptions to complete TCO. Source copies rearrange option labels: FreeCram keys D for Migration Evaluator while local JSON and ExamTopics.cn key A. All inspected copies are single-choice; no confirmed Choose TWO/THREE variant.

review.notes: Domain 4 77/139. Exact-stem external copies support Migration Evaluator; letter varies A/D. No substantiated multi-answer variant. Quick Insights is directional, not complete detailed EKS/RDS TCO.

stem: A company wants to optimize AWS data-transfer costs and compute costs across developer accounts within the company's organization in AWS Organizations Developers can configure VPCs and launch Amazon EC2 instances in a single AWS Region The EC2 instances retrieve approximately 1 TB of data each day from Amazon S3 The developer activity leads to excessive monthly data-transfer charges and NAT gateway processing charges between EC2 instances and S3 buckets, along with high compute costs The company wants to proactively enforce approved architectural patterns for any EC2 instance and VPC infrastructure that developers deploy within the AWS accounts The company does not wantthis enforcement to negatively affect the speed at which the developers can perform their tasks Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

options.text: Create SCPs to prevent developers from launching unapproved EC2 instance types Provide the developers with an AWS CloudFormation template to deploy an approved VPC configuration with S3 interface endpoints Scope the developers* IAM permissions so that the developers can launch VPC resources only with CloudFormation

Create a daily forecasted budget with AWS Budgets to monitor EC2 compute costs and S3 data-transfer costs across the developer accounts When the forecasted cost is 75% of the actual budget cost, send an alert to the developer teams If the actual budget cost is 100%. create a budget action to terminate the developers' EC2 instances and VPC infrastructure

Create an AWS Service Catalog portfolio that users can use to create an approved VPC configuration with S3 gateway endpoints and approved EC2 instances Share the portfolio with the developer accounts Configure an AWS Service Catalog launch constraint to use an approved IAM role Scope the developers' IAM permissions to allow access only to AWS Service Catalog

Create and deploy AWS Config rules to monitor the compliance of EC2 and VPC resources in the developer AWS accounts If developers launch unapproved EC2 instances or if developers create VPCs without S3 gateway endpoints perform a remediation action to terminate the unapproved resources

stem: A company runs applications in hundreds of production AWS accounts. The company uses AWS Organizations with all features enabled and has a centralized backup operation that uses AWS Backup. The company is concerned about ransomware attacks. To address this concern, the company has created a new policy that all backups must be resilient to breaches of privileged-user credentials in any production account. Which combination of steps will meet this new requirement? (Select THREE.)

options.text: Implement cross-account backup with AWS Backup vaults in designated non-production accounts.
Add an SCP that restricts the modification of AWS Backup vaults.
Implement AWS Backup Vault Lock in compliance mode.
Configure the backup frequency, lifecycle, and retention period to ensure that at least one backup always exists in the cold tier.
Configure AWS Backup to write all backups to an Amazon S3 bucket in a designated non-production account. Ensure that the S3 bucket has S3 Object Lock enabled.
Implement least privilege access for the IAM service role that is assigned to AWS Backup.

stem: A company runs an application on AWS. The application uses an Amazon Aurora MySQL database that is encrypted with the default AWS managed AWS KMS key. The company must implement a solution to rotate the database encryption key every 180 days. The solution must provide a notification if the encryption key is noncompliant with this standard. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Configure the rotation period for the existing AWS managed KMS key to be 180 days. Implement the cmk-backing-key-rotation-enabled AWS Config managed rule for the existing KMS key. Configure AWS Config to use Amazon SNS to notify the security team if key rotation is noncompliant.

Create a new AWS managed KMS key with automatic rotation set for 180 days. Take a snapshot of the database. Restore the snapshot to a new Aurora cluster that uses the new KMS key. Create an AWS Config custom rule that uses an AWS Lambda function to validate the key rotation period. Configure AWS Config to use Amazon SES to notify the security team if key encryption is noncompliant.

Create a new customer managed KMS key with automatic rotation set for 180 days. Take asnapshot of the database. Restore the snapshot to a new Aurora cluster that uses the new KMS key. Create an AWS Config custom rule that uses an AWS Lambda function to validate the key rotation period. Configure AWS Config to use Amazon SNS to notify the security team if key encryption is noncompliant.

Create a new customer managed KMS key with automatic rotation set for 180 days. Update the database to use the new KMS key for encryption. Implement the cmk-backing- key-rotation-enabled AWS Config managed rule for the new KMS key. Configure AWS Config to use Amazon SES to notify the security team if key rotation is noncompliant.

stem: A solutions architect has implemented a SAML 2 0 federated identity solution with their company's on-premises identity provider (IdP) to authenticate users' access to the AWS environment. When the solutions architect tests authentication through the federated identity web portal, access to the AWS environment is granted However when test users attempt to authenticate through the federated identity web portal, they are not able to access the AWS environment Which items should the solutions architect check to ensure identity federation isproperly configured? (Select THREE)

options.text: The 1AM user's permissions policy has allowed the use of SAML federation for that user
The 1AM roles created for the federated users' or federated groups' trust policy have set the SAML provider as the principal
Test users are not in the AWSFederatedUsers group in the company's IdP
The web portal calls the AWS STS AssumeRoleWithSAML API with the ARN of the SAML provider, the ARN of the 1AM role, and the SAML assertion from IdP
The on-premises IdP's DNS hostname is reachable from the AWS environment VPCs
The company's IdP defines SAML assertions that properly map users or groups in the company to 1AM roles with appropriate permissions

explanation: B,D,F verified against IAM SAML federation documentation. B IAM role trust policy must trust the same-account SAML provider as Federated Principal and permit sts:AssumeRoleWithSAML, normally with saml:aud condition. D API-based federation exchanges signed assertion plus RoleArn and PrincipalArn using STS AssumeRoleWithSAML; console SAML SSO may instead POST to AWS sign-in endpoint, so portal need not literally call API. F IdP must emit correctly mapped Role/RoleSessionName assertions to IAM role/provider ARNs and user/group authorization.
wrongOptionsExplanation: A wrong: SAML federated users assume IAM roles; no per-person IAM user permission policy required. B correct: role trust policy references federated SAML provider ARN and sts:AssumeRoleWithSAML action. C wrong as universal rule: AWSFederatedUsers is not an AWS-required group, although an enterprise-specific IdP group assignment might be relevant if actually configured. D correct for STS API federation; console federation can use browser redirect/POST to AWS sign-in SAML endpoint. E wrong: user browser/IdP and AWS sign-in endpoint handle federation; IdP DNS need not be reachable from arbitrary VPCs. F correct: IdP assertion must map authorized users/groups to valid role ARN and SAML provider ARN, with appropriate role permissions.
plainWords: If an admin can sign in to AWS through company SSO but ordinary users cannot, check the IAM role trust, the SAML assertion and role/group mapping, and the STS or AWS sign-in federation flow. You do not need an IAM user per employee or VPC access to the company IdP.
keyPoints: SAML federation: IdP signs assertion -> role/provider ARNs -> role trust Federated principal plus sts:AssumeRoleWithSAML and saml:aud -> temporary role credentials. IAM user policies do not gate federation. Role trust and role permission policies are different. IAM Identity Center is modern workforce access option but IAM SAML federation remains supported. Console SAML POST may bypass a direct web portal STS call. Test group membership, attribute claims, NameID/RoleSessionName, audience, expiry and clock skew.
sourceWarning: Original source has OCR corruption ('1AM','SAML 2 0','isproperly') and no punctuation; snapshot preserved. D is phrased as if every portal must call STS, but console SAML federation can post to AWS sign-in instead. C names a nonstandard IdP group and cannot be assumed required. Older SAP-C01 variant keys a group-membership distractor incorrectly; answer letters reorder across sites. No deprecated IAM SAML service.

review.externalVariantStatus: multiple exact reordered SAP-C02 variants B,D,F conceptually; older SAP-C01 source wrongly favors fixed group choice

stem: A company has many separate AWS accounts and uses no central billing or management. Each AWS account hosts services for different departments in the company. The company has a Microsoft Azure Active Directory that is deployed. A solution architect needs to centralize billing and management of the company’s AWS accounts. The company wants to start using identify federation instead of manual user management. The company also wants to use temporary credentials instead of long-lived access keys. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Select THREE)

options.text: Create a new AWS account to serve as a management account. Deploy an organization in AWS Organizations. Invite each existing AWS account to join the organization. Ensure that each account accepts the invitation.
Configure each AWS Account’s email address to be aws+<account id>@example.com so that account management email messages and invoices are sent to the same place.

Deploy AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On) in the management account. Connect IAM Identity Center to the Azure Active Directory. Configure IAM Identity Center for automatic synchronization of users and groups.
Deploy an AWS Managed Microsoft AD directory in the management account. Share the directory with all other accounts in the organization by using AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM).
Create AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On) permission sets. Attach the permission sets to the appropriate IAM Identity Center groups and AWS accounts.
Configure AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) in each AWS account to use AWS Managed Microsoft AD for authentication and authorization.

stem: A company is building an application on AWS. The application sends logs to an Amazon OpenSearch Service cluster for analysis. All data must be stored within a VPC. Some of the company's developers work from home. Other developers work from three different company office locations. The developers need to access OpenSearch Service to analyze and visualize logs directly from their local development machines. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Configure and set up an AWS Client VPN endpoint. Associate the Client VPN endpoint with a subnet in the VPC. Configure a Client VPN self-service portal. Instruct the developers to connect by using the client for Client VPN.
Create a transit gateway, and connect it to the VPC. Create an AWS Site-to-Site VPN. Create an attachment to the transit gateway. Instruct the developers to connect by using an OpenVPN client.

Create a transit gateway, and connect it to the VPC. Order an AWS Direct Connect connection. Set up a public VIF on the Direct Connect connection. Associate the public VIF with the transit gateway. Instruct the developers to connect to the Direct Connect connection.

Create and configure a bastion host in a public subnet of the VPC. Configure the bastion host security group to allow SSH access from the company CIDR ranges. Instruct the developers to connect by using SSH.

stem: A large payroll company recently merged with a small staffing company. The unified company now has multiple business units, each with its own existing AWS account. A solutions architect must ensure that the company can centrally manage the billing and access policies for all the AWS accounts. The solutions architect configures AWS Organizations by sending an invitation to all member accounts of the company from a centralized management account. What should the solutions architect do next to meet these requirements?

options.text: Create the OrganizationAccountAccess IAM group in each member account. Include the necessary IAM roles for each administrator.
Create the OrganizationAccountAccessPoIicy IAM policy in each member account. Connect the member accounts to the management account by using cross-account access.
Create the OrganizationAccountAccessRoIe IAM role in each member account. Grant permission to the management account to assume the IAM role.

Create the OrganizationAccountAccessRoIe IAM role in the management account. Attach the AdministratorAccess AWS managed policy to the IAM role.Assign the IAM role to the administrators in each member account.

stem: A company has developed a mobile game. The backend for the game runs on several virtual machines located in an on-premises data center. The business logic is exposed using a REST API with multiple functions. Player session data is stored in central file storage. Backend services use different API keys for throttling and to distinguish between live and test traffic. The load on the game backend varies throughout the day. During peak hours, the server capacity is not sufficient. There are also latency issues when fetching player session data. Management has asked a solutions architect to present a cloud architecture that can handle the game's varying load and provide low-latency data access. The API model should not be changed. Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Implement the REST API using a Network Load Balancer (NLB). Run the business logic on an Amazon EC2 instance behind the NLB. Store player session data in Amazon Aurora Serverless.
Implement the REST API using an Application Load Balancer (ALB). Run the business logic in AWS Lambda. Store player session data in Amazon DynamoDB with on-demand capacity.
Implement the REST API using Amazon API Gateway. Run the business logic in AWS Lambda. Store player session data in Amazon DynamoDB with on- demand capacity.
Implement the REST API using AWS AppSync. Run the business logic in AWS Lambda. Store player session data in Amazon Aurora Serverless.

explanation: C is correct. API Gateway REST APIs preserve the existing REST model and support API keys, usage plans, API stages and per-client throttling/quota targets. Lambda scales stateless business logic with variable traffic. DynamoDB on-demand is appropriate for unpredictable game-session read/write throughput and low-latency keyed access. An exact-stem third-party SAP-C02 practice PDF identifies C. API keys identify clients for usage-plan metering, NOT authentication or authorization; throttling is best-effort, not a hard limit.
wrongOptionsExplanation: A: NLB is a layer-4 load balancer without API Gateway REST usage plans/API keys, and a single EC2 instance does not inherently handle peak variability; Aurora Serverless is not the most direct key-value session store. B: ALB supports HTTP and Lambda targets, and DynamoDB is suitable, but ALB lacks API Gateway's built-in API-key usage plans and API stages for live/test traffic management. C: Correct: REST API Gateway with stages, API keys and throttling, Lambda elastic compute, DynamoDB on-demand low-latency session store. D: AppSync focuses on GraphQL and managed real-time APIs rather than preserving the specified REST API model; Aurora Serverless does not address API Gateway-style API-key throttling.
plainWords: Keep REST endpoints in API Gateway, execute game logic with Lambda, and store player sessions in DynamoDB on-demand. Separate live/test stages and usage plans.
keyPoints: API Gateway REST API = stages + API keys + usage plans + throttling. Lambda = serverless elastic execution. DynamoDB on-demand = variable throughput and low-latency key-value access. ALB is not equivalent to API Gateway usage plans. AppSync is not a drop-in REST API replacement. API keys are not authorization and usage-plan limits are best effort.
sourceWarning: LOW/MODERATE IMPLEMENTATION CAVEAT: The stem does not explicitly say the API keys are used for authentication; do not use them as authorization. Configure Cognito/IAM/Lambda authorizer as appropriate. Usage-plan throttling/quotas are best effort, not hard security or spend controls. No substantiated Choose TWO/THREE variant found in checked sources; exact-stem third-party PDF keys C.

review.notes: Domain 4 78/139. Q381 skipped (Choose THREE). Exact-stem external SAP-C02 PDF page 83, question 67, keys C; no verified multi-answer variant. API Gateway REST API keys and usage plans distinguish C from B; API keys are not auth.

stem: A company is planning to migrate its on-premises data analysis application to AWS. The application is hosted across a fleet of servers and requires consistent system time. The company has established an AWS Direct Connect connection from its on-premises data center to AWS. The company has a high-precision stratum-0 atomic clock network appliance that acts as an NTP source for all on-premises servers. After the migration to AWS is complete, the clock on all Amazon EC2 instances that host the application must be synchronized with the on-premises atomic clock network appliance. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST administrative overhead?

options.text: Configure a DHCP options set with the on-premises NTP server address. Assign the options set to the VPC. Ensure that NTP traffic is allowed between AWS and the on- premises networks.
Create a custom AMI to use the Amazon Time Sync Service at 169.254.169.123. Use this AMI for the application. Use AWS Config to audit the NTP configuration.

Deploy a third-party time server from the AWS Marketplace. Configure the time server to synchronize with the on-premises atomic clock network appliance. Ensure that NTP traffic is allowed inbound in the network ACLs for the VPC that contains the third-party server.

Create an IPsec VPN tunnel from the on-premises atomic clock network appliance to the VPC to encrypt the traffic over the Direct Connect connection. Configure the VPC route tables to direct NTP traffic over the tunnel.

explanation: A is the best single answer. A VPC DHCP options set supports the ntp-servers parameter for custom NTP server IP addresses. Associate the option set with the VPC, ensure the on-premises NTP server is reachable over existing Direct Connect and UDP/123 is permitted, and confirm the EC2 guest time synchronization client consumes the DHCP-provided NTP setting. This centralizes the configuration without extra servers or tunnels. AWS official VPC documentation explicitly supports custom NTP servers and association with the VPC.
wrongOptionsExplanation: A: Correct, subject to operating-system DHCP/NTP-client support and network reachability. B: Amazon Time Sync Service at 169.254.169.123 is a different clock source; it does not synchronize the instances specifically to the required on-premises atomic clock. C: A third-party relay adds an EC2/server appliance to operate and is unnecessary when clients can reach the on-prem NTP service directly; NACL ingress alone also does not ensure the full bidirectional path. D: An IPsec VPN is unnecessary for ordinary NTP connectivity when Direct Connect and routing already exist, and merely adding a VPN does not configure the EC2 clocks to use the atomic source.
plainWords: Set the on-premises NTP appliance address in the VPC DHCP options and let EC2 instances obtain that time-server setting, using Direct Connect for connectivity.
keyPoints: VPC DHCP options can specify ntp-servers; one option set per VPC. Direct Connect provides private connectivity but requires routes and UDP/123 access. Amazon Time Sync Service 169.254.169.123 is NOT the same as the required on-prem atomic clock. Confirm guest chrony/ntpd/Windows Time actually uses DHCP-provided NTP. Stratum-0 refers to a reference clock, with its NTP-serving appliance typically stratum-1.
sourceWarning: MODERATE: DHCP-provided NTP server settings do not guarantee every AMI/OS time client automatically adopts them; verify and adjust chrony, systemd-timesyncd, or Windows Time if necessary, and remove any overriding default Amazon Time Sync configuration. Also the phrase 'stratum-0 atomic clock network appliance acts as an NTP source' is imprecise: the atomic reference is stratum-0, while the attached NTP server is normally stratum-1. External exact-stem Choose TWO/THREE variants not independently established.

review.notes: Domain 4 79/139. AWS primary documentation validates custom ntp-servers in VPC DHCP option sets. No independently confirmed exact-stem external exam copy or Choose TWO/THREE variant; flag verification limitation. OS-specific NTP client adoption and stratum-0 phrasing caveats.

stem: A company hosts a read-heavy web application on Amazon EKS and Amazon DynamoDB. The company uses Amazon Route 53 as its DNS solution. The application serves hundreds of users during peak usage periods. Most users are in the United States, but the application is experiencing growing usage in Europe and the Middle East. The company needs to reduce application latency for all global users. Which solution will meet this requirement?

stem: A company is planning to migrate an on-premises data center to AWS. The company currently hosts the data center on Linux-based VMware VMs. A solutions architect must collect information about network dependencies between the VMs. The information must be in the form of a diagram that details host IP addresses, hostnames, and network connection information. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Use AWS Application Discovery Service. Select an AWS Migration Hub home AWS Region. Install the AWS Application Discovery Agent on the on-premises servers for data collection. Grant permissions to Application Discovery Service to use the Migration Hub network diagrams.
Use the AWS Application Discovery Service Agentless Collector for server data collection. Export the network diagrams from the AWS Migration Hub in .png format.
Install the AWS Application Migration Service agent on the on-premises servers for data collection. Use AWS Migration Hub data in Workload Discovery on AWS to generate network diagrams.

Install the AWS Application Migration Service agent on the on-premises servers for data collection. Export data from AWS Migration Hub in .csv format into an Amazon CloudWatch dashboard to generate network diagrams.

explanation: A is the documented historical exam answer. AWS Application Discovery Service Discovery Agent running on Linux VMware guests collects detailed server and network connection data; AWS Migration Hub's network diagram visualizes hostnames, IPs and server dependencies. The official Migration Hub network diagram prerequisites specifically require Discovery Agent on mapped servers and access to discovery:GetNetworkConnectionGraph. Select a Migration Hub home Region, deploy agents, collect data, and view the graph. Caveat: Migration Hub became unavailable to new customers in November 2025; do not present this as a universal 2026 greenfield solution.
wrongOptionsExplanation: A: Correct historical choice: Discovery Agent and Migration Hub network diagram meet the dependency mapping requirement. B: Agentless Collector gained network-connection discovery in November 2024, so its premise is no longer inherently wrong; however, the specified direct PNG export of the Migration Hub network diagram is not established by the official workflow, and the network diagram documentation calls for Discovery Agent. C: Application Migration Service replication agent is for server migration, not Application Discovery Service network graph discovery; Workload Discovery does not correct that mismatch. D: CloudWatch dashboards do not transform a CSV export from Migration Hub into the specified server connection topology diagram.
plainWords: Install AWS Application Discovery Agents on the Linux VMs, enable Migration Hub network diagram permissions, and inspect the server-to-server dependency map.
keyPoints: Discovery Agent collects processes and network connections; Migration Hub network diagram visualizes hostnames/IP addresses/dependencies; IAM permission discovery:GetNetworkConnectionGraph. AWS recommends 2–6 weeks of discovery. Agentless Collector added network connection discovery in November 2024, but the option's PNG export remains unsupported. Migration Hub access for new customers changed November 2025.
sourceWarning: HIGH — HISTORICAL/OUTDATED-SERVICE: AWS Migration Hub closed to new customers on November 7, 2025; the original exam workflow is not a universal current new-customer recommendation. Also Agentless Collector gained network-connection discovery November 8, 2024, making B's discovery premise viable, though its PNG-export claim is not documented. The Migration Hub diagram prerequisites still explicitly require Discovery Agent. Exact-stem exam copies checked are single-answer; no verified Choose TWO/THREE variant.

review.notes: Domain 4 80/139. Exact stem found at ExamCollection question 89 and ExamTopics discussion question 423, both single-choice. No confirmed Choose TWO/THREE variant. Historical A documented by Migration Hub network diagram prerequisites; flag agentless 2024 change and Migration Hub 2025 new-customer closure.

stem: A company generates approximately 20 GB of data multiple times each day. The company uses AWS DataSync to copy all data from on-premises storage to Amazon S3 every 6 hours for further processing. The analytics team wants to modify the copy process to copy only data relevant to the analytics team and ignore the rest of the data. The team wants to copy data as soon as possible and receive a notification when the copy process is finished. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively? (Select THREE.)

options.text: Modify the data generation process on premises to create a manifest file at the end of the copy process with the names of the objects to be copied to Amazon S3. Create a custom script to upload the manifest file to an S3 bucket.

Modify the data generation process on premises to create a manifest file at the end of the copy process with the names of the objects to be copied to Amazon S3. Create an AWS Lambda function to load the manifest file data into an Amazon DynamoDB table.

Create an AWS Lambda function that Amazon EventBridge invokes when the manifest file is loaded into Amazon DynamoDB. Configure the Lambda function to copy the data from on-premises storage to the S3 bucket that uses the manifest file.

Create an AWS Lambda function that an S3 Event Notification invokes when the manifest file is uploaded. Configure the Lambda function to invoke the DataSync task by calling the StartTaskExecution API action with a manifest.
Create an Amazon SNS topic. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to send an email notification to the SNS topic when the DataSync task execution status changes to SUCCESS or to ERROR.
Create an Amazon SNS topic. Create an AWS Lambda function to send an email notification to the SNS topic when the DataSync task execution status changes to SUCCESS or to ERROR.

explanation: A,D,E confirmed by AWS docs and multiple exact external variants. A create S3-hosted CSV manifest listing only analytics files. D S3 ObjectCreated event invokes Lambda, which calls DataSync StartTaskExecution with ManifestConfig Source S3 (bucket ARN, object path, access role), triggering transfers when manifest is ready rather than every 6 hours. E EventBridge DataSync Task Execution State Change SUCCESS/ERROR directly targets SNS topic with confirmed email subscription, avoiding custom polling and code.
wrongOptionsExplanation: A correct: manifest limits DataSync scanning and transfers to listed source-relative paths. B wrong: DynamoDB intermediary unnecessary because DataSync natively reads S3 manifest. C wrong: Lambda custom file transfer and DynamoDB trigger increase complexity and Lambda duration limits. D correct: S3 event -> Lambda -> StartTaskExecution ManifestConfig; requires iam:PassRole and permission to start task. E correct: EventBridge filters aws.datasync Task Execution State Change status SUCCESS/ERROR, SNS email target. F wrong: extra Lambda notification handler is unnecessary; EventBridge can directly target SNS.
plainWords: Write a CSV list of only the files analytics needs, upload it to S3, start the existing DataSync task immediately when the list arrives, and use EventBridge plus SNS to email the team when transfer succeeds or fails.
keyPoints: DataSync S3 manifest CSV specifies files, not a DynamoDB table; StartTaskExecution supports ManifestConfig. S3 ObjectCreated -> Lambda -> DataSync for event-driven execution. DataSync -> EventBridge Task Execution State Change SUCCESS/ERROR -> SNS email subscription. EventBridge events best effort; task only one execution active at a time; handle overlap/retries. Manifest IAM access and iam:PassRole; do not mix manifest with include/exclude filters. Enhanced mode now supports on-prem NFS/SMB via Enhanced agent; verify current supported sources and pricing.
sourceWarning: Minor ambiguity: A says 'at the end of the copy process' although manifest must be generated at end of source data generation, before DataSync copying; otherwise circular. S3 notification is at-least-once, can duplicate and arrive out of order; add idempotency and task execution concurrency handling. E says SNS topic 'sends an email' but SNS needs an email subscription and confirmation. DataSync EventBridge delivery is best effort; add monitoring if strict notification guarantee. Most cost-effective depends on data selection patterns; native filters may be simpler for fixed prefixes.
