stem: A company wants to migrate its website to AWS. The website uses microservices and runs on containers that are deployed in an on-premises, self-managed Kubernetes cluster. All the manifests that define the deployments for the containers in the Kubernetes deployment are in source control. All data for the website is stored in a PostgreSQL database. An open source container image repository runs alongside the on-premises environment. A solutions architect needs to determine the architecture that the company will use for the website on AWS. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST effort to migrate?

options.text: Create an AWS App Runner service. Connect the App Runner service to the open source container image repository. Deploy the manifests from on premises to the App Runner service. Create an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL database.

Create an Amazon EKS cluster that has managed node groups. Copy the application containers to a new Amazon ECR repository. Deploy the manifests from on premises to the EKS cluster. Create an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL DB cluster.

Create an Amazon ECS cluster that has an Amazon EC2 capacity pool. Copy the application containers to a new Amazon ECR repository. Register each container image as a new task definition. Configure ECS services for each task definition to match the original Kubernetes deployments. Create an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL DB cluster.

Rebuild the on-premises Kubernetes cluster by hosting the cluster on Amazon EC2 instances. Migrate the open source container image repository to the EC2 instances. Deploy the manifests from on premises to the new cluster on AWS. Deploy an open source PostgreSQL database on the new cluster.

explanation: B is correct. Amazon EKS is managed Kubernetes and supports reusing Kubernetes manifests from the existing cluster, while EKS managed node groups reduce infrastructure management. Amazon ECR provides managed image registry, and Aurora PostgreSQL is PostgreSQL-compatible managed relational storage. Compared with App Runner/ECS conversions or rebuilding Kubernetes and PostgreSQL on EC2, this requires the least replatforming effort among the choices. AWS: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/what-is-eks.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/managed-node-groups.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Aurora.AuroraPostgreSQL.html .
wrongOptionsExplanation: A: App Runner does not deploy Kubernetes manifest files directly; it deploys source code or supported container images, and connecting an arbitrary open-source image repository is not equivalent to an ECR-supported image source. B: Correct; managed EKS retains Kubernetes orchestration and can reuse manifests; Aurora PostgreSQL preserves relational engine compatibility. C: ECS requires translating Kubernetes deployments into ECS task definitions and services, creating more migration work. D: Self-managed Kubernetes, registry, and PostgreSQL on EC2 preserve much of the platform but add operational setup and management compared with EKS and Aurora.
plainWords: Already using Kubernetes? Move to managed Kubernetes (EKS), reuse deployment YAML, put images in ECR, and move PostgreSQL to Aurora PostgreSQL.
keyPoints: Kubernetes manifests + least migration effort -> EKS; managed node groups reduce EC2 node operations; ECR stores container images; Aurora PostgreSQL offers PostgreSQL-compatible managed database. EKS may still need manifest adjustments for ingress, storage, networking, IAM and secrets. Database migration still requires schema/extension compatibility and data migration planning.
sourceWarning: Answer B verified against AWS architecture documentation; Q377 is related but not an exact duplicate. Caveat: Aurora PostgreSQL compatibility is not perfect for all PostgreSQL extensions/versions; Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL might also work but is not paired with EKS in choices. Existing Kubernetes manifests may require modifications for AWS networking/storage. stem: A company is deploying a third-party web application to an AWS account. The company wants to deploy the application across multiple Amazon EC2 instances. The company must have the ability to scale horizontally when necessary. The application uses browser cookies for session state management. The application requires session affinity. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Assign each EC2 instance a public IP address. Configure an Amazon Route 53 multivalue A record for the application. Enable health checks for the A record. Configure a Route 53 Resolver rule that ensures a specific cookie value will consistently return the same EC2 instance. Access the application by using the Route 53 A record.

Place the EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. Configure an Amazon CloudFront distribution and set the Auto Scaling group as the origin. Create a CloudFront function to handle viewer requests. Include cookie processing logic to ensure that users are directed to the correct EC2 instance. Access the application by using the CloudFront distribution URL.

explanation: Correct D: use Amazon SES to send transactional acknowledgment email and store a reusable template in SES with customer-data placeholders. AWS Lambda supplies recipient and JSON template values to SES SendTemplatedEmail (SES v1), which renders and sends the personalized message without a self-managed SMTP server or custom S3 template merge. For a new application SES v2 SendEmail with Content.Template is the modern equivalent. Sources: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/boto3/latest/reference/services/ses/client/send_templated_email.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ses/latest/dg/send-personalized-email-api.html .
wrongOptionsExplanation: A: EC2-hosted SMTP server creates patching, monitoring and email deliverability operations; S3+Lambda template merging adds unnecessary custom code. B: SES is the right sender but S3-hosted templates and Lambda-side merging add work compared with SES-managed templates. C: SES templates are suitable, but the EC2 SMTP server is redundant and would not automatically integrate with SES template rendering as described. plainWords: Instead of running your own mail server, save an email template in SES, send the customer's name and case number from Lambda, and let SES fill the placeholders and send the email.
keyPoints: SES = managed transactional email; SES templates = placeholders and automatic personalization; SES v1 SendTemplatedEmail works but SES v2 SendEmail(Content.Template) is preferred for new implementations. SES verified identities, production access/sandbox status, sending limits, and rendering-failure notifications are practical requirements. S3 templates + Lambda custom merge can work but increase operational effort.
sourceWarning: Original stem OCR 'A3 part' should be 'As part'; option C missing space after 'data.'. stem: A company runs a workload in the AWS Cloud. The company stores data for the application in an older version of Amazon DocumentDB. Several backend services read and write data to the database continuously throughout all hours of the day. All services connect to the database by using the Amazon DocumentDB cluster endpoint, which is registered as a DNS record in Amazon Route 53. The company needs to upgrade the database to the latest version of Amazon DocumentDB without losing any data. The company must be able to test and verify the upgrade before the company allows backend services to use the upgraded version. The company has already enabled change streams and set a retention period of 24 hours. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Create a new Amazon DocumentDB cluster that runs the latest version. Use the Amazon DocumentDB Index Tool to export existing indexes and import them to the new cluster. Create a new AWS DMS instance and a source and target endpoint. Create a DMS task to migrate the data by using the Migrate and replicate migration type. Test and verify the new cluster. Update the Route 53 record to point to the new cluster.

Create a new Amazon DocumentDB cluster that runs the latest version. Install MongoDB command line interface (CLI) database tools on an Amazon EC2 instance. Use the MongoDB CLI to create a binary export, and import the data to the new Amazon DocumentDB cluster. Test and verify the new cluster. Update the Route 53 record to point to the new cluster.

Create a snapshot of the existing Amazon DocumentDB cluster. Perform an in-place major version upgrade. Modify the existing cluster to the latest version and the latest cluster parameter group. Apply modifications immediately. Test and verify the upgrade.

Create a new Amazon DocumentDB cluster that runs the latest version. Deploy the AWS DataSync agent to an Amazon EC2 instance and activate the agent. Create a new AWS DataSync task in enhanced mode. Start the transfer task to copy data to the new cluster. Test and verify the new cluster. Update the Route 53 record to point to the new cluster.

explanation: Correct A: Create a new DocumentDB cluster on the target engine version, migrate indexes using the Amazon DocumentDB Index Tool, then use AWS DMS 'Migrate and replicate' (full load plus CDC) from the old cluster. Change streams let DMS capture ongoing writes. Validate data and indexes and cut over Route 53 only after replication catches up. AWS explicitly documents this approach: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/documentdb/latest/devguide/docdb-migration.versions.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/userguide/CHAP_Source.DocumentDB.html .
wrongOptionsExplanation: A correct: parallel new cluster supports pre-cutover testing and ongoing replication. B: mongodump/mongorestore-style binary export/import is a static copy, without CDC, so continuous writes can be missed. C: in-place major upgrade is supported, but takes the production cluster offline and cannot provide isolated testing before backend services access the upgrade. D: AWS DataSync does not support Amazon DocumentDB as a database source/target or implement its change-stream CDC.
plainWords: Keep the old DocumentDB serving live traffic while AWS DMS copies all documents to a new upgraded cluster and continuously replays changes. Test the new cluster, briefly pause writes to eliminate lag, then switch DNS.
keyPoints: DocumentDB change streams + AWS DMS = CDC; 'Migrate and replicate' = full load and ongoing changes. Index Tool transfers index definitions; use target preparation 'Do nothing' to preserve indexes. Monitor CDCLatencyTarget, migration errors and change-stream retention (24h must cover full load). Before cutover pause writes, drain lag, validate, update Route 53 and handle DNS caching/old connections. DocumentDB 8.0 and in-place MVU exist, but in-place upgrade is disruptive and cannot meet independent pre-cutover verification.
sourceWarning: Verified exact-stem/options external practice variants: ExamCollection SAP-C02 page 3 and Certstopics SAP-C02; no confirmed Choose TWO/THREE variant. AWS official guide explicitly uses Index Tool plus DMS Migrate and replicate. Source option A omits write-quiesce/CDC catch-up, TTL, reconnection, validation and DMS target preparation safeguards; 24h change stream retention may be insufficient for very long full load. Option C is technically supported in-place upgrade but violates independent testing and availability requirements; AWS supports DocumentDB 8.0. Sources: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/documentdb/latest/devguide/docdb-migration.versions.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/documentdb/latest/devguide/docdb-mvu.html ; https://www.examcollection.us/exam/SAP-C02-question-answer-3.html ; https://www.certstopics.com/questions/sap-c02-vce-exam-download.html .

review.notes: AWS DocumentDB migration guide, DMS CDC docs and external exact-option practice sources checked. Single answer; no confirmed multi-answer variant. Cutover caveats documented.

stem: A solutions architect needs to assess a newly acquired company’s portfolio of applications and databases. The solutions architect must create a business case to migrate the portfolio to AWS. The newly acquired company runs applications in an on-premises data center. The data center is not well documented. The solutions architect cannot immediately determine how many applications and databases exist. Traffic for the applications is variable. Some applications are batch processes that run at the end of each month. The solutions architect must gain a better understanding of the portfolio before a migration to AWS can begin. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Use AWS Server Migration Service (AWS SMS) and AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to evaluate migration. Use AWS Service Catalog to understand application and database dependencies.

Use AWS Application Migration Service. Run agents on the on-premises infrastructure. Manage the agents by using AWS Migration Hub. Use AWS Storage Gateway to assess local storage needs and database dependencies.

Use Migration Evaluator to generate a list of servers. Build a report for a business case. Use AWS Migration Hub to view the portfolio. Use AWS Application Discovery Service to gain anunderstanding of application dependencies.

Use AWS Control Tower in the destination account to generate an application portfolio. Use AWS Server Migration Service (AWS SMS) to generate deeper reports and a business case. Use a landing zone for core accounts and resources.

explanation: Correct historical exam answer C. Migration Evaluator inventories on-premises infrastructure and utilization to generate a data-driven AWS migration business case; AWS Migration Hub historically supplied application portfolio visibility; AWS Application Discovery Service discovered infrastructure and application dependencies. Month-end batch jobs require monitoring across the complete monthly cycle, not just a short sample. AWS: https://aws.amazon.com/migration-evaluator/features/ ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/migration-tools/discovery-migration-evaluator.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/migrationhub/latest/ug/gs-new-user-discovery.html . NOTE: For new customers in 2026, AWS Application Discovery Service and Migration Hub are closed to new customers; AWS Transform is AWS's recommended alternative.
wrongOptionsExplanation: A: AWS SMS is retired (April 1, 2023); DMS migrates database data, not full estate assessment; Service Catalog manages approved products, not on-premises dependency discovery. B: Application Migration Service is for moving servers; Storage Gateway supplies hybrid storage access, not application/database dependency discovery. C: Best historical choice: Migration Evaluator for inventory, utilization and business case, Migration Hub for portfolio, ADS for dependencies. D: Control Tower provisions/governs AWS landing zones, not on-premises application discovery; AWS SMS is retired and not a business-case generator.
plainWords: Before moving an acquired company's unknown data center, first discover what servers and databases exist, measure a full monthly business cycle, map which applications talk to each other, and build a cost justification. In the original exam choose C; for new 2026 projects use AWS Transform for discovery instead of ADS/Migration Hub.
keyPoints: Discovery/assessment is different from migration execution. Migration Evaluator = business case, cost and right-sizing; ADS = historical dependency mapping; Migration Hub = historical portfolio visibility; AWS Transform = recommended 2026 alternative for new customers. Collect at least one month of utilization to capture end-of-month batch jobs. SMS reached end of support 2023-04-01. ADS and Migration Hub stopped accepting new customers 2025-11-07.
sourceWarning: OUTDATED 2026: Option C remains the intended historical answer but is not a fully viable greenfield solution because AWS Application Discovery Service and AWS Migration Hub closed to new customers November 7, 2025. AWS Transform is the recommended modern alternative. AWS SMS in A/D ended support April 1, 2023. Option C OCR typo 'anunderstanding' should be 'an understanding'. External exact-stem: Scribd SAP-C02 question 164 has answer C; scalar.usc.edu SAP-C02 question 208 reorders choices and calls identical solution D. No confirmed Choose TWO/THREE variant. References: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/application-discovery/latest/userguide/application-discovery-service-availability-change.html ; https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2025/10/aws-service-availability/ ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/full_shutdown_services.html ; https://aws.amazon.com/migration-evaluator/features/ ; https://www.scribd.com/document/1030319491/SAP-C02-Dg-Re-Vh8uyt ; https://scalar.usc.edu/works/race-and-migration-in-the-united-states-/pass-guaranteed-quiz-useful-amazon---exam-sap-c02-overviews .

review.notes: Exact stem externally verified in two sources with shuffled answer letters; AWS docs verify historical logic. ADS and Migration Hub closed to new customers in 2025; SMS retired 2023. Modern greenfield discovery: AWS Transform.

stem: A company is designing an AWS environment tor a manufacturing application. The application has been successful with customers, and the application's user base has increased. The company has connected the AWS environment to the company's on- premises data center through a 1 Gbps AWS Direct Connect connection. The company has configured BGP for the connection. The company must update the existing network connectivity solution to ensure that the solution is highly available, fault tolerant, and secure. Which solution win meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

options.text: Add a dynamic private IP AWS Site-to-Site VPN as a secondary path to secure data in transit and provide resilience for the Direct Conned connection. Configure MACsec to encrypt traffic inside the Direct Connect connection.

Provision another Direct Conned connection between the company's on-premises data center and AWS to increase the transfer speed and provide resilience. Configure MACsec to encrypt traffic inside the Dried Conned connection.
Configure multiple private VIFs. Load balance data across the VIFs between the on- premises data center and AWS to provide resilience.
Add a static AWS Site-to-Site VPN as a secondary path to secure data in transit and to provide resilience for the Direct Connect connection.

explanation: D is the best technically viable choice among these defective options: an AWS Site-to-Site IPsec VPN carried over an INDEPENDENT internet connection can provide lower-cost encrypted backup when the 1 Gbps Direct Connect fails. A statically routed VPN can be configured for backup, but requires careful routing/health/failover configuration; since BGP is already available, a dynamic BGP VPN would be preferred and is conspicuously missing from the options. AWS Direct Connect resiliency guidance recommends VPN backup for <=1 Gbps DX. https://aws.amazon.com/directconnect/resiliency-recommendation/ ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpn/latest/s2svpn/vpn-static-dynamic.html ; https://aws.amazon.com/directconnect/faqs/ .
wrongOptionsExplanation: A: INVALID despite source key. MACsec is supported only on 10/100/400 Gbps dedicated Direct Connect, not this 1 Gbps link. Private IP VPN runs over Direct Connect transit VIF/Transit Gateway and cannot survive loss of the underlying single DX physical link. B: Second DX can improve physical resilience but costs more, and MACsec is again unsupported on 1 Gbps; no independent end-to-end encryption as specified. C: Multiple private VIFs over one DX share the same physical failure domain and provide no inherent encryption. D: Best remaining option, provided Site-to-Site VPN uses independent public internet transport; static routes must be configured carefully and BGP dynamic VPN would be preferable.
plainWords: A VPN over the same Direct Connect wire dies when that wire dies. A VPN over a separate internet connection can keep the application connected. Also, you cannot enable Direct Connect MACsec on a 1 Gbps dedicated link.
keyPoints: MACsec dedicated DX supported speeds: 10/100/400 Gbps (not 1 Gbps). Private-IP Site-to-Site VPN over DX needs Transit Gateway and transit VIF, and does not create independent physical redundancy. Internet-based IPsec VPN is a cost-effective backup for <=1 Gbps DX. BGP-based dynamic routing is preferred for automatic failover; static VPN is possible but needs careful routing. Multiple VIFs do not equal multiple physical connections.
sourceWarning: DEFECTIVE ORIGINAL ANSWER KEY: Original A is technically impossible as written (MACsec unsupported on 1 Gbps DX), and private IP VPN over the same DX does not survive DX failure. External exact stem P2PExams PDF Q1 keys A and repeats this technical mistake; CertEnsure Q167 exact options, answer not independently confirmed. D is best feasible option if VPN is internet-based, but specifies static rather than recommended BGP routing, and independent internet transport is implicit rather than explicit. Therefore question is flawed; a dynamic public-IP VPN over independent internet is the better absent choice. No confirmed Choose TWO/THREE variant. OCR defects: 'tor' -> 'for', 'win' -> 'will', 'Direct Conned'/'Dried Conned' -> 'Direct Connect'. Sources: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/MACsec.html ; https://aws.amazon.com/vpn/faqs/ ; https://aws.amazon.com/directconnect/resiliency-recommendation/ ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpn/latest/s2svpn/vpn-static-dynamic.html ; https://www.p2pexams.com/free-questions/amazon-sap-c02-dumps-by-foster-09-08-2024-12qa-vceexamstest.pdf ; https://www.certensure.com/amazon-web-services/sap-c02-cert-practice-test.html .

review.notes: AWS MACsec prerequisites invalidate A/B on 1 Gbps; private-IP VPN over same DX is not independent resilience. External P2PExams repeats incorrect A. D best of listed options but static routing inferior to missing dynamic internet VPN choice.

stem: A company needs to optimize the infrastructure for an application that uploads data to Amazon S3. The uploads average 64 KB in size. options.text: Replace the ECS task with an AWS Lambda function for processing. Create S3 Lifecycle rules to move the S3 objects to S3 Intelligent-Tiering after 1 day and to expire the objects after 5 years. Configure DynamoDB Standard-Infrequent Access for the DynamoDB table.

Replace the S3 bucket with Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK) to receive the data. Configure tiered storage for data that is older than 1 day. Configure EventBridge to read messages from Amazon MSK in batches of 1,000 messages. Replace the ECS task with an AWS Lambda function for processing. Configure a TTL of 15 days on the DynamoDB table.

Create an Amazon Data Firehose stream to receive the data. Configure buffering to deliver messages every minute to Amazon S3 in gzip format. Purchase a Compute Savings Plan based on usage recommendations. Create S3 Lifecycle rules to move the S3 objects to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 1 day and to expire the objects after 5 years. Configure a TTL of 15 days on the DynamoDB table.

stem: A company uses AWS CloudFormation to deploy applications within multiple VPCs that are all attached to a transit gateway Each VPC that sends traffic to the public internet must send the traffic through a shared services VPC Each subnet within a VPC uses the default VPC route table and the traffic is routed to the transit gateway The transit gateway uses its default route table for any VPC attachment A security audit reveals that an Amazon EC2 instance that is deployed within a VPC can communicate with an EC2 instance that is deployed in any of the company's other VPCs A solutions architect needs to limit the traffic between the VPCs. stem: A company has a few AWS accounts for development and wants to move its production application to AWS. stem: A company needs to store and process image data that will be uploaded from mobile devices using a custom mobile app. Usage peaks between 8 AM and 5 PM on weekdays, with thousands of uploads per minute. stem: A company is preparing to deploy an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster for a workload. The company expects the cluster to support an unpredictable number of stateless pods. stem: A company wants to migrate to AWS. The company is running thousands of VMs in a VMware ESXi environment. The company has no configuration management database and has little Knowledge about the utilization of the VMware portfolio. A solutions architect must provide the company with an accurate inventory so that the company can plan for a cost-effective migration. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Use AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager to deploy Migration Evaluator to each VM. Review the collected data in Amazon QuickSight. Identify servers that have high utilization. Remove the servers that have high utilization from the migration list. Import the data to AWS Migration Hub.

Export the VMware portfolio to a csv file. Check the disk utilization for each server. Remove servers that have high utilization. Export the data to AWS Application Migration Service. Use AWS Server Migration Service (AWS SMS) to migrate the remaining servers.

Deploy the Migration Evaluator agentless collector to the ESXi hypervisor. Review the collected data in Migration Evaluator. Identify inactive servers. Remove the inactive servers from the migration list. Import the data to AWS Migration Hub.
Deploy the AWS Application Migration Service Agent to each VM. When the data is collected, use Amazon Redshift to import and analyze the data. Use Amazon QuickSight for data visualization.

explanation: Historical best answer C: Migration Evaluator's agentless collector inventories and measures large VMware estates without deploying software to each guest VM; identify inactive/underutilized systems and use inventory for cost-effective migration planning. IMPORTANT original wording is technically imprecise: AWS says deploy the Migration Evaluator collector on a separate Windows Server VM and collect from VMware vSphere APIs; do not install it 'to the ESXi hypervisor'. Migration Hub can historically track imported assets, but it stopped accepting new customers 2025-11-07. AWS Transform is the current alternative for new projects. https://aws.amazon.com/migration-evaluator/faqs/ ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/migrationhub/latest/ug/migrationhub-availability-change.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/transform/latest/userguide/transform-app-assessments.html .
wrongOptionsExplanation: A: Patch Manager patches managed nodes; it does not install a Migration Evaluator collector in each guest VM, and removing highly utilized servers is not a valid migration-assessment rule. B: Manual CSV/disk inspection is labor-intensive and incomplete, high utilization is not a reason to remove servers, and AWS SMS ended support April 1, 2023. C: Correct historical intent, agentless VMware estate inventory and utilization; wording should say separate Windows Server collector VM connecting to vCenter/vSphere, not install on ESXi. D: AWS Application Migration Service agent on every VM is for rehosting/replication, and Redshift+QuickSight are unnecessary for inventory assessment.
plainWords: There are thousands of unknown VMware servers. Instead of logging into each server or installing agents, deploy one agentless collection appliance/VM, connect it to VMware management, measure which servers actually run, and plan which ones to migrate, right-size, or retire.
keyPoints: Migration Evaluator = VMware inventory, utilization, right-sizing and cost case. Agentless collector uses separate Windows Server VM and VMware vSphere APIs; no agent on ESXi or each guest. AWS recommends 2–4 weeks for TCO and 2–6 weeks for migration planning. Inactive VMs are retirement candidates subject to owner verification, not automatic deletion. AWS Migration Hub stopped accepting new customers Nov 7 2025; AWS Transform migration assessments are the modern alternative. AWS SMS ended support Apr 1 2023.
sourceWarning: SOURCE WORDING DEFECT: Option C says 'Deploy the Migration Evaluator agentless collector to the ESXi hypervisor'; AWS official FAQ states collector is deployed as a separate Windows Server virtual machine, not installed on the hypervisor or each server. C remains intended and best historical answer, but not fully accurate as written. OUTDATED: AWS Migration Hub stopped accepting new customers 2025-11-07, AWS Transform recommended for new projects; AWS SMS in B retired 2023-04-01. Stem capitalization 'Knowledge' should be 'knowledge'. External exact-stem copies FreeCram question 101/264, Exam-Tests question 343, CertEnsure and Scribd all key C; no confirmed Choose TWO/THREE variant. review.notes: Official Migration Evaluator FAQ confirms separate Windows Server collector, not ESXi installation; Migration Hub new customer cutoff 2025-11-07, SMS end support 2023. External exact-stem sources key C; no confirmed multi-answer variant.

stem: A solutions architect is determining the DNS strategy for an existing VPC. The VPC is provisioned to use the 10.24.34.0/24 CIDR block. The VPC also uses Amazon Route 53 Resolver for DNS. stem: A company is using AWS to develop and manage its production web application. The application includes an Amazon API Gateway HTTP API that invokes an AWS Lambda function. stem: A company is migrating a legacy application from an on-premises data center to AWS. The application uses MongoDB as a key-value database According to the company's technical guidelines, all Amazon EC2 instances must be hosted in a private subnet without an internet connection. In addition, all connectivity between applications and databases must be encrypted. The database must be able to scale based on demand. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Create new Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility) tables for the application with Provisioned IOPS volumes. Use the instance endpoint to connect to Amazon DocumentDB.
Create new Amazon DynamoDB tables for the application with on-demand capacity. Use a gateway VPC endpoint for DynamoDB to connect to the DynamoDB tables
Create new Amazon DynamoDB tables for the application with on-demand capacity. Use an interface VPC endpoint for DynamoDB to connect to the DynamoDB tables.
Create new Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility) tables for the application with Provisioned IOPS volumes Use the cluster endpoint to connect to Amazon DocumentDB

explanation: Best literal option B, CONDITIONAL/AMBIGUOUS: DynamoDB on-demand automatically scales throughput and a DynamoDB gateway VPC endpoint allows same-VPC private-subnet EC2 clients to use DynamoDB over AWS network without NAT/IGW or endpoint hourly charges. DynamoDB SDK HTTPS/TLS encrypts traffic. But moving a legacy MongoDB app to DynamoDB is NOT API-compatible and requires data-model/code migration; question does not explicitly authorize this. C also technically satisfies privacy/encryption/scaling, but interface endpoint incurs additional charges and is unnecessary for same-VPC EC2. Neither DocumentDB option is valid as written because DocumentDB does not have 'tables with Provisioned IOPS volumes'. AWS: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/vpc-endpoints-ddb.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/on-demand-capacity-mode.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/documentdb/latest/devguide/how-it-works.html .
wrongOptionsExplanation: A: DocumentDB provides MongoDB compatibility but does not use 'tables with Provisioned IOPS volumes'; instance endpoint pins a single instance and is not generally recommended for failover. B: best literal answer if MongoDB-to-DynamoDB application/data model conversion is allowed; gateway endpoint has no extra charge and works for same-VPC clients, HTTPS/TLS encrypts, on-demand scales. C: technically also meets the explicit networking and scaling requirements; DynamoDB interface endpoint is supported, but adds cost and requires client endpoint configuration, so B is preferable only if minimizing cost/simplicity is an implicit criterion. D: cluster endpoint is preferable to instance endpoint for DocumentDB failover, and DocumentDB is MongoDB compatible, but 'DocumentDB tables with Provisioned IOPS volumes' is invalid; encryption-in-transit/TLS configuration is omitted.
plainWords: If you can rewrite the MongoDB application's data access for DynamoDB, use DynamoDB on-demand and a free gateway endpoint so private EC2 instances can connect securely without internet. If you must keep MongoDB compatibility, use a correctly configured Amazon DocumentDB cluster and TLS, but none of the DocumentDB options describes a valid storage setup.
keyPoints: DynamoDB gateway endpoint = free private access from same VPC without NAT/IGW; interface endpoint = supported PrivateLink with endpoint charges, useful for on-premises/peered/transit scenarios. DynamoDB on-demand scales throughput with workload; HTTPS/TLS encrypts API calls. Amazon DocumentDB is MongoDB-compatible, uses collections and managed cluster storage (standard/I/O-optimized), not tables on Provisioned IOPS EBS. DocumentDB cluster endpoint preferred for primary and failover; instance endpoint binds one instance. MongoDB -> DynamoDB requires application/data-model migration. Original answer A technically invalid; C is also feasible, so single-answer question is underspecified.
sourceWarning: DEFECTIVE/AMBIGUOUS: Original source key A is incorrect as written: DocumentDB has no 'tables with Provisioned IOPS volumes', and instance endpoint is poor default for HA. Changed answer to B as best literal, but C ALSO meets explicit requirements; B's superiority relies on unstated cost/simplicity preference. Both B/C require rewriting a MongoDB application to DynamoDB; if preserving MongoDB API is required, neither works and a corrected DocumentDB/TLS/cluster-endpoint option would be needed. External exact-stem FreeCram Q19/171, Exam-Tests Q318, ExamTopics Q890, Scribd Q252, Certsmania PDF all found; Certsmania keys A with incorrect claims that DocumentDB supports Provisioned IOPS and that cluster endpoint load balances replicas. No confirmed Choose TWO/THREE variant. Stem missing punctuation after 'database'. Sources: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/documentdb/latest/devguide/endpoints.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/documentdb/latest/devguide/how-it-works.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/vpc-endpoints-ddb.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/privatelink-interface-endpoints.html ; https://www.freecram.net/question/Amazon.SAP-C02.v2024-03-21.q171/a-company-is-migrating-a-legacy-application-from-an-on-premises-data-center-to-aws-the-application-uses ; https://www.exam-tests.com/SAP-C02-exam/Amazon.SAP-C02.v2025-02-24.q513.html?p=65 ; https://www.certsmania.com/pdf/amazon-web-servicesquestion-answer-preparation-changed-sap-c02-questions-by-frederic.pdf .

review.notes: B best literal if MongoDB migration allowed; C also technically valid, so no uniquely correct answer under explicit requirements. DocumentDB A/D have invalid Provisioned IOPS terminology; external Certsmania repeats A with inaccurate explanation. Recommend rewriting question rather than treating B as unqualified.

stem: A solutions architect is planning to migrate critical Microsoft SOL Server databases to AWS. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Use AWS Application Migration Service and the AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT). Perform an In-place upgrade before the migration. Export the migrated data to Amazon Aurora Serverless after cutover. Repoint the applications to Amazon Aurora.

Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to Rehost the database. Set Amazon S3 as a target. Set up change data capture (CDC) replication. When the source and destination are fully synchronized, load the data from Amazon S3 into an Amazon RDS for Microsoft SQL Server DB Instance.

Use native database high availability tools Connect the source system to an Amazon RDS for Microsoft SQL Server DB instance Configure replication accordingly. When data replication is finished, transition the workload to an Amazon RDS for Microsoft SQL Server DB instance.

Use AWS Application Migration Service. Rehost the database server on Amazon EC2. When data replication is finished, detach the database and move the database to an Amazon RDS for Microsoft SQL Server DB instance. Reattach the database and then cut over all networking.

explanation: Best answer C: use SQL Server native transactional replication with the source as publisher and Amazon RDS for SQL Server as a push subscriber. After initial synchronization, ongoing changes are applied to RDS; validate, briefly stop writes, let replication catch up and cut over. AWS explicitly recommends transactional replication for minimal-downtime migrations to RDS SQL Server: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/migration-sql-server/trans-rep.html . This is replatforming to managed RDS, not heterogeneous database engine modernization; stem is ambiguous about 'modern data architecture'.
wrongOptionsExplanation: A: AWS Application Migration Service rehosts servers; AWS SCT converts schemas, but an in-place upgrade and post-cutover export to Aurora Serverless do not create near-zero-downtime replication. B: AWS DMS CDC to S3 writes data/change files, not a continuously synchronized RDS SQL Server target; bulk-loading S3 afterward creates lag/downtime and requires replay. Use DMS directly to RDS for full-load+CDC instead. C: correct, native SQL Server transactional replication to RDS subscriber supports continuous sync and brief cutover, subject to edition/permissions/object support. D: Application Migration Service can rehost the VM to EC2, but managed RDS cannot accept detached SQL Server MDF/LDF database files for attachment as proposed.
plainWords: Keep the existing SQL Server running, copy its data to Amazon RDS for SQL Server, and continuously send changes using SQL Server transactional replication. Once RDS catches up, briefly stop writes and redirect applications. That avoids a long outage.
keyPoints: SQL Server transactional replication: source publisher/distributor, RDS SQL Server push subscriber, continuous changes, validation, drain replication lag, cutover. AWS DMS full load+CDC DIRECT to RDS is another supported near-zero downtime approach, but option B incorrectly uses S3 as intermediate CDC destination. S3 native SQL Server backup/restore is different from DMS S3 CDC CSV/Parquet files. RDS SQL Server is replatform, not conversion to Aurora. DMS Schema Conversion/SCT + DMS full-load+CDC to Aurora PostgreSQL would better represent heterogeneous modernization.
sourceWarning: SOURCE KEY DEFECT: original B uses AWS DMS with S3 CDC target then loads S3 data into RDS SQL Server only after sync; target RDS is not continuously synchronized, and S3 DMS CDC files are not SQL Server native backup files. Corrected to C, independently supported by AWS Prescriptive Guidance SQL Server transactional replication. Exact stem on CertifHub Q7 with reordered choices keys C for native replication (dataset C); no confirmed Choose TWO/THREE variant. STEM DEFECT: 'Microsoft SOL Server' OCR should be 'Microsoft SQL Server'; 'modern data architecture' ambiguous because RDS SQL Server is managed replatforming rather than heterogeneous engine modernization. Option C uses vague 'high availability tools'; transactional replication specifically, not generic Always On availability groups, is the supported technique. References: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/migration-sql-server/trans-rep.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/userguide/CHAP_Target.S3.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/migration-sql-server/methods.html ; https://blog.certifhub.com/aws/aws-certified-solutions-architect-professional-english/q7/ .

review.notes: Official AWS Prescriptive Guidance explicitly supports native SQL Server transactional replication into RDS with minimal downtime; external exact-stem CertifHub Q7 independently keys equivalent option C. DMS CDC to S3 followed by RDS load is not synchronized RDS target. Stem modernization ambiguous.

stem: A multinational media company is building a video processing platform on AWS. The platform is deployed across multiple AWS accounts in an organization in AWS Organizations. options.text: Deploy separate EU and non-EU processing stacks by using API Gateway and Lambda. Use Amazon Route 53 geolocation routing to send EU uploads to EU endpoints. options.text: Disable source'destination checks on the EC2 instances that run the proxy software

As usage increased, Lambda durations increased and DynamoDB PUTs failed with ProvisionedThroughputExceededException. Lambda also experiences TooManyRequestsException errors. options.text: Increase the write capacity units to the DynamoDB table.

options.text: Use logical cross-Region replication to replicate the Aurora MySQL database to a secondary Region. Replace the web servers with Amazon S3. Deploy S3 buckets in cross- Region replication mode.
Ensure the web and application tiers are each in Auto Scaling groups. Introduce an AWS Direct Connect connection. Deploy the web and application tiers in Regions across the world.

stem: A company runs a processing engine in the AWS Cloud The engine processes environmental data from logistics centers to calculate a sustainability index The company has millions of devices in logistics centers that are spread across Europe The devices send information to the processing engine through a RESTful API The API experiences unpredictable bursts of traffic The company must implement a solution to process all data that the devices send to the processing engine Data loss is unacceptable Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Create an Application Load Balancer (ALB) for the RESTful API Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue Create a listener and a target group for the ALB Add the SQS queue as the target Use a container that runs in Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with the Fargate launch type to process messages in the queue

Create an Amazon API Gateway REST API that implements the RESTful API Create a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group Create an API Gateway Auto Scaling group proxy integration Use the EC2 instances to process incoming data

Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution for the RESTful API Create a data stream in Amazon Kinesis Data Streams Set the data stream as the origin for the distribution Create an AWS Lambda function to consume and process data in the data stream

explanation: ALB target groups do not support SQS; API Gateway HTTP API SQS integration buffers bursts and Lambda consumes messages.
wrongOptionsExplanation: A invalid: SQS cannot be ALB target. B correct: HTTP API to SQS integration and Lambda queue consumer. C invalid: API Gateway has no direct Auto Scaling group proxy integration. D invalid: Kinesis stream is not a CloudFront origin.
plainWords: ALB target groups do not support SQS; API Gateway HTTP API SQS integration buffers bursts and Lambda consumes messages.

stem: A company has a web application that uses Amazon API Gateway. AWS Lambda and Amazon DynamoDB A recent marketing campaign has increased demand Monitoring software reports that many requests have significantly longer response times than before the marketing campaign A solutions architect enabled Amazon CloudWatch Logs for API Gateway and noticed that errors are occurring on 20% of the requests. stem: A company uses infrastructure as code (IaC) to provision Amazon EC2 instances. The company uses a launch template to implement an EC2 Auto Scaling group to manage traffic increases. options.text: Configure the Auto Scaling group termination policy to use the OldestLaunchTemplate setting.

stem: A company's solutions architect is analyzing costs of a multi-application environment. The environment is deployed across multiple Availability Zones in a single AWS Region. stem: A company uses a service to collect metadata from applications that the company hosts on premises. Consumer devices such as TVs and internet radios access the applications. Many older devices do not support certain HTTP headers and exhibit errors when these headers are present in responses. The company has configured an on-premises load balancer to remove the unsupported headers from responses sent to older devices, which the company identified by the User-Agent headers. The company wants to migrate the service to AWS, adopt serverless technologies, and retain the ability to support the older devices. The company has already migrated the applications into a set of AWS Lambda functions. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution for the metadata service. Create an Application Load Balancer (ALB). Configure the CloudFront distribution to forward requests to the ALB. Configure the ALB to invoke the correct Lambda function for each type of request. Create a CloudFront function to remove the problematic headers based on the value of the User-Agent header.

Create an Amazon API Gateway REST API for the metadata service. Configure API Gateway to invoke the correct Lambda function for each type of request. Modify the default gateway responses to remove the problematic headers based on the value of the User- Agent header.

Create an Amazon API Gateway HTTP API for the metadata service. Configure API Gateway to invoke the correct Lambda function for each type of request. Create a response mapping template to remove the problematic headers based on the value of the User-Agent. Associate the response data mapping with the HTTP API.

Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution for the metadata service. Create an Application Load Balancer (ALB). Configure the CloudFront distribution to forward requests to the ALB. Configure the ALB to invoke the correct Lambda function for each type of request. Create a Lambda@Edge function that will remove the problematic headers in response to viewer requests based on the value of the User-Agent header.

explanation: Best current design A, CONDITIONAL: configure the CloudFront Function explicitly on the VIEWER-RESPONSE event (not viewer-request). CloudFront Functions viewer-response event contains both event.request.headers['user-agent'] and event.response.headers, enabling conditional removal of unsupported response headers for legacy clients. CloudFront -> ALB -> Lambda target groups supports existing Lambda functions. AWS explicitly documents using request properties to modify viewer response: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/function-code-choose-purpose.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/functions-event-structure.html . Original A omits event trigger, and D is ambiguous ('in response to viewer requests') so the question is NOT a uniquely valid single-answer item; Lambda@Edge at viewer-response also works.
wrongOptionsExplanation: A: best simple supported option when CloudFront Function is configured for viewer-response. The function can read request User-Agent and remove response headers. B: API Gateway REST default gateway responses control API Gateway-generated errors, not all successful Lambda integration responses. C: HTTP API supports response PARAMETER mappings, not VTL response mapping templates; no specified supported User-Agent-based conditional header removal. D: if 'in response to viewer requests' means a Lambda@Edge VIEWER-REQUEST trigger, impossible to modify origin response headers at that stage. If intended as viewer-response triggered for each viewer request, D is ALSO technically valid; ambiguous wording creates a defective question.
plainWords: An old TV tells the server its device type using User-Agent. CloudFront checks that User-Agent just before sending the reply and deletes the header the old TV cannot understand. This must happen during a response event.
keyPoints: CloudFront Functions viewer-response: event.request and event.response both accessible; inspect User-Agent and delete response.headers['header-name']; lightweight/low latency. Lambda@Edge viewer-response can also read request headers and edit response. Viewer-request cannot edit an origin response not yet generated. API Gateway REST default gateway responses apply gateway-generated errors, not standard integration responses. API Gateway HTTP API response parameter mapping is not VTL mapping template. CloudFront response headers policy is unconditional per behavior, not per User-Agent without extra routing.
sourceWarning: AMBIGUOUS/DEFECTIVE ORIGINAL KEY D: Exact-stem FreeCram Q243/305 and source key D. D says 'in response to viewer requests', which could mean viewer-request event (invalid for origin response header editing) or viewer-response invoked for requests (valid). A CloudFront Function on viewer-response is fully supported and directly reads event.request User-Agent and event.response headers, so A is best current simple design; however A does not explicitly name its trigger, and D is also viable if interpreted as viewer-response. Mark as defective/non-unique. No confirmed Choose TWO/THREE variant. AWS: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/function-code-choose-purpose.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/functions-event-structure.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/lambda-event-structure.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/http-api-parameter-mapping.html ; https://www.freecram.net/question/Amazon.SAP-C02.v2026-08-19.q305/a-company-uses-a-service-to-collect-metadata-from-applications-that-the-company-hosts-on-premises-consumer .

review.notes: CloudFront Functions viewer-response can inspect request User-Agent and delete response headers; source D also possible if viewer-response intended, but viewer-request is wrong. Exact external FreeCram keys D. Question ambiguous; prefer A with explicit viewer-response configuration.

stem: A company operates quick-service restaurants. The restaurants follow a predictable model with high sales traffic for 4 hours daily Sales traffic is lower outside of those peak hours. The company wants to reduce its DynamoDB cost and minimize the operational overhead for the IT staff. Which solution meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

Change the DynamoDB table to use on-demand capacity.
Enable Dynamo DB auto scaling tor the table

stem: A delivery company needs to migrate its third-party route planning application to AWS. The third party supplies a supported Docker image from a public registry. The image can run in as many containers as required to generate the route map. The company has divided the delivery area into sections with supply hubs so that delivery drivers travel the shortest distance possible from the hubs to the customers. To reduce the time necessary to generate route maps, each section uses its own set of Docker containers with a custom configuration that processes orders only in the section's area. The company needs the ability to allocate resources cost-effectively based on the number of running containers. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Create an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster on Amazon EC2. Use the Amazon EKS CLI to launch the planning application in pods by using the -tags option to assign a custom tag to the pod.

Create an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster on AWS Fargate. Use the Amazon EKS CLI to launch the planning application. Use the AWS CLI tag- resource API call to assign a custom tag to the pod.

Create an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster on Amazon EC2. Use the AWS CLI with run-tasks set to true to launch the planning application by using the - tags option to assign a custom tag to the task.

Create an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster on AWS Fargate. Use the AWS CLI run-task command and set enableECSManagedTags to true to launch the planning application. Use the --tags option to assign a custom tag to the task.

explanation: D verified. ECS with Fargate runs supported Docker containers without managing EC2 worker nodes; AWS provisions task CPU/memory as tasks are launched and bills for provisioned Fargate resources while tasks run. The ECS RunTask API supports launchType FARGATE, enableECSManagedTags boolean, and user-supplied tags. AWS CLI syntax is `aws ecs run-task --launch-type FARGATE --enable-ecs-managed-tags --tags key=Section,value=North ...`. Section-specific processing configuration should be supplied through task definition or container overrides (e.g. environment variables), NOT through tags alone. References: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/APIReference/API_RunTask.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/ecs/run-task.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/ecs-using-tags.html .
wrongOptionsExplanation: A: EKS on EC2 requires managing worker node capacity, more operational overhead; Kubernetes pods use labels/annotations, not an Amazon EKS CLI `-tags` option. B: EKS Fargate removes worker node management but is more complex than ECS for a simple Docker batch workload; AWS resource TagResource does not tag individual Kubernetes pods (pod labels are Kubernetes metadata). C: ECS on EC2 requires provisioning/scaling/patching instances; the proposed `run-tasks set to true` is not valid ECS CLI syntax and `- tags` is malformed. D: ECS on Fargate is lowest operational overhead; RunTask supports task tags and managed tags. Managed tags and custom tags are separate; task configuration uses overrides rather than tagging.
plainWords: Each delivery area needs some Docker workers. Start only the workers needed for that area as ECS Fargate tasks. AWS manages the servers, you pay for task CPU/memory while running, and you can label tasks by delivery area for tracking. Pass the actual area configuration as environment variables or command overrides.
keyPoints: ECS Fargate = serverless container orchestration without EC2 worker nodes. `aws ecs run-task --launch-type FARGATE --enable-ecs-managed-tags --tags key=Section,value=North` (with task definition, cluster, and awsvpc network configuration). `enableECSManagedTags` is API camelCase; CLI uses `--enable-ecs-managed-tags`. `--tags` applies user-defined task tags; managed tags add AWS/ECS metadata; tags do NOT determine container processing behavior. Use `--overrides` for per-section environment variables or commands. EKS pod labels != AWS resource tags. Fargate task cost based on configured vCPU/memory and runtime, not strictly a flat per-container fee.
sourceWarning: SOURCE ANSWER D VERIFIED. Minor wording defects: option D mixes API field name `enableECSManagedTags` with CLI; correct CLI flag is `--enable-ecs-managed-tags`. Option C `run-tasks set to true` and `- tags` are invalid syntax; A `-tags` for pods and B `tag-resource` for pods are invalid. Tagging tasks is NOT equivalent to configuring the delivery section: use task overrides. External exact-stem FreeCram 2023 Q121/205 and 2025 PDF Q223 both identify D. No confirmed Choose TWO/THREE variant. No retired/outdated AWS service involved. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/APIReference/API_RunTask.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/ecs/run-task.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/ecs-using-tags.html ; https://www.freecram.net/question/Amazon.SAP-C02.v2023-09-16.q205/a-delivery-company-needs-to-migrate-its-third-party-route-planning-application-to-aws-the-third-party ; https://www.freecram.net/Amazon.SAP-C02.v2025-04-03.q227.pdf .

review.notes: AWS RunTask API and ECS tagging docs confirm D. Clarified camelCase API versus kebab-case CLI and custom task tags versus runtime config. Exact-stem external sources key D; no verified multiple-answer variant.

stem: A company is developing a solution to analyze images. The solution uses a 50 TB reference dataset and analyzes images up to 1 TB in size. The solution spreads requests across an Auto Scaling group of Amazon EC2 Linux instances in a VPC. The EC2 instances are attached to shared Amazon EBS io2 volumes in each Availability Zone. The EBS volumes store the reference dataset. During testing, multiple parallel analyses led to numerous disk errors, which caused job failures. The company wants the solution to provide seamless data reading for all instances. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

options.text: Create a new EBS volume for each EC2 instance. Copy the data from the shared volume to the new EBS volume regularly. Update the application to reference the new EBS volume.

Move all the reference data to an Amazon S3 bucket. Install Mountpoint for Amazon S3 on the EC2 instances. Create gateway endpoints for Amazon S3 in the VPC. Replace the EBS mount point with the S3 mount point.

Move all the reference data to an Amazon S3 bucket. Create an Amazon S3 backed Multi-AZ Amazon EFS volume. Mount the EFS volume on the EC2 instances. Replace the EBS mount point with the EFS mount point.
Upgrade the instances to local storage. Copy the data from the shared EBS volume to the local storage regularly. Update the application to reference the local storage.

stem: A solutions architect wants to cost-optimize and appropriately size Amazon EC2 instances in a single AWS account. The solutions architect wants to ensure that the instances are optimized based on CPU, memory, and network metrics. Which combination of steps should the solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: Purchase AWS Business Support or AWS Enterprise Support for the account.
Turn on AWS Trusted Advisor and review any “Low Utilization Amazon EC2 Instances” recommendations.
Install the Amazon CloudWatch agent and configure memory metric collection on the EC2 instances.
Configure AWS Compute Optimizer in the AWS account to receive findings and optimization recommendations.

stem: A company operates a static content distribution platform that serves customers globally. The customers consume content from their own AWS accounts. The company serves its content from an Amazon S3 bucket. The company uploads the content from its on-premises environment to the S3 bucket by using an S3 File Gateway. The company wants to improve the platform's performance and reliability by serving content from the AWS Region that is geographically closest to customers. The company must route the on-premises data to Amazon S3 with minimal latency and without public internet exposure. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Implement S3 Multi-Region Access Points.
Use S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) to copy content to different Regions.
Create an AWS Lambda function that tracks the routing of clients to Regions.

What is the MOST cost-effective migration recommendation?

options.text: Create a queue using Amazon SQS. Configure the existing web server to publish to the new queue. When there are messages in the queue, invoke an AWS Lambda function to pull requests from the queue and process the files. Store the processed files in an Amazon S3 bucket.

Create a queue using Amazon M. Configure the existing web server to publish to the new queue. When there are messages in the queue, create a new Amazon EC2 instance to pull requests from the queue and process the files. Store the processed files in Amazon EFS. Shut down the EC2 instance after the task is complete.

Create a queue using Amazon MO. Configure the existing web server to publish to the new queue. When there are messages in the queue, invoke an AWS Lambda function to pull requests from the queue and process the files. Store the processed files in Amazon EFS.

Create a queue using Amazon SOS. Configure the existing web server to publish to the new queue. Use Amazon EC2 instances in an EC2 Auto Scaling group to pull requests from the queue and process the files. Scale the EC2 instances based on the SOS queue length. Store the processed files in an Amazon S3 bucket.

explanation: D verified: Amazon SQS buffers fluctuating one-hour media jobs, EC2 workers in an Auto Scaling group process messages without standard Lambda's 15-minute timeout, and S3 stores processed files without maintaining EFS. Scale using SQS backlog per instance (visible messages / in-service workers) and target tracking; protect workers from scale-in during long tasks. Configure SQS visibility timeout for one-hour jobs, delete messages after success, implement idempotency and DLQ. AWS: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/as-using-sqs-queue.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-visibility-timeout.html .
wrongOptionsExplanation: A: Standard AWS Lambda max runtime 900 seconds/15 minutes, so cannot finish up-to-one-hour files; SQS+S3 alone cannot fix timeout. B: Amazon MQ and EFS are unnecessary unless broker compatibility/POSIX filesystem is required; starting one new EC2 per message is operationally complex and slow compared with queue-driven Auto Scaling. C: Same standard Lambda 15-minute timeout; EFS doesn't extend function duration and MQ adds cost. D: Correct queue-backed EC2 workers with Auto Scaling and S3; use backlog-per-instance rather than only raw queue length, and manage long-running task scale-in and visibility timeout.
plainWords: Some files need a full hour to process. Put each job in an SQS queue and have EC2 workers process them. Add workers when many files arrive during business hours and remove workers after the queue drains. Save results to S3.
keyPoints: Standard Lambda 15-minute max, but AWS Lambda Managed Instances now documents up to 90 minutes for eligible asynchronous/event-source-mapping invocations (exception; not specified in A/C). EC2 workers suit long-running queue jobs. Scale EC2 ASG on SQS backlog per instance rather than raw visible count; scale-in protection for in-flight jobs. SQS visibility timeout up to 12h; one-hour tasks require appropriate timeout/heartbeat, idempotency, delete-on-success and DLQ. S3 is object storage; EFS shared POSIX storage only when needed. Amazon MQ useful for existing broker protocol compatibility, otherwise SQS simpler.

explanation: B is the HISTORICAL source-key intent, but is NOT deployable as written for a new 2026 solution. AWS IoT Core natively ingests MQTT and IoT rules can send messages to Amazon Data Firehose, which buffers/delivers to S3. Legacy Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics for SQL formerly supported Firehose input for established customers, but new Firehose-input SQL applications were restricted after 2023-09-12 and the entire Kinesis Data Analytics for SQL service was discontinued 2026-01-27. Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink (modern replacement) generally consumes Kinesis Data Streams or MSK, not a Firehose delivery stream as an ordinary streaming source. Correct modern architecture: IoT Core -> Kinesis Data Streams -> Managed Service for Apache Flink for 5-minute windows/anomaly detection, and Data Firehose reading from Kinesis Data Streams -> S3 for archival. AWS references: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/iot/latest/developerguide/iot-rule-actions.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kinesisanalytics/latest/dev/ ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/managed-flink/latest/java/how-sources.html .
wrongOptionsExplanation: A: IoT Greengrass is edge software, not the lowest-overhead fleet MQTT ingestion service; MSK plus custom Kafka-to-S3 code and SageMaker model development add operational complexity. B: IoT Core MQTT and Firehose-to-S3 are appropriate, but Kinesis Data Analytics SQL was retired in January 2026; its legacy Firehose-as-input arrangement cannot be newly created, and Managed Flink typically reads Kinesis Data Streams/MSK. Historically intended answer, now invalid as written. C: FleetWise is vehicle-focused but closed to new customers April 30 2026; AWS Glue's built-in FindMatches ML transform performs record/entity matching, not telematics time-series anomaly detection. D: RabbitMQ/MQ is unnecessary for native MQTT device connectivity, and Amazon Lookout for Metrics ended support October 10 2025. None is fully correct for a new 2026 deployment.
plainWords: The original exam wanted vehicles to publish MQTT to IoT Core, then Firehose to S3, with analytics on the stream. But the named old Kinesis Data Analytics SQL service has been shut down. Today route the same MQTT events into Kinesis Data Streams, run 5-minute anomaly detection with Managed Service for Apache Flink, and deliver a copy to S3 using Firehose.
keyPoints: AWS IoT Core supports MQTT and rules to Kinesis Data Streams, Firehose and S3. Firehose is delivery/buffering to destinations, not a general-purpose Kinesis Data Streams replacement. Legacy Kinesis Data Analytics for SQL applications discontinued 2026-01-27; historical Firehose source existed but creation restricted from 2023-09-12. Modern Managed Service for Apache Flink reads Kinesis Data Streams or MSK for windowed processing; Firehose can archive a Kinesis stream to S3. IoT FleetWise stopped accepting new customers 2026-04-30. Amazon Lookout for Metrics ended 2025-10-10. Glue FindMatches identifies duplicate/matching records, not time-series anomalies.

stem: A company is migrating infrastructure for its massive multiplayer game to AWS. The game's application features a leaderboard where players can see rankings in real time. The leaderboard requires microsecond reads and single-digit-millisecond write latencies. The datasets are single-digit terabytes in size and must be available to accept writes in less than a minute if a primary node failure occurs. The company needs a solution in which data can persist for further analytical processing through a data pipeline. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Create an Amazon ElastiCache (Redis OSS) cluster with cluster mode enabled. Configure the application to interact with the primary node.
Create an Amazon RDS database with a read replica. Configure the application to point writes to the writer endpoint. Configure the application to point reads to the reader endpoint.
Create an Amazon MemoryDB cluster in Multi-AZ mode. Configure the application to interact with the primary node.
Create multiple Redis nodes on Amazon EC2 instances that are spread across multiple Availability Zones. Configure backups to Amazon S3.

explanation: C verified. Amazon MemoryDB is a fully managed Redis OSS/Valkey-compatible durable in-memory primary database with microsecond read latency and single-digit-millisecond write latency, a Multi-AZ transaction log, and automatic replica promotion (AWS FAQ says typically <20 seconds for unplanned failures). Its shards scale to terabyte datasets. Writes are durably committed to the transaction log before acknowledgement; primary reads are strongly consistent. For later analytics, export MemoryDB snapshots to S3 or build a separate event/CDC-style data pipeline as needed; merely using MemoryDB does not automatically create an analytics pipeline. https://aws.amazon.com/memorydb/faqs/ ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/memorydb/latest/devguide/what-is-memorydb.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/memorydb/latest/devguide/autofailover.html .
wrongOptionsExplanation: A: ElastiCache Redis OSS with cluster mode is primarily a cache; clustering does not itself configure durable primary storage or automatic Multi-AZ failover. In 2026 ElastiCache for VALKEY has a new optional durability feature, but this option explicitly says Redis OSS and does not enable that feature. B: RDS read replicas are not designed for microsecond reads, and a conventional RDS read replica is not automatically a write-ready primary after failure. C: MemoryDB Multi-AZ combines durable writes, low latency, automatic failover and managed operation. D: self-managed Redis on EC2 requires deployment, replication/failover, patching, monitoring and backup administration; S3 backups alone don't give near-instant write failover.
plainWords: A game leaderboard needs Redis-like speed but must not lose scores if a server dies. MemoryDB stores the live scores in memory and also writes changes to a durable log spread across Availability Zones. If the primary fails, a replica takes over in seconds.
keyPoints: MemoryDB: Redis OSS/Valkey-compatible durable primary DB, microsecond reads, single-digit-ms writes, Multi-AZ transaction log, automatic failover typically <20 seconds, strong consistency on primary, eventual on replicas, sharding for TB-scale data. MemoryDB snapshots can be exported to S3 for later analytics, but an analytics pipeline is not automatic. RDS read replica != Multi-AZ writer failover. 2026 nuance: ElastiCache for Valkey gained optional durability June 2026, AWS recommends it for new single-Region durable workloads; option A says Redis OSS and no durability configuration, so C remains best.
sourceWarning: SOURCE KEY C VERIFIED by official AWS MemoryDB FAQs and exact-stem external FreeCram SAP-C02 Topic 2 Q739 / PracticeCF No.1490. No confirmed Choose TWO/THREE variant. MODERNIZATION NUANCE: June 2026 ElastiCache for Valkey introduced Multi-AZ durable storage and is now an alternative for NEW workloads, but not described by option A (Redis OSS). Original stem says 'data can persist for further analytical processing through a data pipeline'; MemoryDB is durable and supports snapshot export to S3, but an explicit downstream pipeline still must be built. Sources https://aws.amazon.com/memorydb/faqs/ ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/memorydb/latest/devguide/autofailover.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/memorydb/latest/devguide/related-services-choose-between-memorydb-and-redis.html ; https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/database/announcing-durability-for-amazon-elasticache/ ; https://www.freecram.com/discussions/Amazon/exam-sap-c02-topic-2-question-739-discussion-p1330600.html ; https://www.examtopics.cn/exam-aws-certified-solutions-architect-professional-2 .

review.notes: MemoryDB official docs confirm latency, durable Multi-AZ transaction log and typically under 20s failover. External exact-stem copies verified. ElastiCache Valkey durability launched June 2026, but option A is Redis OSS without durability. Analytics pipeline not automatic.

stem: A solutions architect is redesigning a three-tier application that a company hosts onpremises. The application provides personalized recommendations based on user profiles. The company already has an AWS account and has configured a VPC to host the application. The frontend is a Java-based application that runs in on-premises VMs. The company hosts a personalization model on a physical application server and uses TensorFlow to implement the model. The personalization model uses artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML). The company stores user information in a Microsoft SQL Server database. The web application calls the personalization model, which reads the user profiles from the database and provides recommendations. The company wants to migrate the redesigned application to AWS. Which solution will meet this requirement with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Use AWS Server Migration Service (AWS SMS) to migrate the on-premises physical application server and the web application VMs to AWS. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to migrate the SQL Server database to Amazon RDS for SQL Server.

Export the personalization model. Store the model artifacts in Amazon S3. Deploy the model to Amazon SageMaker and create an endpoint. Host the Java application in AWS Elastic Beanstalk. Use AWS Database Migration Service {AWS DMS) to migrate the SQL Server database to Amazon RDS for SQL Server.

Use AWS Application Migration Service to migrate the on-premises personalization model and VMs to Amazon EC2 instances in Auto Scaling groups. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to migrate the SQL Server database to an EC2 instance.

Containerize the personalization model and the Java application. Use Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) managed node groups to deploy the model and the application to Amazon EKS Host the node groups in a VPC. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to migrate the SQL Server database to Amazon RDS for SQL Server.

explanation: B is the best answer for LEAST operational overhead. Export the trained TensorFlow personalization model, package its model artifacts in S3, and host inference using an Amazon SageMaker AI endpoint with a compatible TensorFlow inference container and proper IAM/VPC network integration. Deploy the Java web application to Elastic Beanstalk (Java SE/Tomcat managed platform). Use AWS DMS for on-premises SQL Server data migration to Amazon RDS for SQL Server, reducing manual database engine administration. Integrate secure profile-data access and inference requests; the answer omits some production integration details. Official AWS references: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/deploy-model-get-started.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/your-algorithms-inference-code.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticbeanstalk/latest/dg/create_deploy_Java.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/userguide/CHAP_Source.SQLServer.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/userguide/CHAP_Target.SQLServer.html.
wrongOptionsExplanation: A: Incorrect. AWS Server Migration Service (SMS) is a legacy offering and is not an appropriate current strategy to migrate the physical model server; lifting VMs/servers into infrastructure-heavy hosting does not minimize inference operations. B: Correct. SageMaker AI managed inference + Elastic Beanstalk for Java + managed RDS SQL Server is the least-operations three-tier architecture; DMS handles data migration. C: Incorrect. AWS Application Migration Service can lift physical/virtual servers to EC2, but managing the EC2 app/ML servers and self-managed SQL Server on EC2 adds patching, backup, monitoring, scaling and HA responsibilities. D: Incorrect. EKS with managed node groups supports the workloads, but teams must still manage Kubernetes releases, workloads, clusters and nodes; containerizing both applications adds work without a stated Kubernetes requirement. RDS is a good choice in D but does not outweigh EKS overhead.
plainWords: Move each existing component to a managed home: Java website to Elastic Beanstalk, TensorFlow recommendation model to a SageMaker AI inference endpoint (model artifacts in S3), and SQL Server data to Amazon RDS using DMS. This reduces server and Kubernetes operations. Choose B.
keyPoints: LEAST operational overhead + existing TensorFlow ML model -> SageMaker AI real-time inference endpoint. Java on VMs -> Elastic Beanstalk managed Java/Tomcat environment. On-prem SQL Server -> Amazon RDS for SQL Server via AWS DMS. Migrating VMs to EC2 (MGN) is lift-and-shift, not maximum operational reduction. EKS managed node groups still require Kubernetes operations. SageMaker endpoint needs supported inference image, IAM role, model format and secure connectivity to profile data. S3 stores artifacts, not the production relational user-profile database.
