stem: A company wants to use Amazon S3 to back up its on-premises file storage solution. The company's on-premises file storage solution supports NFS, and the company wants its new solution to support NFS. The company wants to archive the backup files after 5 days. If the company needs archived files for disaster recovery, t he company is willing to wait a few days for the retrieval of those files. Which solution meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

options.text: Deploy an AWS Storage Gateway files gateway that is associated with an S3 bucket. Move the files from the on-premises file storage solution to the file gateway. Create an S3 Lifecycle rule to move the file to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) after 5 days.

Deploy an AWS Storage Gateway volume gateway that is associated with an S3 bucket. Move the files from the on-premises file storage solution to the volume gateway. Create an S3 Lifecycle rule to move the files to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 5 days.

Deploy an AWS Storage Gateway tape gateway that is associated with an S3 bucket. Move the files from the on-premises file storage solution to the tape gateway. Create an S3 Lifecycle rule to move the files to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) after 5 days.

Deploy an AWS Storage Gateway file gateway that is associated with an S3 bucket. Move the files from the on-premises file storage solution to the tape gateway. Create an S3 Lifecycle rule to move the files to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) after 5 days.

Deploy an AWS Storage Gateway file gateway that is associated with an S3 bucket. Move the files from the on-premises file storage solution to the file gateway. Create an S3 Lifecycle rule to move the files to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 5 days.

explanation: E verified: Amazon S3 File Gateway presents an NFS file share to on-premises clients and stores files as S3 objects. An S3 Lifecycle policy can transition eligible objects after 5 days to S3 Glacier Deep Archive for low-cost long-term DR backups, accepting delayed restore. Glacier Deep Archive has a 180-day minimum storage duration charge (not a minimum age before transition), typically 12-hour standard or up to 48-hour bulk retrieval. Restoring an archived object is required before normal access; File Gateway access to archived objects can return I/O errors. AWS docs: https://aws.amazon.com/storagegateway/faqs/ ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/filegateway/latest/files3/storage-classes.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/glacier-storage-classes.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/lifecycle-transition-general-considerations.html .
wrongOptionsExplanation: A: NFS File Gateway is right, but S3 Standard-IA is for infrequently accessed online objects and is not as cost-effective as Deep Archive for long-retained backup files that tolerate delayed restoration. B: Volume Gateway is block storage (iSCSI), not an NFS share, and the described S3 object lifecycle model is wrong for gateway volumes. C: Tape Gateway exposes virtual tapes to backup software rather than an NFS file share; Standard-IA is also not the cheapest long-term archival tier. D: Contradicts itself by deploying File Gateway but moving files to Tape Gateway, and chooses Standard-IA rather than Deep Archive. E: File Gateway supports NFS and maps files to S3 objects; lifecycle after 5 days to Glacier Deep Archive matches low-cost archival and slow disaster recovery.
plainWords: Your office file server speaks NFS. Use S3 File Gateway so it can send backups into S3 without changing the file protocol. After five days, automatically move the backup objects to S3 Glacier Deep Archive. If a disaster happens, request a restore and wait hours to a couple of days.
keyPoints: S3 File Gateway = NFS/SMB file interface backed by S3 objects; Volume Gateway = iSCSI block volumes; Tape Gateway = virtual tapes for backup software. S3 Lifecycle transition to Glacier Deep Archive can be after 5 days; Deep Archive 180-day MINIMUM BILLING DURATION, not minimum transition age. Glacier Deep Archive restore is asynchronous (standard ~12h, bulk up to 48h); objects cannot be directly read via File Gateway while archived. Since Sept 2024 lifecycle default blocks transitions of objects <128 KB unless appropriate exception configuration; archive transition costs and metadata overhead matter.
sourceWarning: SOURCE ANSWER E VERIFIED. Exact-stem external ITDumpsKR SAP-C02 single-answer variant reorders A-D but also keys E: https://www.itdumpskr.com/SAP-C02-practice-test.html . No verified Choose TWO/THREE variant. Source defects: stem 't he' typo; A 'files gateway' inconsistent term; D says File Gateway then 'tape gateway' (internally impossible); B/C incorrectly assume File Gateway-style S3 lifecycle behavior for block/tape gateways. Modern nuance: lifecycle default since Sept 2024 prevents transitions for objects smaller than 128KB unless configured otherwise; Deep Archive 180-day minimum billing; archived objects need restore and File Gateway may show I/O errors. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/lifecycle-transition-general-considerations.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/filegateway/latest/files3/storage-classes.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/glacier-storage-classes.html ; https://aws.amazon.com/storagegateway/faqs/ .

review.notes: AWS File Gateway NFS and S3 lifecycle Deep Archive official docs confirm E; external ITDumpsKR same stem single-choice key E, options reordered; no confirmed Choose TWO/THREE. Original wording retained; D contradiction, typo, 128KB transition default and 180-day minimum billing flagged.

stem: A company needs to migratesome Oracle databases to AWSwhile keeping otherson- premisesfor compliance. The on-prem databases containspatial dataand runcron jobs. The solution must allowquerying on-prem data as foreign tablesfrom AWS.

options.text: Use DynamoDB, SCT, and Lambda. Move spatial data to S3 and query with Athena.
Use RDS for SQL Server and AWS Glue crawlers for Oracle access.
Use EC2-hosted Oracle with Application Migration Service. Use Step Functions for cron.
Use RDS for PostgreSQL with DMS and SCT. Use PostgreSQL foreign data wrappers. Connectvia Direct Connect.

explanation: D is the correct architecture. AWS SCT converts Oracle schema/code where compatible; AWS DMS migrates data to Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL. PostGIS supports spatial data, pg_cron schedules supported database jobs, and oracle_fdw enables RDS PostgreSQL to query retained on-premises Oracle tables as foreign tables over appropriately configured AWS Direct Connect private connectivity. Direct Connect alone does not implement FDW; configure network routing/security, Oracle user mapping and extension permissions. AWS: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/postgresql-oracle-fdw.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/Appendix.PostgreSQL.CommonDBATasks.Extensions.foreign-data-wrappers.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/PostgreSQLReleaseNotes/postgresql-extensions.html .
wrongOptionsExplanation: A: DynamoDB, S3/Athena and Lambda do not provide Oracle foreign-table SQL access, PostgreSQL/PostGIS spatial migration or equivalent database cron maintenance. B: Glue crawlers discover schemas/metadata, not live Oracle foreign-table queries from RDS SQL Server; heterogeneous conversion and cron requirements not addressed. C: EC2 Oracle lift-and-shift increases server management and does not provide the specified FDW design; MGN is not bidirectional database CDC, and Step Functions is not itself a database cron replacement. D: RDS PostgreSQL + SCT/DMS + PostGIS + pg_cron + oracle_fdw + private Direct Connect routing meets hybrid migration, spatial, maintenance and remote foreign-table query needs.
plainWords: Move only the Oracle databases allowed by compliance into RDS PostgreSQL using SCT for schema and DMS for data. Use PostGIS for maps/spatial data, pg_cron for scheduled database jobs, and oracle_fdw to read tables in Oracle databases still on-premises through Direct Connect. Choose D.
keyPoints: AWS SCT = heterogeneous schema/code conversion; AWS DMS = data migration/CDC. RDS PostgreSQL supports PostGIS, pg_cron and oracle_fdw (version/permissions dependent). oracle_fdw, not Direct Connect alone, exposes remote Oracle tables as PostgreSQL foreign tables. Direct Connect provides private network transport; routing, VPC connectivity, security groups and Oracle listener connectivity still required. Original Q616 is heavily abbreviated; external full SAP-C02 question 73 maps the same PostgreSQL solution to C (different option order).
sourceWarning: SOURCE KEY D TECHNICALLY VERIFIED; ORIGINAL STEM/OPTIONS SEVERELY ABBREVIATED with missing spaces, omitting PostGIS and pg_cron details. External longer variant SAP-C02 question 73 keys C (equivalent PostgreSQL architecture), but its explanation inconsistently calls it D. No confirmed Choose TWO/THREE variant. Source: https://myportal.utt.edu.tt/ICS/icsfs/d97df75f-867e-411a-ac5f-e13435c2eedc.pdf?target=c53e5228-7ce9-4ef5-a5ec-d932dc3abaad ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/postgresql-oracle-fdw.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/PostgreSQLReleaseNotes/postgresql-extensions.html .

review.notes: External full variant question 73 maps equivalent solution to C; inconsistent external explanation says D. AWS docs confirm oracle_fdw, PostGIS, pg_cron. Original abbreviated source retained. No confirmed multi-answer variant.

stem: A machine learning (ML) company continuously develops new versions of its models. The models are integrated into a web application that uses a RESTful API to call custom Python code to invoke the models. The application runs in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group. Customer feedback indicates that new model versions sometimes perform worse than previous versions. The company wants to implement a gradual deployment approach in which 10% of traffic is initially routed to new models to verify performance. The solution must also reduce operational overhead for infrastructure management. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Deploy model versions to an Amazon SageMaker AI multi-model endpoint. Configure the weight for the new version to 10% and the previous version to 90%. Migrate the Python code to an AWS Lambda function. Use Amazon API Gateway to invoke the Lambda function.

Deploy each model version to a separate Amazon SageMaker Serverless Inference endpoint. Configure an AWS Lambda function to route 10% of invocation calls to the new endpoint and 90% to the previous version based on weighted random selection. Use Amazon API Gateway to invoke the Lambda function.

Deploy each model version to a separate Amazon SageMaker AI single-model endpoint. Configure an AWS Lambda function to route 10% of invocation calls to the new endpoint's URL and 90% to the previous version. Use Amazon API Gateway to invoke the Lambda function.

Deploy model versions to an Amazon SageMaker Serverless Inference endpoint. Use Amazon API Gateway with a canary deployment to gradually shift 10% of traffic to the new model version while maintaining 90% of traffic on the previous version.

explanation: D is the intended least-operational-overhead answer: API Gateway REST API canary deployments can route 10% of API requests to a new deployment and 90% to production, while SageMaker Serverless Inference avoids provisioning and scaling ML inference instances. IMPORTANT implementation caveat: SageMaker Serverless Inference does not support multiple production variants in a single endpoint. Configure separate old/new serverless inference endpoints and use different API Gateway integration backends (for example separate Lambda integrations or stage-variable overrides) for production versus canary; the wording of D omits this integration detail. AWS: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/canary-release.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/serverless-endpoints.html .
wrongOptionsExplanation: A: Incorrect as stated. A multi-model endpoint dynamically hosts multiple model artifacts, but weighted 90/10 traffic splitting uses SageMaker production variants, not automatic per-model weights on a multi-model endpoint. B: Technically feasible: two serverless endpoints and Lambda randomized 90/10 selection, but requires maintaining custom routing logic rather than API Gateway native canary controls. C: Technically feasible: two real-time single-model endpoints and Lambda routing, but adds instance provisioning/scaling plus custom routing and uses imprecise 'endpoint URL' terminology (SageMaker InvokeEndpoint API). D: Best intended: serverless inference plus API Gateway canary percentage. Requires two separately addressable model backends; a single serverless endpoint cannot host weighted production variants.
plainWords: Let API Gateway send 90 of every roughly 100 requests to the stable API deployment and 10 to a canary deployment. Configure those deployments to invoke separate old and new SageMaker serverless model endpoints. You avoid managing EC2 inference servers and avoid writing random routing code.
keyPoints: API Gateway REST API canary deployment = percent-based split between production and canary deployments, with stage-variable overrides for integrations. SageMaker Serverless Inference = automatic scaling, no managed instances, but NO multiple production variants, NO multi-model endpoints and possible cold starts. SageMaker real-time production variants support model A/B weighted routing, a different feature from multi-model endpoints. Option D requires separate backends/integrations; it is incomplete if interpreted as a single serverless endpoint hosting both models.
sourceWarning: SOURCE KEY D MATCHES exact-stem ExamCollection SAP-C02 Q178. Technically intended, but option D omits necessary separation of old/new inference backends; SageMaker Serverless Inference explicitly excludes multiple production variants, so one serverless endpoint cannot itself route 90/10 between model versions. Use two serverless endpoints with API Gateway canary deployment integrations. Option A confuses multi-model endpoint routing with weighted production variants. No confirmed Choose TWO/THREE variant. review.notes: ExamCollection exact stem Q178 keys D. AWS API Gateway REST canary + SageMaker Serverless supports intended design only with distinct old/new backend integrations; serverless endpoints cannot contain multiple production variants. No confirmed multiple-answer variant.

Create a Network Load Balancer (NLB). Associate the NLB with one static IP addresses in multiple Availability Zones. Create an ALB-type target group for the NLB and add the existing ALAdd the NLB IP addresses to the firewall appliance. Update the clients to connect to the NLB.

Create a Network Load Balancer (NLB). Associate the LNB with one static IP addresses in multiple Availability Zones. Add the existing target groups to the NLB. Update the clients to connect to the NLB. Delete the ALB Add the NLB IP addresses to the firewall appliance.

Create a Gateway Load Balancer (GWLB). Assign static IP addresses to the GWLB in multiple Availability Zones. Create an ALB-type target group for the GWLB and add the existing ALB. Add the GWLB IP addresses to the firewall appliance. Update the clients to connect to the GWLB.

explanation: B verified. Place an internal Network Load Balancer with static private IP address per enabled Availability Zone in front of the existing internal Application Load Balancer. Configure an NLB TCP listener on port 443 and an 'alb'-type target group with the existing ALB as its single target, so TLS continues to terminate on the ALB and existing HTTPS path-based listener rules remain intact. Allow-list all NLB AZ private IPs on the on-premises firewall, ensure Direct Connect routes to the NLB subnets, and update client DNS to the NLB. AWS docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/network/application-load-balancer-target.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/network/network-load-balancers.html .
wrongOptionsExplanation: A: ALB IPs are not configurable static addresses; its nodes and DNS-resolved addresses may change. B: Correct: NLB supplies static private IPs while forwarding TCP 443 to the ALB, preserving ALB TLS termination and path routing. C: NLB has no HTTP URL path-based routing, so removing the ALB and attaching its target groups cannot preserve the existing behavior; option also contains typos. D: GWLB distributes traffic to network appliances and does not accept ALB-type target groups or replace this NLB-to-ALB pattern.
plainWords: The office firewall only allows known IP addresses. Put an internal NLB in front of the ALB, allow-list the NLB's fixed private IP for each Availability Zone, and forward TCP 443 to the ALB. The ALB keeps decrypting HTTPS and routing /api and /app to the right servers.
keyPoints: NLB = Layer 4 TCP and static private IP per enabled AZ; internal NLB private IPs are appropriate for Direct Connect. ALB = Layer 7 HTTP/HTTPS host/path rules and TLS termination. NLB target group type 'alb' can register exactly one ALB, in same VPC and account, with matching listener/target group ports; use TCP pass-through to retain ALB TLS termination. NLB does not support ALB path rules. Allow-list all enabled-AZ NLB IPs and use DNS pointing to NLB. GWLB targets network appliances.
sourceWarning: SOURCE KEY B VERIFIED by exact-stem FreeCram SAP-C02 Q137 and official AWS NLB ALB-type target group docs. stem: A company's solutions architect needs to provide secure Remote Desktop connectivity to users for Amazon EC2 Windows instances that are hosted in a VPC. The solution must integrate centralized user management with the company's on-premises Active Directory. Connectivity to the VPC is through the internet. The company has hardware that can be used to establish an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

options.text: Deploy a managed Active Directory by using AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory. Establish a trust with the on-premises Active Directory.Deploy an EC2 instance as a bastion host in the VPC. Ensure that the EC2 instance is joined to the domain. Use the bastion host to access the target instances through RDP.

Configure AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On) to integrate with the on- premises Active Directory by using the AWS Directory Service for MicrosoftActive Directory AD Connector. Configure permission sets against user groups for access to AWS Systems Manager. Use Systems Manager Fleet Manager toaccess the target instances through RDP.

Implement a VPN between the on-premises environment and the target VPC. Ensure that the target instances are joined to the on-premises Active Directory domain over the VPN connection. Configure RDP access through the VPN. Connect from the company's network to the target instances.

Deploy a managed Active Directory by using AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory. Establish a trust with the on-premises Active Directory.Deploy a Remote Desktop Gateway on AWS by using an AWS Quick Start. Ensure that the Remote Desktop Gateway is joined to the domain. Use the Remote Desktop Gateway to access the target instances through RDP.

explanation: DISPUTED. Published SAP-C02 exam-site answer keys select D: managed AWS Microsoft AD trust plus Remote Desktop Gateway. D provides centralized AD authentication and secure remote RDP through an RD Gateway but incurs managed directory and EC2 gateway infrastructure charges. Given the explicit available Site-to-Site VPN hardware and the 'MOST cost-effectively' criterion, C may be cheaper: use VPN to link the company's on-premises network to the VPC, join Windows EC2 to existing on-premises AD, and restrict RDP to private VPN traffic. However C assumes users connect from the company's network, not arbitrary internet clients. The stem does not clarify this. Therefore retain published key D with disputed-key flag; do NOT present D as conclusively technically optimal. AWS VPN and Windows connectivity docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpn/latest/s2svpn/customer-gateway-device-windows.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/saas-network-access-options/options-onprem.html .
wrongOptionsExplanation: A: Managed AWS Microsoft AD and an EC2 bastion provide AD-integrated RDP but add recurring infrastructure costs; bastion requires hardening/maintenance. B: IAM Identity Center plus AD Connector and Systems Manager Fleet Manager can support browser-based RDP without inbound RDP exposure, but requires managed-node permissions/configuration; not clearly lowest cost and identity-center authentication behavior differs from native on-prem AD Windows logon. C: Potentially MOST cost-effective with existing VPN-capable hardware: join EC2 directly to on-prem AD over Site-to-Site VPN and allow RDP only from corporate network. Caveat: this does not directly serve off-network users. D: Source-key answer on multiple exam sites; secure RD Gateway and AWS Managed Microsoft AD trust, but higher cost than reusing on-prem AD and VPN if corporate-network access suffices.
plainWords: Published exam sites say D: set up AWS Managed AD and a Remote Desktop Gateway. But the question asks for cheapest and already has VPN hardware. If employees connect from the office network, C (VPN + existing AD + private RDP) avoids paying for a new managed directory and gateway server. Treat this as a disputed exam question, not a reliable memorization of D.
keyPoints: AWS Site-to-Site VPN joins on-premises network and VPC over encrypted IPsec, NOT arbitrary remote user devices. EC2 Windows instances can join existing on-prem AD when network/DNS/AD ports are reachable. RD Gateway centralizes remote RDP over HTTPS but requires infrastructure; managed Microsoft AD incurs charges. Fleet Manager supports browser-based RDP and IAM Identity Center authentication but its authentication may create local admin accounts and has limits. Cost-sensitive questions must distinguish corporate network vs remote internet users.
sourceWarning: DISPUTED SOURCE ANSWER D. Exact-stem FreeCram, DumpsTech, JPNTest variants key RD Gateway/Managed AD (option letters differ), but AWS Site-to-Site VPN plus existing on-prem AD (repository C) is arguably more cost-effective given existing hardware and corporate-network users. If users are internet-based outside company network, C alone does not serve them; question ambiguous. Retain D as historical key, mark disputed rather than verified. No confirmed Choose TWO/THREE variant. Wording defects missing spaces after periods and 'MicrosoftActive' and 'toaccess'. Sources https://www.freecram.net/question/Amazon.SAP-C02.v2024-03-21.q171/a-company-s-solutions-architect-needs-to-provide-secure-remote-desktop-connectivity-to-users-for-amazon ; https://www.dumpstech.com/free-amazon-web-services/sap-c02-practice-9.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpn/latest/s2svpn/customer-gateway-device-windows.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/us_en/systems-manager/latest/userguide/fleet-manager-remote-desktop-connections.html .

review.notes: External sites key D (RD Gateway) but cost criterion plus preexisting VPN hardware make C plausible/likely cheaper for corporate-network users. Off-network internet access favors RD Gateway; ambiguous stem. Do not silently change answer; source key retained with disputed status. No verified multi-answer variant.

options.text: Deploy the application to Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instances with load balancing across multiple Availability Zones. Use scheduled Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling to add capacity before the high volume of submissions on Fridays

Deploy the application in a container using Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with load balancing across multiple Availability Zones Use scheduled Service Auto Scaling to add capacity before the high volume of submissions on Fridays

stem: A company is running applications on AWS in a multi-account environment. The company's sales team and marketing team use separate AWS accounts in AWS Organizations. Create an SCP to grant access to the S3 bucket to the marketing account. Use AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) to share the KMS key from the sates account with the marketing account. Update the QuickSight permissions in the marketing account to grant access to the S3 bucket.

Grant decrypt access to the QuickSight role. Update the QuickSight permissions in the marketing account to grant access to the S3 bucket.

stem: A company that provides image storage services wants to deploy a customer-lacing solution to AWS. Millions of individual customers will use the solution. The solution will receive batches of large image files, resize the files, and store the files in an Amazon S3 bucket for up to 6 months. The solution must handle significant variance in demand. The solution must also be reliable at enterprise scale and have the ability to rerun processing jobs in the event of failure. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

options.text: Use AWS Step Functions to process the S3 event that occurs when a user stores an image. Run an AWS Lambda function that resizes the image in place and replaces the original file in the S3 bucket. Create an S3 Lifecycle expiration policy to expire all stored images after 6 months.

Use Amazon EventBridge to process the S3 event that occurs when a user uploads an image. Run an AWS Lambda function that resizes the image in place and replaces the original file in the S3 bucket. Create an S3 Lifecycle expiration policy to expire all stored images after 6 months.

Use S3 Event Notifications to invoke an AWS Lambda function when a user stores an image. Use the Lambda function to resize the image in place and to store the original file in the S3 bucket. Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to move all stored images to S3 Standard- Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) after 6 months.

Use Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) to process the S3 event that occurs when a user stores an image. Run an AWS Lambda function that resizes the image and stores the resized file in an S3 bucket that uses S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA). Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to move all stored images to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 6 months.

explanation: A is the best available option: Step Functions Standard Workflows support retry/redrive of failed image-processing executions; an S3 Lifecycle expiration policy removes objects after six months. Option C transitions objects to Standard-IA only after six months, which does not enforce six-month retention. Configure separate output prefix/bucket or S3 event filtering to prevent Lambda recursion. AWS Step Functions Standard redrive eligibility is limited (typically within 14 days after failed execution).
wrongOptionsExplanation: B: EventBridge routing does not by itself provide Step Functions Standard workflow redrive. C: S3 Standard-IA transition after six months does not expire objects and lacks explicit failed-job replay. D: Glacier Deep Archive transition after six months is not expiration and does not explicitly handle reprocessing; retrieval is slow.
plainWords: Use Step Functions to track and retry image resizing, and use S3 Lifecycle expiration to delete images after six months. Moving images to a cheaper storage tier is not the same as deleting them.
keyPoints: Step Functions Standard redrive; S3 Lifecycle expiration vs transition; S3 event recursion avoidance; Lambda runtime suitability must be checked for large images.
sourceWarning: A assumes Step Functions Standard Workflows for redrive; event filtering or distinct output prefix/bucket is needed to avoid S3 recursive triggers. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/step-functions/latest/dg/redrive-executions.html https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/EventNotifications.html

review.notes: A best available option based on workflow redrive and six-month expiration; Standard Workflow assumption; avoid same-prefix S3 recursion. Verify source variants independently.

stem: A company wants to migrate virtual Microsoft workloads from an on-premises data center to AWS The company has successfully tested a few sample workloads on AWS. The company also has created an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection to a VPC A solutions architect needs to generate a total cost of ownership (TCO) report for the migration of all the workloads from the data center Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) has been enabled on each VM in the data center The company cannot add more VMs m the data center and cannot install additional software on the VMs The discovery data must be automatically imported into AWS Migration Hub Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Use the AWS Application Migration Service agentless service and the AWS Migration Hub Strategy Recommendations to generate the TCO report
Launch a Windows Amazon EC2 instance Install the Migration Evaluator agentless collector on the EC2 instance Configure Migration Evaluator to generate the TCO report
Launch a Windows Amazon EC2 instance. Install the Migration Evaluator agentless collector on the EC2 instance. Configure Migration Hub to generate the TCO report
Use the AWS Migration Readiness Assessment tool inside the VPC Configure Migration Evaluator to generate the TCO report

explanation: DISPUTED SOURCE KEY A. AWS Migration Evaluator is AWS's documented tool for SNMP/WMI-based agentless discovery and TCO/business case reporting. Option B runs its collector on a Windows EC2 instance across existing Site-to-Site VPN, avoids adding on-prem VMs or installing agents on existing workloads, and generates the TCO report; however, automatic import of this collector's discovery data into Migration Hub is not demonstrated by the cited AWS docs. Option A combines AWS Application Migration Service agentless migration and Migration Hub Strategy Recommendations, which are not the clearly documented Migration Evaluator TCO-reporting workflow. No choice unambiguously meets ALL requirements. Preserve source answer A but mark disputed, and identify B as the best documented TCO choice. AWS: https://aws.amazon.com/migration-evaluator/faqs/ ; https://aws.amazon.com/migration-evaluator/features/ ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/migrationhub/latest/ug/gs-new-user-discovery.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/application-discovery/latest/userguide/discovery-import.html .
wrongOptionsExplanation: A (source key, disputed): Application Migration Service is primarily for moving servers; Strategy Recommendations offers migration strategy assessments rather than the specified Migration Evaluator TCO business case. Agentless migration does not itself establish SNMP-based TCO reporting or automatic Migration Hub discovery import. B (best TCO answer, with caveat): Migration Evaluator agentless collector on Windows EC2 can collect on-prem SNMP/WMI metrics over VPN without source agents or new on-prem VMs and produce TCO report. Automatic import into Migration Hub not established. C: Misassigns TCO reporting to Migration Hub instead of Migration Evaluator. D: Migration Readiness Assessment is not the SNMP collector or TCO reporting engine.
plainWords: TCO means calculating what your on-premises Microsoft servers would cost on AWS. Migration Evaluator is the AWS tool for that; it can use SNMP without agents on each server. The repository says A, but B matches the TCO requirement better. The question also requires automatic Migration Hub import, which none of these answers clearly proves.
keyPoints: Migration Evaluator = agentless SNMP/WMI/vSphere collection, rightsizing and TCO business case. Migration Hub = discovery inventory, migration planning/tracking; it is not the primary TCO generator. Migration Hub import supports data file imports and separate discovery collectors; do not assume Migration Evaluator auto-imports to Migration Hub without verified integration. MGN agentless = migration/replication, not inherently TCO. Existing VPN permits EC2-hosted collector reachability if networking and permissions allow. Strategy Recommendations on-prem offering is in KTLO for existing customers as of AWS docs.
sourceWarning: DISPUTED SOURCE ANSWER A; exact stem published with CONFLICTING keys. CertEnsure Q67 keys A (MGN + Strategy Recommendations); DumpsReview Q219 keys D (same MGN design); FreeCram question 217/355 keys A (Migration Evaluator design = repository B). Official AWS Migration Evaluator FAQ/features support B for SNMP agentless TCO, but automatic Migration Hub import not verified. None of four options conclusively satisfies both TCO and auto-import. Preserve A for source traceability and flag defective/ambiguous. No confirmed Choose TWO/THREE variant. Typos 'AWS The', 'VPC A', 'VMs m', missing periods. https://aws.amazon.com/migration-evaluator/faqs/ ; https://aws.amazon.com/migration-evaluator/features/ ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/migrationhub/latest/ug/gs-new-user-discovery.html ; https://www.freecram.net/question/Amazon.SAP-C02.v2025-07-25.q355/a-company-wants-to-migrate-virtual-microsoft-workloads-from-an-on-premises-data-center-to-aws-the-company ; https://www.certensure.com/amazon-web-services/sap-c02-cert-practice-test.html ; https://www.dumpsreview.com/articles/guide-new-2024-actual-amazon-sap-c02-exam-questions-q214-q233/ .

review.notes: Conflicting exact-stem external keys: FreeCram favors repo B (Migration Evaluator), CertEnsure and DumpsReview favor repo A (MGN+Strategy). AWS supports B for TCO, but automatic Migration Hub import not established. Retained A historical key and flagged as disputed/defective. No verified multi-answer variant.

stem: SIMULATION A research company conducts mathematical simulations in the AWS Cloud. The simulations run on several hundred Amazon EC2 Linux instances. Attach the IAM policy to the engineers' IAM role with an Allow statement for the GetSecretValue action. Instruct the engineers to retrieve the SSH key from Secrets Manager when the engineers connect through any SSH client.

Attach the IAM policy to the engineers' IAM role with an Allow statement to run Systems Manager documents. stem: A company is migrating its legacy .NET workload to AWS. The company has a containerized setup that includes a base container image. The base image is tens of gigabytes in size because of legacy libraries and other dependencies. The company has images for custom developed components that are dependent on the base image. The company will use Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) as part of its solution on AWS. Which solution will provide the LOWEST container startup time on AWS?

options.text: Use Amazon ECR to store the base image and the images for the custom developed components. Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) onAWS Fargate to run the workload.
Use Amazon ECR to store the base image and the images for the custom developed components. Use AWS App Runner to run the workload.

Use Amazon ECR to store the images for the custom developed components. Create an AMI that contains the base image. Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) on Amazon EC2 instances that are based on the AMI to run the workload

Use Amazon ECR to store the images for the custom developed components. Create an AMI that contains the base image. Use Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) on AWS Fargate with the AMI to run the workload.

explanation: C verified: ECS on EC2 supports custom AMIs containing pre-pulled Docker/container base image layers, so a very large shared base image need not be downloaded afresh at task startup. Derived custom component images reuse identical base layers; pull only missing layers from ECR. For repeat tasks configure ECS_IMAGE_PULL_BEHAVIOR=once or prefer-cached when appropriate. AWS docs https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/pull-behavior.html ; https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/ecs-create-custom-amis ; https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/ecs-images-latency .
wrongOptionsExplanation: A: ECS on Fargate cannot use a custom EC2 AMI to prepopulate container image caches, so a huge base image must be fetched for the task. B: App Runner manages hosts and does not permit custom host AMIs to pre-cache tens-of-GB base image layers. C: Correct: ECS EC2 custom AMI with preloaded base layers minimizes container image pull startup time, assuming compatible image layer hashes, adequate local disk and correct cache settings. D: EKS Fargate cannot run pods on customer AMIs; an AMI with the base image cannot be attached to Fargate nodes.
plainWords: The base container image is huge. Instead of downloading it every time a container starts, bake its actual image layers into a custom EC2 AMI, launch ECS EC2 worker instances from that AMI, and pull only the small custom changes from ECR. This is option C.
keyPoints: ECS on EC2 permits custom AMIs and Docker/containerd local image caching; Fargate/App Runner do not accept custom EC2 host AMIs. ECS_IMAGE_PULL_BEHAVIOR=once or prefer-cached can reduce unnecessary pulls. The AMI must contain the container engine's cached image layers, not just copied application files. Image digests/layers must match the dependent images; maintain AMI freshness, OS/container engine compatibility, and disk capacity. Container startup time vs EC2 cold provisioning time are distinct.
sourceWarning: ANSWER C VERIFIED against AWS ECS caching/custom AMI docs and independent exact-stem sites: P2PExams SAP-C02 PDF Q1 C; Exam-Tests Q219 option A maps to repository C; GoShiken Q234 option C same. No verified Choose TWO/THREE variant. Source wording typo 'onAWS' and missing period in C. Practical nuance: cached base layers only help if image layer digests match, image is actually pre-pulled into AMI container runtime and ECS cache behavior permits reuse. https://www.p2pexams.com/free-questions/expert-designed-amazon-sap-c02-exam-study-material-by-goodwin.pdf ; https://www.exam-tests.com/SAP-C02-exam/Amazon.SAP-C02.v2025-02-24.q513.html?p=45 ; https://www.goshiken.com/blog/%E7%84%A1%E6%96%99sap-c02%E3%82%B5%E3%83%B3%E3%83%97%E3%83%AB%E5%95%8F%E9%A1%8C%E3%81%A7100-%E3%82%AB%E3%83%90%E3%83%BC%E7%8E%87%E3%81%AE%E3%83%AA%E3%82%A2%E3%83%AB%E8%A9%A6%E9%A8%93%E5%95%8F%E9%A1%8C-%E6%9B%B4%E6%96%B0%E3%81%95%E3%82%8C%E3%81%9F485%E5%95%8F%E3%81%82%E3%82%8A%E3%81%BE%E3%81%99-q227-q245/ .

review.notes: AWS ECS EC2 cached image/custom AMI confirms C. P2PExams Q1 keys C, Exam-Tests Q219 keys A equivalent to C, GoShiken Q234 has C equivalent. No confirmed Choose TWO/THREE variant.

stem: A company has a critical application in which the data tier is deployed in a single AWS Region. The data tier uses an Amazon DynamoDB table and an Amazon Aurora MySQL DB cluster. The current Aurora MySQL engine version supports a global database. The application tier is already deployed in two Regions. Company policy states that critical applications must have application tier components and data tier components deployed across two Regions. The RTO and RPO must be no more than a few minutes each. stem: A company is migrating a large on-prem Oracle database (withstored procedures) to AWS. The solution must usemanaged services, behighly available, and enable afast migrationwithminimal downtime.

options.text: Use AWS DMS to replicate data to RDS for Oracle. Store database files in S3.
Use backup and restore into EC2-hosted Oracle cluster.
Use DMS to move data to DynamoDB. Recreate stored procedures in Lambda.
Use DMS to migrate toAmazon Aurora PostgreSQL. UseAWS SCTto convert stored procedures.

explanation: D is the intended best answer among the choices. AWS SCT converts Oracle schemas and many stored procedures/functions for Aurora PostgreSQL, while AWS DMS performs initial full load and ongoing CDC replication, keeping Oracle operational until cutover. Aurora PostgreSQL is managed and can provide HA. AWS prescriptive guidance explicitly documents Oracle -> Aurora PostgreSQL with DMS + SCT: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/patterns/migrate-an-oracle-database-to-aurora-postgresql-using-aws-dms-and-aws-sct.html . Caveat: Oracle-to-PostgreSQL is heterogeneous; SCT may require manual procedure rewrites and application changes. If fastest migration with fewest changes is paramount and Oracle licensing acceptable, RDS for Oracle may be better than cross-engine migration, but option A's S3 database-file architecture is defective.
wrongOptionsExplanation: A: DMS Oracle-to-RDS Oracle can provide low downtime and preserve stored procedures through appropriate homogeneous migration methods, but storing RDS Oracle database files in S3 is not a valid deployment architecture; option omits proper handling of database objects. B: EC2 Oracle cluster is self-managed and backup/restore for large databases can entail extended downtime. C: DynamoDB is NoSQL and cannot directly run Oracle PL/SQL procedures; rewriting them as Lambda functions requires major application redesign. D: Best intended; SCT converts schema and supported procedural code, DMS moves data and CDC, Aurora provides managed HA; conversion and testing still needed.
plainWords: Oracle contains both data and PL/SQL procedures. DMS copies and continuously synchronizes the data; SCT translates the Oracle-specific database structure and procedures into PostgreSQL-compatible code. Put the result on managed Aurora PostgreSQL and switch over after validation. Answer D, with manual fixes for procedures SCT cannot convert.
keyPoints: DMS = full-load plus CDC data migration, not general stored-procedure translation. SCT = schema and code conversion; unsupported PL/SQL requires manual fixes. DMS Schema Conversion is a managed alternative to desktop SCT. Aurora PostgreSQL managed high availability; heterogeneous migration needs compatibility assessment, application changes, validation and cutover. RDS for Oracle is a valid homogeneous alternative if minimal code change is prioritized, but S3 is not a database-file storage target for RDS Oracle.
sourceWarning: ANSWER D verified as intended by AWS official Oracle-to-Aurora DMS/SCT prescriptive guidance and exact-text ExamCollection SAP-C02 Q22. Second independent exact-match exam-site not established; do not claim multiple verified external matches. No confirmed Choose TWO/THREE variant. Defective abbreviated stem lacks explicit final question; many missing spaces ('withstored','usemanaged','behighly','afast','migrationwithminimal','toAmazon','UseAWS','SCTto'). Question does not state Oracle engine replacement is desired, so D's heterogeneous conversion may not be fastest versus a correctly specified homogeneous RDS Oracle option; A invalidly suggests S3 database files. AWS SCT is still documented, and managed DMS Schema Conversion is also available. https://www.examcollection.us/exam/SAP-C02-question-answer-2.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/patterns/migrate-an-oracle-database-to-aurora-postgresql-using-aws-dms-and-aws-sct.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/userguide/CHAP_SchemaConversion.html .

review.notes: AWS DMS+SCT Oracle->Aurora PostgreSQL official pattern, exact ExamCollection SAP-C02 Q22 answer D. No second confirmed external exact-match; no multi-answer variant. Abbreviated malformed stem and heterogeneity assumptions flagged.

explanation: C verified. Amazon AppStream 2.0 (renamed Amazon WorkSpaces Applications) streams an existing Windows desktop app to Windows and Linux users via supported web browsers, without rewriting it. Package the application using an image builder, deploy an On-Demand fleet with fleet auto scaling, and use built-in user pools for simplified independent authentication. wrongOptionsExplanation: A: WorkSpaces full desktops are heavier than streaming one app, and Cognito identity pools are not the native WorkSpaces user login mechanism. B: Windows EC2 Auto Scaling and RDP can host the app but demand custom remote access, security and fleet management; original option is garbled ('Auto Scarlet', 'Ama7on'). plainWords: Employees use Windows and Linux, but the app only runs on Windows. Instead of rewriting it, install it once into a WorkSpaces Applications (formerly AppStream 2.0) image and stream it to everyone in a browser. Built-in user pools provide simple sign-in. Choose C.
keyPoints: AppStream 2.0 was renamed Amazon WorkSpaces Applications, not retired. Streams existing Windows desktop apps to HTML5 browser on Linux/Windows without code rewrite. Image builder -> image -> stack -> On-Demand fleet -> auto scaling. User pools are service-local identities; SAML 2.0 federation reuses on-prem AD/IdP and is required for domain-joined fleets. On-Demand may add 1-2 minute session startup versus Always-On. Amazon WorkSpaces Personal delivers whole virtual desktops, distinct from app streaming. Cognito identity pools grant temporary AWS credentials, not normal WorkSpaces desktop authentication.
sourceWarning: ANSWER C VERIFIED. Exact-stem CertEnsure keys C; P2PExams PDF keys C; PassTest keys B equivalent to repo C after reordering. No confirmed Choose TWO/THREE variant. AppStream 2.0 renamed Amazon WorkSpaces Applications (current AWS naming). OCR defects: 'lo AWS', '(or all', 'Auto Scarlet', 'Ama7on', 'That', 'starling browse''; preserve original options for traceability. On-prem AD mentioned but C uses separate user pools; if AD sign-in is required, use SAML federation instead, which is not offered in C. One of the applications uses AWS Lambda functions and store’s inventory data in an Amazon Aurora database. The application deploys the Lambda functions by using a deployment package. The application processes critical data, so the company must minimize downtime. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Download the Lambda function deployment package from the Source account. Use the deployment package and create new Lambda functions in the Target account. Share the automated Aurora DB cluster snapshot with the Target account.

Download the Lambda function deployment package from the Source account. Use the deployment package and create new Lambda functions in the Target account Share the Aurora DB cluster with the Target account by using AWS Resource Access Manager {AWS RAM). Grant the Target account permission to clone the Aurora DB cluster.
Use AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) to share the Lambda functions and the Aurora DB cluster with the Target account. Grant the Target account permission to clone the Aurora DB cluster.
Use AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) to share the Lambda functions with the Target account. Share the automated Aurora DB cluster snapshot with the Target account.

explanation: B is the only valid choice: download/redeploy Lambda deployment packages in Target; share the existing Aurora DB cluster through AWS RAM to Target and authorize cross-account copy-on-write cloning. Aurora cross-account cloning is faster than snapshot restore, minimizing provisioning time. Lambda functions are NOT supported AWS RAM shareable resources; use deployment packages/IaC to recreate functions, IAM roles, triggers and configuration. Automated Aurora cluster snapshots cannot be shared directly: copy to manual snapshot first if snapshot method is chosen. IMPORTANT: an Aurora clone is a point-in-time copy, not continuously replicated; for write-heavy workloads coordinate final write freeze/sync and cutover to prevent divergence. AWS https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Aurora.Managing.Clone.Cross-Account.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ram/latest/userguide/shareable.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-share-snapshot.html .
wrongOptionsExplanation: A: Lambda package redeployment is valid, but automated Aurora DB cluster snapshots cannot be shared directly; first copy to a manual snapshot. B: Correct: recreate Lambda functions in Target and use RAM to share/clone Aurora DB cluster, which is faster than snapshot restore. C: Invalid: AWS RAM does not support sharing Lambda functions; only the Aurora cluster part is valid. D: Invalid for both reasons: Lambda functions cannot be shared through RAM, and automated Aurora snapshots cannot be shared directly.
plainWords: To move Lambda to another AWS account, deploy the function code again there. To move Aurora quickly, share its cluster through AWS RAM and clone it in the new account. Do NOT try to share Lambda through RAM or share an automated snapshot directly. Answer B, not the original C.
keyPoints: AWS RAM supports Aurora DB cluster cross-account clone, NOT Lambda function sharing. Lambda cross-account invocation permissions are not function migration. Automated Aurora DB cluster snapshots must be copied to MANUAL snapshots before sharing. Aurora clone uses copy-on-write and is faster than snapshot restore, but is a point-in-time independent cluster; ensure write consistency/cutover. For encrypted Aurora source, customer-managed KMS key access required; default RDS KMS key blocks cross-account cloning. Recreate Lambda code, role, event source mappings, environment variables, VPC settings and permissions.
sourceWarning: CORRECTED ORIGINAL WRONG KEY C -> B. AWS RAM shareable resources list supports Aurora clusters but not Lambda functions.
